W002-HELP-001.8,diagnostics.json is the canonical WASM-002 diagnostic registry build resource,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The human-inspectable development/build source for the WASM-002 diagnostic registry is exactly diagnostics.json , encoded as UTF-8 without BOM. It is Data Sculptor product/build content, not a Suitcase artifact; it must not use the __DS__ namespace, consume an artifact-class token, or be copied into an analyst's Suitcase merely because Data Sculptor runs. The top-level JSON object has exactly two fields: registry_version and diagnostics . registry_version is the string ""1"" . diagnostics is an array written in ascending UTF-8 byte order of diagnostic_id . Each diagnostic entry has exactly seven fields: diagnostic_id , severity , phase , behavior , next_action , required_facts , and optional_facts . Diagnostic IDs must be unique and satisfy W002-HELP-001.1. Severity, phase, behavior, and next-action values must satisfy W002-HELP-001.2 through W002-HELP-001.6. required_facts and optional_facts are arrays of canonical fact-key strings sorted in ascending UTF-8 byte order; keys must be unique within each array and the two arrays must be disjoint. {
  ""registry_version"": ""1"",
  ""diagnostics"": [
    {
      ""diagnostic_id"": ""DS-CNV-001"",
      ""severity"": ""INFO"",
      ""phase"": ""SOURCE_CERTIFICATION"",
      ""behavior"": ""CONTINUE"",
      ""next_action"": ""RUN_WINDOWS_1252_CONVERSION"",
      ""required_facts"": [""source_filename"", ""windows_1252_compatibility_outcome""],
      ""optional_facts"": []
    },
    {
      ""diagnostic_id"": ""DS-ENC-001"",
      ""severity"": ""ERROR"",
      ""phase"": ""SOURCE_CERTIFICATION"",
      ""behavior"": ""REFUSE"",
      ""next_action"": ""NONE"",
      ""required_facts"": [""first_invalid_byte_offset"", ""source_filename"", ""stop_reason""],
      ""optional_facts"": [""analytical_outputs_published"", ""materialization_started"", ""source_modified_by_data_sculptor"", ""store_state_committed""]
    },
    {
      ""diagnostic_id"": ""DS-HLP-001"",
      ""severity"": ""ERROR"",
      ""phase"": ""DIAGNOSTIC_ASSEMBLY"",
      ""behavior"": ""REFUSE"",
      ""next_action"": ""NONE"",
      ""required_facts"": [""intended_diagnostic_id"", ""missing_required_facts""],
      ""optional_facts"": []
    }
  ]
} The PRD does not need to enumerate every allocated WASM-002 diagnostic row. The complete registry delivered with the build is retained acceptance evidence. A diagnostic ID becomes permanent once allocated and must not later be reused for a different meaning. Build validation must fail on malformed JSON; extra/missing entry fields; duplicate or noncanonical diagnostic IDs; invalid fixed tokens; unsorted, duplicate, overlapping, or invalid fact-key declarations; engine diagnostic definitions whose fixed semantics disagree with the registry; engine diagnostic definitions absent from the registry; Help-catalog IDs absent from the registry; or Help placeholders that name facts not declared as required or optional by the matching diagnostic. F-07 DS-ENC-001 fact mapping: the canonical lower-case diagnostic facts for strict UTF-8 refusal are first_invalid_byte_offset , source_filename , and stop_reason . For this diagnostic, stop_reason is exactly INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE . The generic fact name byte_offset is retired for this UTF-8 refusal diagnostic. P2-03 clock-order diagnostic facts: whichever stable WASM-002 Diagnostic ID is allocated to refusal because a successor Store MAP or WKO MAP cannot satisfy the strict monotonic UTC publication guard must declare these exact lower-case required facts in its diagnostic-registry entry: map_profile , observed_host_utc , predecessor_map_filename , and predecessor_utc . map_profile has exactly two permitted values: STORE for a Store-MAP chronology guard and WKO for a Work-Order-registry-MAP chronology guard. These facts identify both the governed MAP profile, the blocking predecessor artifact, and the truthful clock observation that caused refusal. F-16 DS-CNV-001 allocation: DS-CNV-001 is emitted only when the complete read-only compatibility assessment under W002-CONV-002 through W002-CONV-002.5 reaches EOF with outcome COMPATIBLE . Its required fact windows_1252_compatibility_outcome is therefore exactly the JSON string ""COMPATIBLE"" . behavior: CONTINUE means this informational diagnostic introduces no additional refusal; it does not reverse the already-established DS-ENC-001 refusal or resume Stage 2. F-17 DS-HLP-001 allocation: DS-HLP-001 is the canonical fail-safe event when the engine cannot satisfy the complete required-fact contract of an intended registered diagnostic. intended_diagnostic_id is the exact canonical ID that was being assembled. missing_required_facts is a JSON array of every missing required fact-key string, sorted in ascending UTF-8 byte order with no duplicates. The intended diagnostic is suppressed rather than emitted incompletely. DS-HLP-001 always refuses and has next_action: NONE . F-22 QA-independence boundary: diagnostics.json is authoritative for the fixed semantic contract of an allocated Diagnostic ID — its ID, severity, phase, behavior, next action, and permitted required/optional fact keys — but the implementation-delivered registry is not, by itself, an independent oracle proving that every arbitrary runtime condition was mapped to the correct Diagnostic ID. WASM-002 does not require a second QA-owned registry duplicating every implementation allocation. Where this PRD independently freezes a condition-to-diagnostic mapping or exact required facts — including the named DS-ENC-001 , DS-CNV-001 , and DS-HLP-001 contracts and other explicitly pinned diagnostic facts — that PRD text remains normative and acceptance must test the mapping independently of the implementation registry. For allocations not independently pinned by the PRD, WASM-002 accepts the validated build registry as the build allocation while retaining all registry-shape, permanence, semantic-agreement, fact-discipline, and Help cross-validation gates. This is an explicit accepted QA-scope risk, not a claim of independent condition-to-ID verification. W002-HELP-002,Three-voice parity,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The Help Engine must support the three established Data Sculptor help voices. All three renderings must preserve the same diagnostic truth. Voice selection may change wording, sentence structure, degree of technical detail, and explanatory style. F-24 session default and persistence: Technical is the canonical Help voice at the start of every new browser application instance. The analyst may select Casual or Office Speak during that instance, but WASM-002 retains the selected voice only in volatile runtime state and does not persist the preference in browser-private storage. A new application instance therefore returns to Technical. This default does not alter the F-17 rule that a missing diagnostic-specific catalog entry visibly falls back to Generic Technical Help.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-HELP-002.8,One validated Help message catalog is the source of truth for all three voices,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The Help layer resolves a canonical diagnostic ID through one validated catalog that associates an authored ID with Casual, Office Speak, and Technical templates. The human-maintained development source is exactly help_messages.json , encoded as UTF-8 without BOM. help_messages.json is a Data Sculptor product/build resource, not a Suitcase artifact. It must not use the __DS__ governed artifact namespace, consume a semantic artifact-class token, or be copied into an analyst's Suitcase merely because Data Sculptor runs. Run-specific structured facts remain authoritative in the canonical diagnostic event and are supplied separately to the selected template. The three authored voices must not be maintained as unrelated message stores. F-17 coverage fallback: absence of an authored catalog entry for an otherwise complete registered diagnostic is permitted at run time and does not make the diagnostic incomplete. Data Sculptor must instead render the deterministic Generic Technical Help view defined by W002-HELP-002.9. The fallback consumes only the canonical event semantic core and its emitted governed facts; it is not a second message catalog and does not manufacture replacement diagnostic facts.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-002.9,WASM-002 may use mechanically generated placeholder voice text to prove Help wiring,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WASM-002 acceptance does not require the complete production Help corpus. Authored catalog entries may use unmistakable placeholder strings, and placeholder entries may be generated mechanically from the validated diagnostics.json registry; no production prose authorship is required. Deterministic Generic Technical Help fallback. When a complete registered canonical diagnostic has no matching entry in help_messages.json , all selected Help voices fall back visibly to one Generic Technical rendering. The rendering must show, in this exact conceptual order, the diagnostic ID, severity, phase, behavior, next-action token, and then every emitted governed fact ordered by ascending UTF-8 byte order of fact key. It must state that no diagnostic-specific authored explanation is available. It must not infer cause beyond the diagnostic, invent remediation, default missing facts, inspect undeclared external state, or substitute prose for governed fact values. The Generic Technical fallback preserves the original diagnostic unchanged. Catalog incompleteness is therefore distinct from diagnostic incompleteness: a valid event can always be rendered generically, while inability to satisfy the event's own required_facts contract suppresses that intended event and produces DS-HLP-001 under W002-HELP-001.4 and W002-HELP-001.8. Acceptance must prove correct diagnostic-ID lookup, selected-voice resolution, structured-fact interpolation where a template exists, voice switching, deterministic Generic Technical fallback for a deliberately absent catalog entry, and semantic parity across authored voices. Final authored Help wording, examples, editorial polishing, and production-corpus quality remain deferred to a later Help-content milestone.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-002.10,help_messages.json has one deterministic WASM-002 source schema,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The top-level JSON object has exactly two fields: catalog_version and messages . catalog_version is the string ""1"" . messages is an array written in ascending UTF-8 byte order of diagnostic_id . Each message entry has exactly four fields: diagnostic_id , casual , office_speak , and technical . diagnostic_id must satisfy the canonical DS-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> grammar and must be unique in the catalog. Each voice field is a JSON string. A voice string may contain zero or more structured-fact placeholders using the exact form {fact_name} . Each catalog diagnostic_id must exist in the validated diagnostics.json registry, and each referenced placeholder must be declared in that diagnostic's required_facts or optional_facts . Duplicate IDs, missing voice fields, null voice values, malformed JSON, noncanonical or unregistered diagnostic IDs, or undeclared fact placeholders make catalog validation fail. The catalog is intentionally allowed to be non-exhaustive. A registered diagnostic with no message entry is rendered through the deterministic Generic Technical fallback in W002-HELP-002.9. Therefore a missing catalog entry for a registered diagnostic is not a build-validation failure and must not cause the engine to synthesize an authored entry or suppress the diagnostic. WASM-002 therefore does not require one global exhaustive fact-name table in the PRD. Fact-key authority is per diagnostic: the validated registry declares which fact names are legal for each stable diagnostic meaning. {
  ""catalog_version"": ""1"",
  ""messages"": [
    {
      ""diagnostic_id"": ""DS-ENC-001"",
      ""casual"": ""[CASUAL PLACEHOLDER] {source_filename}"",
      ""office_speak"": ""[OFFICE PLACEHOLDER] {source_filename}"",
      ""technical"": ""[TECHNICAL PLACEHOLDER] {source_filename} {first_invalid_byte_offset} {stop_reason}""
    }
  ]
} Later Help-content revisions may extend or version this schema only through an explicit PRD revision. F-07 placeholder mapping: Help for the strict UTF-8 refusal may render {first_invalid_byte_offset} and {stop_reason} because those exact fact names are declared by the canonical DS-ENC-001 diagnostic registry entry. The older generic {byte_offset} placeholder is not valid for DS-ENC-001. P2-03 Help rendering duty: Help for the monotonic-UTC refusal must identify the exact blocking predecessor MAP and show both predecessor UTC and truthful observed host UTC. It must distinguish an incorrect host clock from a genuinely future-dated governed MAP and may explain the approved analyst-owned choices: correct the clock, wait/rerun after truthful time advances, or deliberately move the exact future-dated current MAP out of the active Suitcase root with the warning that an older snapshot/registry may become current and that restoring the moved MAP may restore its authority.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-002.11,The validated Help catalog is embedded into the released HTML build and supplied to the shared core,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Before a WASM-002 browser build is accepted, the build must parse and validate help_messages.json , then serialize the validated catalog directly into the Data Sculptor HTML itself as one non-executable application/json payload with the exact element ID ds-help-catalog . The embedded JSON must be HTML-safe so catalog text cannot terminate the containing script element; at minimum, literal less-than characters in JSON string content must be escaped during embedding. At runtime, the browser host obtains this embedded payload and supplies the validated catalog to the shared Rust/WASM Help core. Browser JavaScript must not implement a competing template-selection, fact-interpolation, fallback, escaping, or HLP-semantic engine. The browser host must not fetch a Help catalog from the network, the filesystem, the Suitcase, or an adjacent deployment file. Missing or malformed embedded catalog JSON, or a build whose embedded catalog does not correspond to the validated build input, is a build-validation failure. The released HTML therefore remains one offline portable front door for the browser Help catalog. A later native host may supply the same governed catalog semantics to the same shared core from its own build-bundled resource; host packaging may differ, but Help semantics must not fork.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-HELP-004.11,Four canonical Boolean facts describe the WASM-002 execution boundary.,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"When the governed diagnostic context can determine the execution boundary, the canonical fact names are exactly: source_modified_by_data_sculptor materialization_started analytical_outputs_published store_state_committed When one of these facts has an established Boolean value, the JSON/structured value is the native Boolean true or false , never the strings ""TRUE"" or ""FALSE"" . source_modified_by_data_sculptor states only whether Data Sculptor modified the analyst-owned source in place; it must not imply knowledge that no external process or analyst changed the source between sessions. materialization_started records whether the governed analytical materialization phase began. analytical_outputs_published records whether governed analytical outputs were successfully published for user use; transient SCR candidates or abandoned/uncommitted debris do not make this fact true. store_state_committed records whether the successor Store MAP commit point was crossed. If a present boundary fact must express governed absence rather than an established Boolean, its JSON/structured value is the exact applicable shared absence-state string ""NONE"" , ""NOT_RUN"" , ""NOT_AVAILABLE"" , or ""NOT_APPLICABLE"" . JSON null is not a valid encoding for these four boundary facts because it would discard the reason for absence. A boundary fact that is optional for a particular diagnostic may instead be omitted under W002-HELP-001.4; that omission carries no absence-state meaning. A missing, omitted, unavailable, or not-run fact must never be interpreted as false . If one of these facts is declared required for an intended diagnostic and the required value cannot be produced, it must not be silently defaulted; the intended diagnostic is suppressed and the fail-safe DS-HLP-001 contract in W002-HELP-001.4/W002-HELP-001.8 applies.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-004.12,Governed Work Order lineage sufficient to establish user intent.,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,Included lineage must obey the disclosure boundary defined for Help reports and must not automatically expand into source-data disclosure.,NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-005,Deterministic rendering uses a closed governed input set,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Given the same canonical diagnostic event or ordered set of events, selected voice, PRETTY rules, validated Help catalog, and built-in presentation version, Help rendering must be deterministic except for explicitly permitted event/report-specific fields. W002-HELP-009,"WASM-002 establishes HLP identity, lineage, multiplicity, and one canonical embedded provenance payload.",W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A durable generated Help Report is an immutable governed HLP artifact whose physical filename is: __DS__HLP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.html The UTC token is the HLP's own governed generation/publication time. The report is the final self-contained HTML artifact using the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation; no unstyled intermediate is the canonical HLP. Report-request multiplicity: one explicit Help Report request publishes exactly one HLP. The request may be bound to one active governed diagnostic, including a diagnostic that is not associated with a Run, or to one governed Run containing one or more canonical diagnostic events. A Run-level report includes the governed diagnostic events selected by that request in deterministic event order. HLP generation is never an automatic one-artifact-per-diagnostic side effect. Every HLP must expose a visible deterministic Provenance section and exactly one embedded non-executable application/json payload whose element ID is exactly ds-hlp-provenance . F-34 supersedes the earlier draft schema version ""1"" . For schema version ""2"" , the JSON top-level object contains exactly these ten fields: {
  ""schema_version"": ""2"",
  ""hlp_filename"": ""__DS__HLP__20260922T191500123Z__<uuid-v4>.html"",
  ""hlp_generation_utc"": ""20260922T191500123Z"",
  ""diagnostic_ids"": [""DS-ENC-001"", ""DS-MAT-004""],
  ""originating_wko_filename"": ""__DS__WKO__...txt"",
  ""originating_rcp_filename"": null,
  ""selected_help_voice"": ""technical"",
  ""presentation_id"": ""red5sorcery-data-sculptor"",
  ""presentation_version"": ""1"",
  ""data_sculptor_build"": ""<exact-build-id>""
} hlp_generation_utc must use the canonical fixed-width millisecond UTC form YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ . diagnostic_ids is a non-empty JSON array containing one canonical diagnostic ID for each diagnostic event included in the report, in the same deterministic event order used by the report. Repeated IDs are permitted when distinct included events legitimately share one diagnostic type. selected_help_voice is exactly one of casual , office_speak , or technical , matching the Help catalog keys. For WASM-002 the built-in presentation identity is exactly red5sorcery-data-sculptor and its presentation version is exactly ""1"" . data_sculptor_build must contain the exact running build identifier used for the tested/released build; the literal scope label WASM-002 alone is not sufficient unless it is also the exact build identifier. originating_wko_filename and originating_rcp_filename are schema-declared nullable lineage fields . When the relationship exists and the exact physical filename is known, the value is that filename as a JSON string. When the relationship itself does not apply to this Help event/report request, the machine-readable value is JSON null . That null has one schema-defined meaning: the nullable relationship has no value, equivalent to Rust Option<T>::None and to the governed semantic state NOT_APPLICABLE . The visible Provenance section renders it as NOT APPLICABLE . If the lineage relationship does apply but the exact filename cannot be obtained, JSON null must not be used; the field value is the exact string ""NOT_AVAILABLE"" and the visible Provenance section renders NOT AVAILABLE . Empty strings, invented lineage, N/A , UNKNOWN , or another substitute are forbidden. For these two lineage fields, null and ""NOT_AVAILABLE"" are deliberately non-interchangeable. A non-run HLP may therefore legitimately carry JSON null for both lineage fields when neither relationship applies. This nullable-field rule is a schema-specific serialization choice, not a fifth absence state and not a generic JSON encoding rule. Other diagnostic JSON facts follow W002-HELP-001.4 and W002-HELP-004.11. The visible and machine-readable HLP provenance must express the same governed semantics even where their physical representations differ; a semantic mismatch is an HLP-generation failure and must not be silently tolerated. The embedded JSON must be HTML-safe so provenance text cannot terminate the containing script element; at minimum literal less-than characters in JSON string content must be escaped during embedding. The provenance payload remains subject to W002-HELP-010 and must not introduce source rows, source values, absolute local paths, arbitrary Work Order content, or other context excluded by the fixed HLP disclosure policy. WASM-002 does not automatically compute or embed a SHA-256 of the HLP, and saving an HLP must not create, refresh, or verify an LCK . The final HLP bytes remain eligible for exact-byte integrity evidence under the later explicit FINGERPRINT/LCK workflow. Configurable Brand Manifest provenance remains deferred to V1-BACKLOG / a future build. F-14 HLP publication: the complete self-contained report is first written as the corresponding SCR candidate under W002-STOR-023.1. It must close, reopen, and validate the required visible Provenance section, exact schema-version-2 embedded JSON shape, HTML-safe serialization, self-contained presentation and visible/machine semantic parity before the class token may be renamed from SCR to HLP . A partial or semantically mismatched candidate never becomes a canonical HLP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-010,Help Report disclosure uses one fixed WASM-002 allowlist.,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Generating a Help Report must not silently become a data-export path. WASM-002 therefore uses one deterministic allowlist rather than collecting broad context and attempting to redact it afterward. There are no disclosure checkboxes, permissive export modes, or per-report overrides in WASM-002. Always eligible when present and applicable: diagnostic ID; severity/classification; governed operation/phase; continue/refuse decision; safe next action; selected Help voice; HLP identity and generation UTC; relevant governed artifact filenames; and the four canonical boundary facts from W002-HELP-004.11. Eligible only when necessary to explain the diagnostic: the exact source filename but not an absolute OS path; a relevant source column header only when Data Sculptor has structurally established an actual CSV header record; the relevant 1-based column number; a relevant governed Store/RID/COL alias only when that alias itself is necessary to explain the diagnostic, such as an alias collision, ambiguity, or governed alias mutation; byte offset, row/count, or byte-length evidence; Store/RID/COL/MAP/WKO physical filenames; and only the minimum executable Work Order clause or clauses needed to establish intent and the diagnostic trigger. If that minimum Work Order excerpt necessarily contains a governed alias, that alias is disclosed and counts as alias text included. Headerless boundary: record position alone never establishes a source header. If the governed parser has not established a valid header record, including a headerless-source refusal, HLP generation must not treat any field from the first data row or any later data record as header text. Structural evidence such as 1-based column ordinal, governed diagnostic/location facts, or an applicable operational fallback name must be used instead. Never included automatically: source rows; source field values or arbitrary data samples; field data mislabeled as header text; absolute local paths; unrelated source headers, aliases, or column names; the complete Work Order; Work Order comments; unrelated Suitcase contents; browser/environment internals not governed as diagnostic evidence; or raw ungoverned stack traces. Every generated HLP must contain a visible Disclosure section stating, at minimum: Source rows included: NO ; Source values included: NO ; Source header text included: YES or NO ; Governed alias text included: YES or NO ; Absolute local paths included: NO ; Work Order comments included: NO ; and Work Order excerpt: RELEVANT EXECUTABLE CLAUSES ONLY . The two YES/NO declarations must truthfully reflect the actual HLP bytes. A genuine established source header does not count as a source field value; this distinction applies only after the governed parser has established the header record. The renderer must not weaken any declaration when the underlying policy has not changed. This durable-HLP allowlist does not prohibit transient local Help from showing a relevant governed alias or a genuinely established source header when useful to explain the same canonical diagnostic event. Local presentation does not enlarge what the portable HLP may disclose.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-011,Help owns the cross-session source-continuity edge-case explanation,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"When an unexpected analytical result, row-alignment concern, or support question raises the possibility that an analyst-owned source changed between sessions, Data Sculptor-controlled guidance must flow through the Help Engine. Help must not imply that the engine monitored or cryptographically protected the source when it did not. The explanation must distinguish ordinary analyst-controlled workflow from stronger optional evidence. It may ask whether the analyst edited, replaced, sorted, re-exported, synchronized, copied over, or otherwise changed the source after the Store was established.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-011.1,Help presents continuity evidence in explicit assurance levels,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For a suspected cross-session source change, Help must distinguish at least these evidence levels: No continuity evidence: state that cross-session byte continuity cannot be independently verified from filename/Store metadata alone. INVENTORY available: use filename, exact byte length, and last-modified metadata as lightweight clues; changed metadata may indicate that the source changed, while unchanged metadata must not be presented as proof of unchanged bytes. Explicit fingerprint evidence available: exact-byte SHA-256 evidence may establish whether the compared file bytes match or differ under the later governed FINGERPRINT workflow. Help must not collapse these levels into one generic statement of certainty.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-011.2,WASM-002 does not impose automatic cross-session hashing or Suitcase surveillance,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Ordinary WASM-002 materialization and Store inheritance must not automatically SHA-256 the source, recursively fingerprint the Suitcase, or maintain hidden whole-Suitcase surveillance merely to guard against the possibility that an analyst-owned file changed between sessions. This is an intentional product boundary for the lone-office-analyst model. The product assumes the analyst normally controls the Suitcase, provides lightweight explicit INVENTORY evidence in WASM-002, preserves a later explicit FINGERPRINT path for stronger assurance, and relies on Help to explain unusual cross-session continuity questions proportionately. WASM-002 must not create, refresh, or silently verify an LCK Suitcase Lock as a side effect of Work Order save, materialization, Store inheritance, INVENTORY, alias maintenance, or ordinary project use. LCK publication belongs to the explicit later-V1 FINGERPRINT workflow. F-13 single-writer Help boundary: Help must distinguish cross-session continuity from concurrent writing. WASM-002 does not claim that two Data Sculptor tabs/windows can safely write the same Suitcase at once. User guidance must say to use one writing Data Sculptor context per Suitcase; read-only viewing is not itself a governed write. When a pre-commit guard detects that relevant governed state changed underneath an operation, Help must identify the changed authority where available and direct the analyst to refresh or reopen current state and rerun deliberately. It must not imply that Data Sculptor acquired a cross-tab lock, merged the competing work, or automatically rebased the refused transaction.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-PRETTY-001,Separation of truth and presentation,W002-PRETTY,W002-PRETTY,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,The PRETTY Engine must not decide analytical truth or reinterpret diagnostic meaning. W002-PRETTY-004,Accessibility and inspectability,W002-PRETTY,W002-PRETTY,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"PRETTY HTML must remain ordinary inspectable HTML. W002-QA-001,Governed test-only seams and acceptance coverage,W002-QA,W002-QA,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every material frozen WASM-002 behavior must have retained acceptance evidence sufficient to exercise the governed success, refusal, mutation, publication, or recovery boundary that makes the behavior meaningful. Related cases may share one fixture when the shared fixture proves each required condition explicitly; acceptance coverage must not rely on a behavior being difficult to reproduce under an uncontrolled host environment. Permitted deterministic test-only seams. WASM-002 acceptance may use controlled clock values; controlled UUID sequences and collision outcomes; controlled filesystem create/write/close/rename/promotion failures; and controlled run-local source-handle reread/substitution conditions. A seam supplies only the external condition required to reach the governed behavior. It must not bypass validation, alter the normative semantic result, change governed serialization, relax publication rules, rewrite diagnostic truth, or create a second analytical execution model. Release boundary. Test-only controls must not be invocable through the ordinary Data Sculptor UI, DS-STEPS, saved Work Orders, URL/query parameters, Suitcase configuration, or another analyst-facing product path. Compile-time exclusion, test-build configuration, or an isolated acceptance harness are permitted implementation techniques. Retained acceptance evidence must identify any seam used and must separately demonstrate that the accepted release surface cannot invoke that seam as a user feature. Named storage acceptance gaps. Acceptance must include a case-variant governed namespace/class fixture proving that Data Sculptor does not silently normalize the variant spelling into canonical governed identity; an unknown syntactically valid governed-class fixture proving that the file remains byte-for-byte unchanged while a canonical INFO diagnostic and INVENTORY surface the unknown/unrecognized class; and at least one known-but-not-emitted-class fixture drawn from DGN , RCV , BRD , or LCK proving the same preserve-and-report behavior without activating a producer, lifecycle, or interpretation path. Carried feature gates remain feature-owned. Mechanisms whose normative lifecycle is integrated in another package — including the F-02 Work Order-registry/alias-replacement behavior, the F-04 existing-Store cardinality refusal, and the F-24 CER-history decision — cannot be considered accepted without their corresponding feature acceptance gates. This requirement does not invent those feature semantics. If a proposed mechanism is removed from WASM-002 rather than integrated, no acceptance gate for that removed mechanism is required.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-ENC-ACC-001,UTF-8 certification pass,W002-ENC-ACC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,A valid multi-gigabyte UTF-8 fixture must complete whole-source certification with exact byte accounting under bounded memory.,NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-ENC-ACC-002,UTF-8 certification fail,W002-ENC-ACC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A fixture containing an invalid UTF-8 sequence, including a sequence that crosses an input-window boundary, must deterministically produce STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: FAIL , UTF8_STOP_REASON: INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE , and the exact governed zero-based UTF8_FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET . Stage 2 must not begin and no analytical materialization output may be published. The same bytes tested under different permitted Stage-1 input-window sizes and boundary placements must yield the same outcome, stop-reason token, and first-invalid offset.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-ENC-ACC-003,Run-local source substitution refusal,W002-ENC-ACC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An acceptance fixture must attempt to present Stage 2 with a different source instance/reference than the one retained from Stage 1. The run must refuse before materialization rather than accept the substitute merely because filename, alias, path, or byte length appears compatible. F-23 governed seam: this fixture must use the test-only source-handle substitution/reread seam permitted by W002-QA-001 so the different Stage-2 instance is injected without changing the analyst-visible SOURCE syntax or adding a product-level source-selection path. Release-surface evidence must demonstrate that an analyst cannot invoke this substitution seam through the normal UI, Work Order, URL/query, or Suitcase configuration.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-ENC-ACC-004,ASCII-only fast path,W002-ENC-ACC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,An all-ASCII fixture must certify successfully without invoking non-ASCII sequence validation and must produce exact byte accounting.,NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-ENC-ACC-005,Valid non-ASCII sequence matrix,W002-ENC-ACC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must cover valid two-byte, three-byte, and four-byte UTF-8 sequences, including sequences placed at window boundaries and split at every legal boundary position.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-ENC-ACC-006,Strict invalid-sequence matrix,W002-ENC-ACC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must reject at known exact offsets: lone continuation bytes, malformed continuation sequences, truncated sequences, overlong encodings, UTF-16 surrogate encodings, invalid lead bytes 0xC0 / 0xC1 , values introduced by 0xF5 - 0xFF , and code points above U+10FFFF. Every invalid fixture must serialize the same canonical UTF-8 stop reason INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE while preserving its fixture-specific exact first-invalid byte offset. Separate valid fixtures covering ASCII-only, valid multibyte UTF-8, and permitted leading-BOM forms must complete with STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: PASS ; their UTF-8 refusal-only Receipt fields are NOT_APPLICABLE .",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-ENC-ACC-008,Window-size invariance,W002-ENC-ACC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,The same fixture matrix must return the same PASS/FAIL and first invalid absolute offset across at least two materially different bounded window sizes.,NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-ENC-ACC-009,EOF pending-state refusal,W002-ENC-ACC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,EOF with an incomplete UTF-8 sequence must fail deterministically and report the governed offset; no replacement character may be inserted.,NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-ENC-ACC-010,BOM behavior,W002-ENC-ACC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A UTF-8 BOM at offset zero must be accepted as metadata while the remainder of the source is still fully certified; a BOM must not mask later invalid UTF-8. The BOM is excluded from analytical CSV content but included in the absolute physical source-byte coordinate system.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-ACC-001,Multi-column one-pass Stage 2 materialization,W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Using a valid UTF-8 source and a Work Order requesting at least four source columns through a mixture of HEADER and COLUMN selectors, acceptance must prove that Stage 1 completes first, Stage 2 restarts at byte zero of the same run-local source instance, parses the header once, resolves all selectors before the first data row, and reads the source data records only once while producing all requested columns. Evidence must reconcile total source bytes read by Stage 2, logical data-row count N, per- COL data-record count N, selector-to-source ordinal/header resolution, resolved KEEP order, and the resulting successor MAP. A one-column rerun of the same source/column must produce the same canonical physical column bytes as that column produced inside the multi-column run, apart from governed artifact identity. F-20 width/one-pass acceptance: acceptance must include a maximum-width fixture whose valid source has exactly 16,384 columns and whose KEEP resolves all 16,384 distinct columns. W002-MAT-ACC-002,"Automatic Store MAP creation, inheritance, and rematerialization continuity",W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An acceptance fixture must materialize four previously unseen source columns in one Store-establishing Work Order and prove that one successor Store MAP is created with four mapping rows. W002-MAT-ACC-003,Stage 2 structural window-invariance matrix,W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance fixtures must force input boundaries at structurally difficult positions including before/after delimiters, before/after opening and closing quotes, between doubled quote bytes, between CR and LF, inside quoted multiline field content, at empty fields, and inside already-certified multi-byte UTF-8 sequences. Across permitted window sizes and boundary placements, the logical row count, selected values, canonical COL bytes, first refusal location/condition, and resolved mapping semantics must remain invariant. P3-09 fixtures: acceptance must include both byte forms identified by the Pass 3 finding: (1) an exactly zero-byte source and (2) a source containing only the three UTF-8 BOM bytes EF BB BF . Both must pass the applicable Stage 1 UTF-8 gate and then refuse in Stage 2 with NO_HEADER_RECORD . The exact expected location tuples are respectively (offset 0, physical line 1, logical record 1, field ordinal 1) and (offset 3, physical line 1, logical record 1, field ordinal 1) . The fixtures must also distinguish this case from an existing-but-blank first logical record, which remains BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD . P3-10 delimiter-help fixture: acceptance must include a quoted semicolon-delimited form such as ""a"";""b"" and an equivalent TAB-delimited quoted form that reach INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE . The canonical refusal condition and location facts must remain unchanged, while the Help rendering is permitted to surface the delimiter-mismatch hint for offending byte 0x3B or 0x09 . F-06 structural-refusal acceptance matrix An unexpected quote in an unquoted field must report the quote byte and UNEXPECTED_QUOTE_IN_UNQUOTED_FIELD . A prohibited byte after a closing quote must report that byte and INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE . A bare CR outside quoted content must report the CR byte and BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD . CR, LF, and CRLF inside valid quoted values must remain field content and must not trigger the bare-CR rule. EOF in an open quoted field must report the one-past-end source offset and EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD . A blank logical record must report BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD , not TOO_FEW_FIELDS . A short record must report the terminator/EOF location and the first missing field ordinal. A wide record must report the comma delimiter opening the first extra field and that extra field ordinal. All five refusal facts must remain identical across permitted source-window sizes and boundary placements. Fixtures must force boundaries around commas, opening and closing quotes, doubled-quote pairs, CR/LF pairs, quoted multiline content, empty fields, and already-certified multibyte UTF-8 sequences. A semicolon-separated file must not refuse solely because it uses semicolons; Help may explain comma-only interpretation when header selection fails. Day 060 H-13 Receipt-corpus binding for P3-09 The two analytical P3-09 source fixtures above must each have a corresponding byte-exact refusal Receipt under W002-RCP-ACC-002. The zero-byte and BOM-only cases therefore prove both the parser/refusal oracle and the Receipt serialization oracle independently.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-MAT-ACC-005,"Field-limit, ragged-record, blank-record, and failure-publication acceptance",W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must include decoded field sizes exactly 16 MiB and 16 MiB + 1 byte, malformed runaway quoted-field cases, nonblank records with too few and too many fields, a bare blank logical data record, explicit empty fields, and a physical blank line inside a valid quoted multiline field. The first invalid case must refuse without truncation or silent repair. Publication evidence must additionally exercise both a new-Store multi-column materialization and a later existing-Store materialization. For the new Store, the shared publication-transaction UTC must be established before any new RID/COL SCR candidate is opened, and each candidate-specific UUID must be allocated before its candidate is created. RID and COL outputs must remain governed SCR until the complete candidate set validates; the RID must then promote first, requested COLs must promote in deterministic KEEP order, the successor MAP UUID must be allocated before its MAP SCR candidate is opened, that MAP candidate must be written/closed/reopened/validated while still SCR , and its final SCR -to- MAP rename must occur last. For every successfully promoted RID, COL, and MAP artifact, acceptance must prove that the candidate and final identity have the exact same UTC, UUID, extension, and bytes and differ in the governed filename only by the three-letter semantic class token. For the existing Store, the inherited RID must remain byte-for-byte and filename-identical with no new RID candidate. F-04 existing-Store cardinality acceptance: acceptance must include two otherwise valid existing-Store materializations using the same exact governed SOURCE identity. In the equal-cardinality fixture, Stage 2 candidate N must equal the inherited RID-header N and publication may proceed under the ordinary rules. In the mismatch fixture, candidate N must differ from RID-header N ; the Run must refuse before any candidate COL is promoted into the final COL namespace and before any successor MAP is published. The inherited RID, current MAP, existing COL artifacts, and Store health must remain unchanged, with the existing Store remaining VALID. The equal-cardinality case must not be represented as proof of source-byte or row-semantic identity. Forced failure cases must cover: failure before any promotion; RID-promotion failure; failure during COL promotion after RID and at least one COL have promoted; MAP-candidate write/close/reopen/validation failure; MAP final-rename failure; and interruption after physical RID/COL promotion but before MAP commit. Each case must prove rollback where safely possible or visible non-authoritative SCR failure evidence otherwise, must prove that unreferenced final-class-looking RID/COL files are not treated as committed Store membership, and must prove that the prior valid MAP remains authoritative for an existing Store or that no committed Store exists for an uncommitted first materialization. F-20 bounded-width/name acceptance: acceptance must cover exactly 16,384 versus 16,385 source columns; KEEP widths of 1 and 16,384 ; operational-name derivation at 1,024 versus 1,025 Unicode scalar values; physical ordinals producing Column A , Column Z , Column AA , and Column XFD ; and deterministic oversized-header fallback collisions proving [ordinal] then -2 progression. A separate short-header alias collision must prove refusal rather than automatic suffixing.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-CONV-ACC-001,Separate Windows-1252 conversion,W002-CONV-ACC,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A non-UTF-8 fixture compatible with the supported Windows-1252 converter must cause the analytical task to stop, permit a Help suggestion, and succeed only when the separate conversion Work Order is explicitly run. P3-08 acceptance: the fixture set must convert an analyst-owned legacy source successfully, materialize the resulting CVT, then perform a second successful conversion from a refreshed legacy source using the same analyst-owned filename. The second conversion must publish a different CVT physical filename. First materialization of that second CVT must establish a distinct Store/RID lineage rather than inherit from the first CVT-backed Store. Acceptance must also prove that Help discloses this consequence at conversion success and again when the CVT is first materialized, and that no hidden original-source identity is used to join the two CVTs into one lineage. F-16 acceptance: the compatible non-UTF-8 fixture must prove that strict UTF-8 certification first emits DS-ENC-001 with next_action: NONE ; Stage 2 does not start; Data Sculptor restarts at byte 0 of the same bound source instance and scans the complete source under the frozen mapping; the Receipt records WINDOWS_1252_COMPATIBILITY_OUTCOME: COMPATIBLE and WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET: NOT_APPLICABLE ; and only then is DS-CNV-001 emitted with severity: INFO , behavior: CONTINUE , and next_action: RUN_WINDOWS_1252_CONVERSION . The refused MATERIALIZE run must remain refused. A separate valid-UTF-8 fixture must prove that both Windows-1252 compatibility Receipt fields are NOT_RUN and DS-CNV-001 is not emitted. F-10 conversion-gate and byte-output acceptance A source already valid as complete strict UTF-8 must refuse CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 as unnecessary and create no CVT . A source that fails strict UTF-8 but passes the complete Windows-1252 compatibility assessment may convert only when the separate conversion WKO is explicitly run. The analyst-owned source bytes must remain unchanged. The published CVT must pass complete strict UTF-8 certification. Source CR, LF, and CRLF bytes must be preserved in place rather than normalized. The conversion must remain bounded/streaming. The published CVT must not begin with a UTF-8 BOM introduced by Data Sculptor. The successful Receipt must contain the frozen conversion operation token and required conversion facts. Frozen minimal byte oracle: Windows-1252 source bytes:
63 61 66 E9 0D 0A

UTF-8 CVT bytes:
63 61 66 C3 A9 0D 0A This is café followed by CRLF. The expected CVT begins with byte 63 ; no EF BB BF prefix is present. Day 060 H-25 / BM-04 acceptance: the already-valid-UTF-8 CONVERT fixture must use a complete source whose byte stream is valid strict UTF-8 and must produce a byte-exact refused Receipt containing: SOURCE_ENCODING: UTF-8
UNDEFINED_WINDOWS_1252_BYTE_OFFSET: NOT_RUN
MATERIALIZED_ENCODING: NOT_RUN
TRANSCODING: NOT_RUN
SOURCE_CHANGED: NO
OUTPUT_FILENAME: NONE The same fixture must prove that no Windows-1252 compatibility assessment runs, no transcoding begins, the analyst-owned source bytes remain unchanged, and no CVT file is created.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-CONV-ACC-002,Undefined Windows-1252 byte refusal,W002-CONV-ACC,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A fixture containing a byte undefined by the frozen Windows-1252 mapping must not be silently converted. A separate injected read-failure fixture after the compatibility pass begins must prove NOT_AVAILABLE for both compatibility Receipt fields and no conversion recommendation. MATERIALIZED_ENCODING: NOT_RUN
TRANSCODING: NOT_RUN
SOURCE_CHANGED: NO
OUTPUT_FILENAME: NONE
RESULT: REFUSED The analyst-owned source bytes must remain exactly 41 81 42 ; no CVT is published; no replacement character is introduced; and no ISO-8859-1 or permissive-decoder fallback is permitted. W002-HP-ACC-013,Diagnostic-registry and Help cross-validation acceptance,W002-HP-ACC,W002-HP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WASM-002 acceptance must retain the validated diagnostics.json used by the accepted build and verify its exact version-1 schema, canonical sort order, unique permanent IDs, fixed-token grammars, and disjoint required/optional fact declarations. W002-WKO-007,Work Order syntax is the analytical contract,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"If a value, reference, option, or instruction changes what Data Sculptor analytically does, that intent must be represented in governed Work Order text or in a separately governed artifact explicitly referenced by that Work Order. Browser permission, directory selection, UI focus, a highlighted file, an alias display, or another GUI gesture must not silently become analytical intent. For WASM-002, every executable saved WKO begins with the common preamble: SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS ""<non-whitespace alias>"" Ignoring blank lines and governed comments, the WKO must then parse completely under exactly one of these seven executable operation grammars: Operation Governed DS-STEPS structure after the common preamble MATERIALIZE SOURCE ""..."" ; optional MAP ""..."" ; KEEP ; one or more selectors; terminal MATERIALIZE . INVENTORY terminal INVENTORY only. UPDATE ALIASES exactly one Store-state selector: SOURCE ""..."" or MAP ""..."" ; one or more governed alias mutations; terminal UPDATE ALIASES . REPAIR MAP exactly one MAP ""<exact current Store MAP filename>"" ; terminal REPAIR MAP . REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY terminal REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY only. CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 exactly one SOURCE ""..."" ; terminal CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 . CATALOG STORES terminal CATALOG STORES only. Each operation-specific numbered requirement remains authoritative for its detailed selectors, preconditions, mutations, publication semantics, and acceptance behavior. This requirement freezes the cross-operation boundary: unknown semantic lines refuse; clauses from another operation grammar refuse unless the selected operation explicitly defines them; there is no best-effort interpretation and no silent cross-operation mixing. Lexical token separation. DS-STEPS keywords are matched ASCII case-insensitively; canonical examples render them uppercase. Wherever two adjacent lexical tokens would otherwise run together, they must be separated by one or more ASCII SPACE ( 0x20 ) or horizontal TAB ( 0x09 ) characters. Leading SPACE/TAB indentation is semantically neutral. Thus REPAIR MAP , SOURCE ""crime.csv"" , and COLUMN 7 are valid tokenizations, while REPAIRMAP , SOURCE""crime.csv"" , and UPDATE_ALIASES are not alternate DS-STEPS spellings. Quoted-string contents are never case-folded or whitespace-normalized merely because keywords are case-insensitive. The browser may authorize resources, edit text, validate, save, invoke Run, display evidence, and provide Help. Authorization to access a resource is not authorization to use that resource analytically.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-008,Every executable Work Order explicitly declares its Suitcase,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For WASM-002, every executable saved Work Order must contain the exact portable declaration SUITCASE: . . The dot means the filesystem directory that physically contains the saved WKO artifact being executed. A Work Order lacking this declaration must not be treated as an executable WASM-002 Work Order. The declaration is analytical/execution syntax, not a substitute for browser filesystem permission. The host must still possess valid access to the directory before execution can proceed. Help obligation: Data Sculptor Help must explain SUITCASE: . in plain language: the saved Work Order uses the folder that contains that WKO as its Suitcase; the dot means “this folder”; ordinary Work Order file references are therefore portable and Suitcase-relative; and browser/host permission to the folder is granted separately. Help must not teach an absolute machine path as the normal replacement for . .",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-009,Ordinary Work Order file references are Suitcase-relative,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Unless another numbered requirement explicitly governs a different reference mechanism, file references in an executable WASM-002 Work Order resolve relative to the declared Suitcase. A portable Work Order must not depend on an absolute machine-specific path to identify ordinary Suitcase files. Resolution must be deterministic in browser and later native hosts. Moving an intact Suitcase to another permitted filesystem location must not change the logical meaning of the Work Order solely because the parent machine path changed.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-009.1,WASM-002 SOURCE eligibility is exact and root-bounded,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A WASM-002 SOURCE clause names exactly one physical regular file in the Suitcase root by exact filename only. It must not name an absolute path, drive or UNC path, subdirectory, path containing / or \ , traversal such as .. , URL/URI, or another external reference. Resolution uses the exact Unicode-scalar filename identity and reference-bounded rules frozen by F-15; no case-folding, normalization, trimming, or filesystem-equivalence search is permitted. The only eligible WASM-002 SOURCE kinds are: Analyst-owned CSV: a regular Suitcase-root file whose exact filename does not begin with the reserved exact prefix __DS__ and whose final extension is .csv under ASCII case-insensitive extension recognition. Thus .csv , .CSV , and mixed-case equivalents are candidate CSV extensions. This case-insensitivity applies only to extension recognition; the complete filename reference remains exact. If the physical file is crime.CSV , a differently cased full filename does not become an alternate reference to it. Governed converted source: a successfully published CVT whose exact canonical identity and class-specific publication/validity predicate satisfy W002-CONV-004, W002-STOR-023, and PB-STOR-008. A filename that merely resembles a CVT is not sufficient. No other governed semantic class is eligible as SOURCE in WASM-002, even when its physical serialization is CSV. In particular, COL , RID , MAP , CAT , INV , RCP , HLP , CER , SCR , RCV , and WKO artifacts cannot be reintroduced as SOURCE merely because their bytes or extension appear compatible. A recognized .csv extension establishes only candidate SOURCE form. It does not certify encoding or CSV structure; the normal strict UTF-8 and structural certification contracts still govern after source resolution. Conversely, CSV-like bytes stored under a non-CSV analyst-owned extension are not an eligible WASM-002 SOURCE.",PARTIAL,PORTION_VERIFIED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,CP-008; CP-009; CP-010,"T-ACCEPTED, BANKED; W002-WKO-010,WIP and WKO are distinct Work Order lifecycle states,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WIP is the editable, non-executable Work Order state. WKO is the saved, validated, immutable Work Order artifact that may become a Run target. Validation establishes that a Work Order is structurally eligible to run; it does not guarantee that runtime conditions will succeed. Loading a WKO for inspection does not make it mutable. If its instruction text is changed, the editor must treat the edited text as a new WIP derived from the original WKO. The original WKO bytes and physical identity remain unchanged, and the derived WIP cannot Run until saved as a new WKO. F-08 Run distinction: the browser Run action invokes one selected saved immutable WKO that is eligible under the governed WKO-registry rules. No ordinary WASM-002 WKO contains a textual RUN line merely to execute itself. The DS-STEPS token RUN is reserved for future saved-Work-Order composition under W002-WKO-011 and is not repurposed as the browser execution trigger.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-013,WASM-002 executes one saved Work Order without Work Order chaining,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For WASM-002, one saved immutable WKO is one top-level executable request. It must not invoke, include, chain, or execute another WKO. The governed RUN composition operation and equivalent nested-orchestration constructs are not executable in WASM-002. If a saved WKO contains composition syntax, validation must refuse before analytical execution begins. The canonical diagnostic and Help path must explain that Work Order composition is deferred rather than treating the syntax as arbitrary text, silently ignoring it, or partially executing surrounding instructions. This scope cut does not prohibit one Work Order from selecting and materializing multiple columns in the single Stage 2 operation defined by WASM-002.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012,Materialization COL alias assignment uses AS; standalone alias maintenance uses UPDATE ALIASES,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within the WASM-002 DS-STEPS materialization form, an analyst assigns or changes the alias of a selected materialized COL with the optional same-line clause AS ""alias"" under W002-STEPS-005. This syntax is part of the governed Work Order and is not a GUI gesture. A single KEEP block may therefore assign aliases to multiple selected columns in one governed materialization. Automatic source-header COL aliases and inherited rematerialization aliases are resolved first; explicit AS clauses then determine requested successor COL aliases before complete Store-MAP validation and publication. Revision BD freezes alias-only creation/replacement with UPDATE ALIASES and explicit historical Store-MAP selection with MAP ""<exact Store MAP filename>"" . Revision BE completes the bounded alias lifecycle with explicit CLEAR ... ALIAS and RESET ... ALIAS forms under W002-WKO-012.5 through W002-WKO-012.6. Empty-string AS """" is not the clearing syntax.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.1,Canonical standalone alias-maintenance Work Order uses UPDATE ALIASES,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The canonical alias-only Store metadata forms are: SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS ""Rename crime store""
SOURCE ""35100178.csv""
STORE AS ""Crime Statistics""
UPDATE ALIASES or, when the analyst intentionally selects one exact Store snapshot: SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS ""Rename crime store""
MAP ""__DS__MAP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv""
STORE AS ""Crime Statistics""
UPDATE ALIASES UPDATE ALIASES is the explicit terminal commitment clause for an alias-only Work Order. The WKO must identify exactly one Store-state base using either SOURCE ""..."" for ordinary Store-aware current-state selection or MAP ""..."" for exact Store-MAP selection, never both. At least one supported alias mutation clause must occur after the Store-state selector and before UPDATE ALIASES . An alias-only Work Order must not contain KEEP , MATERIALIZE , INVENTORY , conversion, Store repair, Work Order registry repair, cataloging, deferred Work Order composition, or another operation's terminal clause. Alias maintenance changes governed human-facing metadata only.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.2,"STORE AS, RID AS, and COL ... AS are the canonical alias-replacement clauses",W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, the canonical mutation clauses are: STORE AS ""Crime Statistics""
RID AS ""Row Number""
COL ""Crime Rate"" AS ""Police-Reported Crime Rate"" STORE AS ""..."" replaces the selected Store snapshot's store_alias . RID AS ""..."" replaces its rid_alias . COL ""<reference>"" AS ""..."" replaces the alias of exactly one existing mapped COL. The COL reference resolves under W002-STOR-021: it may be the exact physical column_filename or one unique current COL alias from the selected Store MAP. Missing, ambiguous, non-COL, or conflicting resolution must refuse rather than guess. One Work Order may update the Store alias, RID alias, and multiple distinct COL aliases together, provided the complete successor state satisfies all existing alias uniqueness/shadowing rules.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.3,"MAP ""<filename>"" is the exact historical Store-MAP selector",W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The canonical explicit Store-MAP selection clause is: MAP ""__DS__MAP__20260920T184512347Z__<uuid-v4>.csv"" The value is always the exact physical filename of one structurally valid immutable Store MAP. It is not a Store alias, WKO alias, timestamp shorthand, UUID-only selector, or latest expression. For MATERIALIZE, if present, the clause occurs immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP . It overrides automatic Store-MAP inheritance and binds the run to exactly the named Store snapshot. For alias-only maintenance, the Work Order uses either SOURCE ""..."" or MAP ""..."" as its Store-state selector, not both. For materialization, SOURCE ""..."" remains mandatory and an optional MAP ""..."" supplies the exact historical/current Store-state base. Validation must refuse an incompatible source/MAP pairing or a MAP that is not a valid Store-MAP profile. Health rule: explicit historical selection does not override the current Store-lineage health gate. The selected lineage must currently be VALID and every RID/COL binding referenced by the named MAP must currently be present and valid. Otherwise the operation refuses. This applies equally to MATERIALIZE and UPDATE ALIASES. F-05/P2-01 source-compatibility predicate: for materialization, an explicitly named MAP is compatible only when the mandatory Work Order SOURCE exactly equals the one common source_filename carried by that Store MAP. If the exact filenames differ, validation refuses before the F-04 existing-Store cardinality gate in W002-MAT-002.6. Equal row count never authorizes a different source to enter the selected Store lineage.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.4,Alias-only execution publishes one complete successor Store MAP and no rewritten data artifacts,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A successful UPDATE ALIASES operation begins from the selected complete Store MAP, applies only the requested alias replacements in memory, validates the complete resulting Store state, writes the successor MAP under governed SCR , closes and reopens it, validates it fully, and promotes it to a new immutable MAP last. That successful promotion is the alias-update commit point. The operation must preserve the selected Store's physical RID and COL filenames and bytes, source-column keys, row order, cardinality, and lineage except for the human-facing alias fields explicitly changed by the Work Order. It must not reread source data rows merely to change aliases, must not create RID/COL artifacts, and must not rewrite or delete the inherited MAP. The prior MAP remains visible historical state. If validation or MAP publication fails, no successor alias state becomes current. The failure is reported through the governed diagnostic/Help path and any incomplete candidate remains subject to the retained- SCR failure-evidence rules in W002-STOR-023.1; WASM-002 does not emit RCV. Revision BM E-02 integration: when the alias-only operation uses an explicitly named historical Store MAP, publication is permitted only if the Store lineage currently evaluates VALID and every RID/COL binding referenced by that named MAP is currently present and valid. An older MAP cannot be used to bypass current damage. P3-06 validation depth: because UPDATE ALIASES does not consume RID/COL analytical contents, its Store-health and binding checks use Tier 1 under W002-STOR-019.10. The operation must not scan every RID/COL record merely to change aliases. This does not weaken later operations that actually consume those artifacts; they must perform the applicable Tier 2 validation before relying on the contents.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-007,Standalone Store/RID/COL alias maintenance acceptance,W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must establish a Store with one RID and at least three materialized COLs, then execute an alias-only Work Order that changes the Store alias, RID alias, and at least two COL aliases in one UPDATE ALIASES operation. One COL must be targeted by its unique current alias and another by its exact physical COL filename. The fixture must prove that exactly one complete successor Store MAP becomes current; prior MAP, RID, and COL artifacts remain byte-for-byte unchanged; no source-data row read is required; no new RID/COL artifact is published; and the successor MAP contains exactly the requested aliases while preserving all physical bindings and logical source-column keys. Missing/ambiguous COL references and successor alias collisions must refuse without publishing a successor MAP. F-23 CLEAR/RESET alias fixtures: acceptance must separately exercise CLEAR STORE ALIAS , CLEAR RID ALIAS , CLEAR COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS , RESET STORE ALIAS , RESET RID ALIAS , and RESET COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS . Each CLEAR fixture must prove that the successor MAP stores the governed empty alias without renaming or rewriting the referenced artifact. Each RESET fixture must prove restoration of the exact deterministic default governed by W002-WKO-012.6 and W002-STOR-019.7, including the oversized-header operational fallback where applicable. The fixtures must prove that CLEAR and RESET require no source-data row read, publish exactly one complete successor Store MAP on success, leave the predecessor MAP/RID/COL bytes unchanged, and deterministically refuse duplicate mutation of the same alias field or a reset/default value that fails the complete successor alias validity/uniqueness/shadowing rules.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-008,Explicit historical Store-MAP selection acceptance,W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must create at least two valid Store MAP snapshots for one Store, then prove that a Work Order containing MAP ""<older exact Store MAP filename>"" binds to that exact older snapshot even though a newer valid MAP exists. An alias-only fixture must publish its successor from the explicitly named older base rather than from the newer automatic current state. A materialization fixture must retain mandatory SOURCE ""..."" while using the explicit MAP as its Store-state base. The tests must also prove refusal for a missing MAP, malformed MAP, WKO-MAP profile supplied as Store MAP, and source/MAP incompatibility. No implementation may substitute the newest MAP after an explicit MAP clause has validated. F-21 chronology acceptance: the fixture must use at least three successive valid MAP snapshots for one Store so that an explicitly selected older base and a distinct pre-run current MAP both exist. Merely selecting/validating the older MAP must leave current authority unchanged. A successful governed operation from that older base must then publish exactly one new successor whose requested state is derived from the named older base, whose publication UTC is later than the pre-run current chronology predecessor, and which becomes current under ordinary greatest-UTC selection. The selected historical MAP and the formerly current MAP must remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Acceptance must prove that later mappings/aliases present only in the formerly current MAP are not silently merged into the historical-base successor unless the Work Order explicitly recreates them. Receipt evidence must identify the exact operation base and exact published successor through the already-frozen operation-specific Receipt fields. W002-WKO-012.5,CLEAR ... ALIAS deliberately removes a human-facing alias,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, the canonical clearing forms are: CLEAR STORE ALIAS
CLEAR RID ALIAS
CLEAR COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS CLEAR deliberately stores the empty string in the corresponding alias field of the successor Store MAP. It does not restore a default alias. An empty-string replacement such as STORE AS """" , RID AS """" , or COL ""..."" AS """" is not the canonical clearing form and must be rejected by the bounded WASM-002 grammar. For CLEAR COL , <reference> resolves against the selected pre-mutation Store MAP by exact physical column_filename or one unique current COL alias under W002-STOR-021. All COL references in one UPDATE ALIASES Work Order are resolved before any mutation is applied so clause order cannot change target identity.
