W002-WKO-012.6,RESET ... ALIAS restores the deterministic default alias,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, the canonical reset forms are: RESET STORE ALIAS
RESET RID ALIAS
RESET COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS RESET STORE ALIAS restores the Store MAP's common exact source_filename . RESET RID ALIAS restores the literal RID . RESET COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS restores that mapped COL's deterministic operational default defined by W002-STOR-019.7 from its exact recorded source_header and physical source ordinal: the exact header when it contains at most 1,024 Unicode scalar values, or the deterministic Column <LETTERS> fallback/disambiguation rule when the recorded header exceeds that boundary. RESET never substitutes the potentially oversized exact header into the alias field merely because that header remains authoritative source evidence. RESET is therefore distinct from CLEAR . The restored value must pass the same governed alias validity, uniqueness, and shadowing rules as any explicit alias. If the deterministic default is empty or conflicts in the complete successor Store MAP, RESET must refuse except for the narrow oversized-header fallback/disambiguation rule already frozen in W002-STOR-019.7; Data Sculptor must not otherwise invent a suffix, alternate spelling, or substitute. AS , CLEAR , and RESET mutations may coexist in one Work Order when they target distinct alias fields; duplicate mutation of the same alias field in one Work Order must refuse. A successful operation publishes exactly one complete successor Store MAP under the existing UPDATE ALIASES commit contract.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-001,Canonical WASM-002 DS-STEPS materialization form,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The canonical WASM-002 materialization Work Order form is: # Optional human comment
SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS ""Prepare monthly crime data""
SOURCE ""crime.csv""
[MAP ""__DS__MAP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv""]

KEEP
  HEADER ""REF_DATE"" AS ""Year""      # reporting year
  HEADER ""GEO""
  COLUMN 7 AS ""Crime Rate""

MATERIALIZE SUITCASE: . is governed by W002-WKO-008. WORK ORDER AS ""..."" is mandatory for an executable/saved WASM-002 Work Order and declares the immutable human-facing WKO alias governed by W002-STEPS-001.1. SOURCE ""..."" names the exact Suitcase-root source file. MAP ""..."" is optional with cardinality 0..1. If present, it occurs immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP , names one exact physical governed Store MAP filename, and binds the run to that exact current or historical Store lineage subject to W002-STOR-019.3 and W002-WKO-012.3. If absent, the Store-aware exact-source routing rules apply. KEEP is the bare governed keyword and introduces one or more column selectors. KEEP: is not valid WASM-002 syntax. Each selector is either HEADER ""..."" or COLUMN n and may optionally end with AS ""..."" . MATERIALIZE is the explicit terminal commitment verb. Duplicate structural clauses refuse. An empty KEEP refuses. After MATERIALIZE , only blank lines or comments may follow; a trailing comment on the physical MATERIALIZE line is permitted because comments are removed from the semantic token stream. # comments are governed by W002-STEPS-001.2. No RID/row-index clause appears in the Work Order. If this materialization establishes a new Store, the engine automatically generates exactly one RID artifact under W002-RID-002 and W002-RID-008. If it extends an existing Store, the existing RID is reused subject to the Store health/cardinality rules. This requirement freezes the bounded keyword structure and selector forms shown above for BM integration. Other complete-language lexical features remain outside this bounded syntax freeze unless separately specified. F-08 common-grammar boundary: MATERIALIZE is one of the seven executable WASM-002 operation grammars governed by W002-WKO-007. Its optional MAP clause remains in the frozen position immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP . The terminal MATERIALIZE clause is DS-STEPS syntax; the browser's Run action is not written into the Work Order. F-20 bounded KEEP: the canonical KEEP block contains at least one and at most 16,384 selectors, and after resolution those selectors must identify at least one and at most 16,384 distinct source columns. This is the complete WASM-002 selection-width bound.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-001.1,WORK ORDER AS declares the immutable human-facing Work Order alias,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An executable or saved WASM-002 Work Order must contain exactly one top-level clause: WORK ORDER AS ""<alias>"" In canonical forms it appears after SUITCASE: . and before the operation-specific source/selector clauses. The decoded alias must be non-empty. The quoted alias may contain spaces and ordinary UTF-8 phrase text subject to the governed string-literal rules. The alias affects display and governed alias resolution only; it does not replace the WKO filename/UUID as physical execution identity. The alias is stored in the immutable WKO bytes and is published into the current WKO MAP when the WKO save transaction commits. Changing the alias therefore requires saving a new WKO under the frozen WKO lifecycle. No valid executable/saved WKO in WASM-002 is unaliased. P3-10 alias-content rule: “non-empty” means that, after decoding the quoted string literal, the alias must contain at least one non-whitespace character. An alias consisting only of whitespace refuses Work Order validation. Data Sculptor must not trim, collapse, normalize, or otherwise rewrite leading or trailing whitespace in an otherwise valid alias; the decoded alias text remains authoritative and is preserved exactly in the immutable WKO and governed WKO MAP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-001.2,# introduces a DS-STEPS line comment outside double-quoted strings,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Outside a double-quoted string, the first # on a line begins a comment that continues through the line's LF terminator. Whole-line comments and trailing comments are permitted. Comment text has no execution semantics and is ignored by the DS-STEPS parser after lexical recognition. A # inside a double-quoted string is ordinary string content and does not begin a comment; for example WORK ORDER AS ""Analysis #3"" and HEADER ""CATEGORY #"" preserve the hash character. WASM-002 defines no block-comment syntax. Comments are preserved byte-for-byte in the saved immutable WKO TXT. Editing, adding, or removing a comment changes the WKO bytes and therefore requires saving a new WKO artifact even though analytical semantics may remain unchanged.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-002,HEADER selects by exact decoded source-header value,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"HEADER ""name"" resolves against the exact decoded header values established for the certified source. Header equality is exact Unicode scalar-value sequence equality under PB-STOR-010: Data Sculptor performs no case folding, locale folding, Unicode normalization, trimming, or filesystem-style comparison. A selector that matches no source header must refuse. If the same exact decoded header sequence occurs in more than one source column, the header selector is ambiguous and must refuse rather than choose by position, discovery order, normalization, case-insensitive similarity, or another heuristic. An analyst can disambiguate duplicate exact header text with the 1-based COLUMN n selector. F-20 selector identity: HEADER always matches the authoritative exact decoded source header. It never matches an operational fallback name such as Column AA , a generated collision-disambiguation suffix, a COL alias, or a truncated form of the source header.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-003,COLUMN selects by 1-based source ordinal,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"COLUMN n identifies the source column by 1-based ordinal position. COLUMN 1 is the first source column. Zero, negative values, non-integers, and ordinals greater than the source width must refuse. Ordinal selection does not suppress source metadata: Data Sculptor must still resolve and record the selected column's actual decoded source header in the successor MAP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-004,HEADER and COLUMN selectors may be mixed but may not select one source column twice,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"One KEEP block may contain any supported mixture of HEADER and COLUMN selectors. Selector order expresses the analyst's requested selection order for the governed operation. After resolution, two or more selectors that identify the same physical source column constitute a duplicate selection and must refuse before materialization. Data Sculptor must not materialize the same source column twice merely because it was named once by header and once by ordinal.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-005,AS assigns the resulting materialized-column alias,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The optional clause AS ""alias"" belongs to the immediately preceding HEADER or COLUMN selector and expresses an intentional human-facing alias assignment in the governed Work Order. For a logical source column not present in the inherited MAP, omission of AS uses the exact source header as the default alias. For a logical source column already present in the inherited MAP, omission of AS preserves the inherited alias. An explicit AS overrides either default for the successor MAP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-006,The complete successor MAP must contain unique aliases,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"After inheritance, selector resolution, default-alias application, rematerialization continuity, and all explicit AS clauses are applied, every alias in the complete successor MAP must identify exactly one logical materialized column. If two different logical columns would have the same alias, including a collision with an inherited mapping, validation must refuse unless the Work Order has explicitly resolved the conflict through supported governed syntax. Data Sculptor must not invent suffixes such as Year_2 , use last-write-wins behavior, or silently shadow an existing alias. F-20 narrow generated-name exception: the prohibition on invented suffixes applies to ordinary source-header defaults and analyst-authored aliases. The only automatic suffixing permitted in WASM-002 is deterministic disambiguation of an oversized-header operational fallback under W002-STOR-019.7. That mechanism is not an alias-repair heuristic and must not be applied to an explicit AS value or to a short exact source-header default.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-007,MATERIALIZE commits the resolved KEEP set to the governed structural pass,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"MATERIALIZE is the explicit commitment verb for this WASM-002 DS-STEPS form. The KEEP selectors express which source columns belong in the operation; they do not themselves authorize data-row materialization. Before the bounded structural pass begins, the source, all selectors, actual source ordinals/headers, requested aliases, inherited alias state, and resulting alias uniqueness must be resolved and validated. Successful multi-column execution then follows the one-pass materialization contract.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-008,The Store MAP records resolved truth rather than selector spelling,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The successor Store MAP must record the fully resolved materialization result using the frozen eight-column schema store_alias,rid_filename,rid_alias,source_filename,source_column_number,source_header,alias,column_filename , regardless of whether the analyst selected a column with HEADER or COLUMN . For example, COLUMN 7 AS ""Crime Rate"" records the Store alias, RID filename/alias, common source filename, source ordinal 7 , the actual decoded header found at column 7, alias Crime Rate , and the newly generated physical COL filename. DS-STEPS expresses intent; the Store MAP persists the resolved durable mapping truth.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-009,DS-STEPS materialization syntax acceptance,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must cover: one column selected by exact header; one column selected by 1-based ordinal; mixed header/ordinal selectors in one KEEP block; multiple columns materialized in one governed structural pass; AS alias assignment; default header aliasing; inherited-alias preservation on rematerialization; explicit alias replacement on rematerialization; duplicate-header ambiguity refusal; invalid ordinal refusal; duplicate resolved-column refusal; and duplicate successor-alias refusal. Acceptance must also prove that the generated successor MAP records the same resolved source filename, source ordinal, actual source header, resulting alias, and physical COL identity whether a column was selected by header or by ordinal. For a new Store, both the single-column and multi-column materialization fixtures must contain no RID/row-index instruction yet must automatically publish exactly one RID artifact. For a later permitted same-Store materialization, the fixture must likewise contain no RID instruction and must reuse the original RID without publishing another. Damaged-lineage Help acceptance: fixtures must prove that exact source routing to an INVALID Store, and to a DEGRADED Store whose every mapped COL is broken, refuses ordinary materialization without silently treating the source as unseen. The canonical diagnostic/Help evidence must identify the blocked lineage/current MAP and preserve the frozen analyst-owned exits: external restoration under the original governed physical filename followed by governed validation; source rename to begin a distinct new Store lineage; or moving all lineage MAPs out of the active Suitcase to retire that lineage from routing. The all-COLs-broken fixture must warn that moving only the latest MAP is insufficient. No fixture may imply a new Data Sculptor recovery command, automatic RID regeneration, silent replacement of the damaged lineage, or historical byte identity based only on a restored filename. P3-06 validation-tier acceptance: acceptance must prove that a routine routing/status or alias-only path can use Tier 1 without an end-to-end scan of every RID/COL value, while an operation that consumes artifact contents performs Tier 2 before relying on them. Fixtures must include: a RID that passes Tier 1 but fails Tier 2 because its declared N /sequence is internally wrong beyond the Tier-1 boundary; a COL that passes Tier 1 but fails Tier 2 because its data-record count or CSV body is invalid beyond the Tier-1 boundary; and a REPAIR MAP fixture proving that the Tier-2 failure set determines exactly which COL bindings are removed. P3-07 routing acceptance: fixtures must prove that routing discovers a lineage from a structurally valid Store MAP regardless of whether later Store-health evaluation is VALID , DEGRADED , or INVALID . A separate fixture must present no routable lineage together with at least one structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifact in the active Suitcase and prove that ordinary materialization refuses before publishing a new RID or first Store MAP, while Help identifies the malformed MAP artifact or artifacts. No fixture may treat an all-MAPs-damaged condition as permission for a silent replacement lineage. F-08 cross-operation grammar acceptance: fixtures must prove the common preamble, ASCII-case-insensitive keywords, exact quoted-value preservation, required SPACE/TAB token separation, unknown-line refusal, one-operation-per-WKO refusal, and separation between DS-STEPS terminal phrases and Receipt OPERATION tokens. At least one fixture for each of the seven executable operations must prove that its canonical structure validates while an otherwise similar WKO containing another operation's terminal clause refuses. Separate fixtures must prove that browser Run does not require a textual RUN clause and that parsed RUN composition syntax refuses as deferred before analytical execution. P2-04 restoration-language acceptance: Help, diagnostics, UI text, and acceptance evidence may say that a file restored under the exact governed physical filename passed the required validation tier and may therefore re-enter use. They must not state or imply that filename equality alone proves restoration of the historical original bytes. If stronger historical-byte identity is desired, Help may point to the separately governed explicit fingerprint/LCK direction rather than silently hashing ordinary Store artifacts. F-20 selector/name/width acceptance: fixtures must additionally prove that HEADER resolves only against exact decoded source-header text and never against an operational fallback/default alias; a KEEP selecting all 16,384 columns is valid; a source wider than 16,384 refuses before data-row materialization; and RESET of an oversized-header COL restores the deterministic operational fallback rather than the exact oversized header as alias text. F-03 Store-health and REPAIR MAP acceptance set Target required: REPAIR MAP without exactly one current Store MAP target refuses. Historical target: a structurally valid but non-current historical Store MAP refuses for repair. Wrong profile: a WKO MAP supplied as the repair target refuses. DEGRADED repair: one or more broken COL bindings are removed while every valid binding and the exact RID identity are preserved. All COLs broken: repair refuses, publishes no successor MAP, and the Store remains DEGRADED . Malformed newest MAP: current-state resolution falls back to the greatest earlier structurally valid MAP in the same lineage and reports the malformed artifact. Missing COL in current valid MAP: no fallback occurs; the current MAP remains current and the Store evaluates DEGRADED . Missing RID in current valid MAP: no fallback occurs; the current MAP remains current and the Store evaluates INVALID . Original RID externally restored: the Store is re-evaluated after governed validation without Data Sculptor creating or inferring a replacement RID. No silent fork: neither DEGRADED nor INVALID permits ordinary materialization to create a replacement Store for the same routed lineage.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-003,Suitcase-relative Work Order portability acceptance,W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An acceptance fixture must execute a saved WKO containing SUITCASE: . and ordinary Suitcase-relative file references, then move the intact fixture Suitcase to a different permitted parent path and execute the same saved WKO again. Resolution must identify the same logical Suitcase files without editing the WKO to insert the new absolute machine path.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-004,WIP/WKO lifecycle acceptance,W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance evidence must show that an editable WIP cannot Run; saving a valid WIP produces a distinct immutable WKO Run target; loading that WKO and changing instruction text creates a new non-runnable WIP; and the original WKO bytes, filename, identity, and provenance remain unchanged. F-02 alias-registry lifecycle acceptance: a first save for an unused alias must publish a successor WKO MAP containing exactly one CURRENT row for that alias. Saving a second valid WKO with the same exact alias must surface exactly Replace alias target and Cancel . The Cancel fixture must leave the predecessor WKO MAP authoritative and must not commit the pending WKO/WKO-MAP pair as a registry update. The Replace fixture must publish a successor WKO MAP in which the former owner is DEPRECATED , the new WKO is the sole CURRENT row for that alias, and any earlier deprecated history remains preserved. The former WKO bytes and filename and every predecessor WKO MAP must remain unchanged. Alias resolution against the successor registry must resolve to the new CURRENT row and never to a DEPRECATED row. A malformed fixture containing more than one CURRENT row for one exact alias must fail structural validation rather than choose by filename UTC, modified time, discovery order, or row order. P2-03 WKO-registry clock acceptance: using a deterministic injected clock seam, acceptance must prove that a successor WKO MAP publishes only when the observed transaction UTC is strictly greater than the current structurally valid WKO MAP UTC; equal-millisecond and backward/future-dated-predecessor cases refuse without committing the new WKO/registry state. The diagnostic must expose predecessor_map_filename , predecessor_utc , and observed_host_utc . A separate fixture must deliberately move the future-dated current WKO MAP out of the active Suitcase, rescan, and prove deterministic reselection of the remaining current structurally valid WKO MAP without Data Sculptor silently moving or deleting anything itself. Day 060 H-12: every equal/backward/future-predecessor chronology refusal in this acceptance set must emit DS-UTC-001 with exact map_profile: WKO , observed_host_utc , predecessor_map_filename , and predecessor_utc facts. F-23 save-transaction filesystem-fault fixture, reconciled by F-33: using a controlled create/write/close/rename/promotion failure at a deterministic point after a valid WIP has entered the governed save path, acceptance must prove that a failed WKO/WKO-MAP save is never represented as a committed alias-registry update. The pre-run current WKO MAP must remain authoritative; no malformed or unpromoted candidate may become current; and any rollback or retained SCR evidence must follow W002-STOR-018.3 and the shared non-Store publication/retained-evidence contract. No RCV artifact is emitted. F-02 registry-repair acceptance set Deadlock escape: with a repair-required current WKO MAP, a newly saved structurally valid repair-only WKO can Run by exact filename and successfully publish a repaired successor registry. No broad bypass: a newly saved unregistered WKO for any other operation remains ineligible to Run. Missing reference: repair removes a stale registry row but does not recreate the missing WKO, substitute a historical WKO, or promote an older WKO automatically. Discovered alias, no owner: one discovered valid WKO with an otherwise unowned alias becomes CURRENT . Discovered alias collision: a discovered WKO whose alias is already owned by a surviving CURRENT row becomes DEPRECATED . Several discovered WKOs, no owner: all become DEPRECATED ; no winner is inferred by UTC, filename, UUID, directory order, discovery order, or modified time. Mandatory alias: an unaliased WKO cannot be structurally valid. Line endings: otherwise-identical structurally valid WKO fixtures with LF and CRLF line endings are accepted; the lone-CR form refuses. Deterministic successor: repaired successor rows serialize in ascending UTF-8 byte order of exact wko_filename . Historical Run: a registered DEPRECATED WKO can Run by exact physical filename but not by alias. Receipt identity: a successful or refused registry-repair Receipt uses REPAIR_WORK_ORDER_REGISTRY as the operation token. Day 060 H-10 / BM-07 registry-repair Receipt-count acceptance Acceptance must include a successful repair-required-registry fixture in which the exact repair-only bootstrap WKO is initially visible and unregistered, runs by the bounded exact-filename bootstrap, and is then registered by the repair result. The committed successor WKO MAP must contain the repair WKO row. The successful Receipt must list that exact repair WKO under either REGISTERED_CURRENT_WKO_<INDEX>_FILENAME or REGISTERED_DEPRECATED_WKO_<INDEX>_FILENAME , according to the ordinary alias-ownership rule. The corresponding REGISTERED_*_COUNT must equal the number of newly registered rows in that status class, including the repair WKO when applicable. Pre-existing surviving CURRENT / DEPRECATED rows in the base registry must not inflate either registered count. A fixture containing both pre-existing surviving rows and newly registered rows must prove that the Receipt reports the repair change set while the successor MAP reports the complete resulting registry state.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-005,"Store MAP inheritance, historical override, and immutable snapshot acceptance",W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An acceptance fixture must execute a saved Store-establishing Work Order containing multiple COL alias assignments when no routable Store lineage exists and no structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifact is present , and prove that exactly one new immutable complete Store MAP is created while the GUI supplies no alias-edit gesture and target artifacts remain unchanged. A later Work Order with the same exact source and no explicit MAP must route to that Store's lineage and inherit its unique newest permitted MAP automatically. Another Work Order must explicitly select an older valid MAP even though newer MAPs for that Store exist and prove that Store/RID binding, alias resolution, and inheritance use exactly the named historical MAP instead. A fixture specifying more than one MAP must refuse. A fixture with two otherwise permitted current MAP candidates for the selected Store sharing the greatest UTC millisecond timestamp must refuse automatic inheritance rather than use UUID as chronology. A separate fixture must remove or corrupt every Store MAP in a prior lineage so that no structurally valid Store MAP remains while at least one malformed Store-MAP-class artifact remains visible in the active Suitcase. Re-running ordinary materialization must refuse before creating a new RID or first Store MAP, and Help must identify the malformed MAP artifact or artifacts. P2-03 Store chronology acceptance: injected-clock fixtures must prove later observed UTC success, equal-millisecond refusal, backward-UTC refusal, and a genuinely future-dated current Store MAP that remains current while blocking successor publication. Every refusal must leave the chronology predecessor unchanged and publish no successor Store MAP. A historical-base fixture must derive requested state from an older eligible MAP while proving that the strict-greater-than comparison uses the actual current Store MAP as chronology predecessor, not the historical base. A deliberate analyst-removal fixture must move the future-dated current MAP out of the active Suitcase and prove deterministic reselection of the remaining structurally valid history; restoring that MAP must make ordinary greatest-UTC authority rules applicable again. Day 060 H-12: every equal/backward/future-predecessor Store-MAP chronology refusal in this acceptance set must emit DS-UTC-001 with exact map_profile: STORE , observed_host_utc , predecessor_map_filename , and predecessor_utc facts.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-006,Work Order chaining refusal acceptance,W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An acceptance fixture must submit a structurally saved WKO containing a RUN or other recognized Work Order-invocation construct and prove that WASM-002 refuses it during validation before Stage 1, Stage 2, conversion, inventory, or other governed execution begins. W002-UI-001,One explicit Work Order command surface,W002-UI,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The WASM-002 browser front end shall use the Work Order editor as the single human command-entry surface for governed execution. It shall not expose a second interactive command prompt or point-and-click analytical path that can become an independent source of analytical intent. The editable draft may be syntax-highlighted, validated, and saved, but it is not itself executable authority. The browser Run action operates only on one loaded/selected saved immutable WKO that is eligible under the governed Work Order registry rules. Run is a browser action, not a line that ordinary WASM-002 Work Orders must contain. If a WKO contains the reserved DS-STEPS RUN composition token, WASM-002 refuses before executing any child or top-level analytical operation because saved-Work-Order chaining is deferred. The token remains reserved so later ordered composition can be added without repurposing existing syntax. F-24 fresh-application state: each new Data Sculptor browser application instance begins without a selected Suitcase and without a restored unsaved Work Order draft. Initial page load and full reload therefore return the command surface to the pre-Suitcase gate. A previously selected folder, loaded WKO, or dirty WIP must not be silently reconstructed from browser-private persistence.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-UI-002,Front end presents and authorizes; shared Rust core decides,W002-UI,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The browser front end may authorize files, edit and validate Work Orders, invoke the shared engine, display governed state, render diagnostics, and present generated artifacts. It must not independently decide analytical truth, silently reinterpret a Work Order, or implement a competing semantic path. Where front-end presentation and shared-core semantics disagree, the shared governed semantics and frozen requirements are authoritative.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-UI-004,Certification gate is visible and blocking,W002-UI,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The front end shall visibly represent strict whole-file UTF-8 certification as a required stage before analytical materialization. A certification refusal must stop the current analytical Work Order, prevent later materialization stages from being presented as successful, and provide the canonical diagnostic / Help path.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-UI-005,One-pass multi-column materialization is represented truthfully,W002-UI,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"When a valid Work Order requests multiple source columns, the front end shall represent them as one governed multi-column materialization request through one bounded structural CSV pass, not as unrelated per-column scans when the frozen engine contract performs one pass. W002-UI-006,Visible Suitcase Directory is the artifact orientation surface,W002-UI,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"After Suitcase validation, the browser shall present a human-readable directory view of the visible files in the selected Suitcase, including physical filename, read-only governed alias where applicable, file type, and size. Governed artifacts created by a run shall appear in that same visible inventory after refresh or update. The directory is an orientation and metadata surface over the real flat Suitcase. It is not a hidden browser cache, a second persistence system, or an analytical command surface. CAT integration: this existing directory remains the sole WASM-002 artifact-orientation surface. CAT and MAP artifacts are first-ranked under W002-CAT-UI-001 through W002-CAT-UI-008; no second catalog browser is introduced.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-UI-007,All user-facing Help flows through the Help Engine,W002-UI,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"All Data Sculptor-controlled user-facing Help messages, warnings, refusals, explanations, validation guidance, safe-next-action messages, and governed success/status messages that participate in the Help/status/evidence system shall be produced through the Help Engine from governed facts or canonical diagnostic events. Individual UI controls must not maintain an independent competing stock of semantic Help text. Governed success/status events in this system use canonical INFO diagnostics. Ordinary static labels, headings, decorative copy, and presentation-only UI text are not diagnostics and need not be routed through the diagnostic registry merely because they are visible. Help voice may change wording and depth but must not change diagnostic identity, evidence, severity, refusal/continue behavior, provenance, or safe next action. Durable Help Reports derive from the same governed truth. F-17 fallback behavior: when a complete registered diagnostic lacks an authored help_messages.json entry, the UI must show the deterministic Generic Technical Help rendering from W002-HELP-002.9 for Casual, Office Speak, and Technical selections rather than a blank state, guessed prose, or UI-local explanation. When diagnostic assembly itself fails its required-fact contract, the UI presents DS-HLP-001 ; it must not display the incomplete intended diagnostic as if valid.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-UI-008,Legacy encoding conversion remains a separate operation,W002-UI,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"If UTF-8 certification fails and the bytes are eligible for the separately governed Windows-1252 compatibility/conversion path, the front end may explain or help draft that separate conversion Work Order. It must not silently reinterpret the failed analytical Work Order as Windows-1252 and continue materialization. P3-08 front-end disclosure: after a successful conversion, the visible result/Help path must identify the exact published CVT filename and explain that it is a new source identity for later Store routing. W002-UI-009,Front-end branding is presentation-only,W002-UI,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The WASM-002 browser front end shall use the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor branding and approved presentation tokens without changing analytical or diagnostic meaning. W002-PLAT-001,WASM-002/V1 browser and modest-hardware acceptance baseline,W002-PLAT,W002-PLAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The canonical modest-hardware acceptance machine for the WASM-002 browser release and the browser path carried into V1 is the project's 11-inch Windows 11 laptop with an Intel N100 processor, 16 GB RAM, and a 1920×1200 native display. W002-UI-ACC-017,"Store-aware MAP selection, historical override, and anti-rebinding acceptance",W002-UI-ACC,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A saved materializing Work Order that does not explicitly name a MAP must use exact SOURCE matching against the one common source_filename carried by each routable Store lineage's Store MAP. A routable Store lineage is one with at least one structurally valid Store MAP, regardless of later Store-health state. A fixture with exactly one routable Store lineage must route to that lineage and, when its health permits materialization, inherit the Store's unique newest permitted MAP and record both the MAP identity and bound rid_filename in execution evidence. A fixture with no routable Store lineage and no structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifact present may establish a new Store. A fixture with more than one routable Store lineage for the same source must refuse automatic selection. An explicit-MAP fixture must prove that SOURCE must exactly equal the selected MAP's common source_filename . A different source must refuse before materialization even when source/RID row counts happen to match. A separate all-MAPs-damaged fixture must leave one or more structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifacts visible while no routable lineage can be established. The UI/run path must refuse before new-Store/RID creation and expose Help that identifies the malformed MAP artifact or artifacts; it must not present the condition as an unseen source. Another fixture must prove that explicitly naming an older valid MAP overrides the newer default for that same Store. More than one explicitly named MAP must refuse. An equal-greatest-timestamp ambiguity within the selected Store lineage must refuse automatic selection. Once an inherited Store MAP has been selected for a run, creation of a newer MAP during execution must not silently rebind that in-progress run. P2-03 authority/clock acceptance: the UI/evidence path must distinguish the selected operation base MAP from the chronology predecessor used for successor UTC validation. When a future-dated current MAP blocks publication, the UI must not label that MAP corrupt merely because of its timestamp, must identify it as the blocking current authority, and must route to Help describing the clock correction/wait/deliberate-removal choices without performing any automatic fallback or filesystem move.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-UI-ACC-018,Help-Engine-only messaging acceptance,W002-UI-ACC,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For representative Suitcase validation, Work Order validation, source-resolution, and analytical refusal cases, user-facing guidance must be traceable to the Help Engine/canonical diagnostic path. Acceptance must show no competing ad hoc semantic refusal text generated independently by individual analytical controls.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-UI-ACC-019,No standalone Work Order Description acceptance,W002-UI-ACC,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must prove the architecture that WASM-002 permits: the browser exposes no standalone editable Work Order Description field; no separate mutable or hidden Work Order-description store exists; editing any governed WKO byte transitions a loaded saved WKO into a derived draft; the predecessor WKO TXT bytes, physical filename, and UUID remain unchanged; and the derived draft cannot Run until saved as a new WKO identity.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-UI-ACC-020,Theme semantic-invariance acceptance,W002-UI-ACC,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The same saved Work Order and governed diagnostic fixture must be exercised under Modern Dark and Modern Light. The browser must expose no Custom or Terminal governed theme choice in WASM-002. Acceptance must also verify that switching between Modern Dark and Modern Light does not change the canonical built-in presentation of a generated HLP or CER.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-UI-ACC-021,Flight Recorder read-only derivation acceptance,W002-UI-ACC,W002-UI,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must populate the Suitcase with governed RCP artifacts for at least one successful Run and one refused Run whose Receipt publication succeeded, then reconstruct the Flight Recorder surface solely from those Receipts. A separate fixture must represent a Run for which Receipt publication failed under W002-RCP-010 and prove that the Flight Recorder does not invent, backfill, or reconstruct a canonical Receipt from transient execution state. User interaction with the Flight Recorder must not modify, delete, rename, rewrite, supersede, or create RCP artifacts and must not create hidden persistent history state.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-ARCH-014,WASM-002 and V1 analytical execution are sequential,W002-ARCH,W002-ARCH,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WASM-002 must execute governed analytical operations sequentially and predictably. The product must not expose worker-count, thread-count, task-parallelism, or similar tuning controls, and it must not silently introduce a parallel analytical execution mode whose ordering or resource use changes the governed semantics. Sequential execution does not require inefficient repeated scans. One bounded structural source pass may process multiple requested columns together, and implementation may use ordinary low-level/runtime mechanisms that do not create user-visible analytical concurrency or change deterministic operation order. Any future analytical parallelism requires a separate measured experiment and explicit PRD decision.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-ARCH-014.1,WASM-002 has a single-writer Suitcase contract,W002-ARCH,W002-ARCH,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WASM-002 assumes one user, one active Suitcase, and one Data Sculptor writing execution context at a time . Multiple read-only views may observe the same Suitcase, but concurrent governed writers—including a second browser tab or window attempting governed writes against the same Suitcase—are outside the supported WASM-002 contract. WASM-002 does not implement cross-tab locks, filesystem leases, lockfiles, hidden coordination state, or multi-writer merge/rebase semantics. This is an explicit product boundary, not an implicit guarantee that concurrent writers are safe. Before a governed transaction reaches its authoritative commit point, Data Sculptor must re-resolve and revalidate the governing state on which the transaction depends. If relevant governed state has changed since the transaction established its basis, publication must refuse rather than overwrite the newer authority, silently rebase itself, synthesize another chronology, or report success. Candidates already created remain subject to the existing rollback and attributable SCR recovery-evidence rules. Help must explain the boundary in ordinary terms: do not run two writing Data Sculptor contexts against the same Suitcase at the same time. If a pre-commit guard detects changed authority, the safe next action is to refresh or reopen the current governed state and rerun deliberately. Acceptance evidence must inject a relevant Store-MAP and WKO-MAP authority change after transaction preparation but before commit and prove that the newer authority remains authoritative and the stale transaction refuses.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

PB-STOR-001,Suitcase is the complete Data Sculptor-controlled persistence surface,PB-STOR,PB-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every persistent project or analytical artifact intentionally created by Data Sculptor must be written into the visible, user-controlled Suitcase. Data Sculptor must not intentionally persist user data, analytical state, scratch state, logs, recovery state, or project metadata in hidden AppData-style locations or browser-private persistence such as OPFS. Incidental browser/OS runtime caches outside Data Sculptor control are explicitly outside this contract. F-24 browser-session persistence boundary: WASM-002 must not use IndexedDB, localStorage , OPFS, another browser-private database, or an equivalent hidden Data Sculptor-controlled persistence surface to remember a Suitcase directory handle, unsaved WIP text, project truth, analytical state, or live UI preferences between application instances. A later build may deliberately define a user-visible preferences or continuity mechanism, but WASM-002 does not create one implicitly. Volatile in-memory runtime state within the current application instance is permitted.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

PB-STOR-011,Generated identity collisions regenerate the UUID and never overwrite,PB-STOR,PB-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Data Sculptor must never overwrite, rename, truncate, or mutate an existing artifact merely because a newly generated governed filename collides with it. For an ordinary immutable artifact using the governed UTC+UUID identity grammar, Data Sculptor must keep the originally established canonical UTC millisecond creation timestamp, generate a new canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID v4, reconstruct the candidate filename, and try creation again. Collision retry must not advance or falsify the artifact creation timestamp merely to obtain a different sort position. This retry may repeat until an unused valid identity is obtained. If UUID generation fails, the host cannot safely test/create the target, or another filesystem error prevents safe allocation, creation must refuse through the canonical diagnostic path rather than risk overwrite. Collision retry changes only the not-yet-created artifact's UUID. UUID is never used as a chronology field.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

The artifact's governed content, lineage, receipt, fingerprint, provenance, and other required evidence establish what is actually true.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
PB-STOR-013,Ordinary immutable governed artifacts use class → UTC millisecond → UUID v4 identity order,PB-STOR,PB-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The exact default filename grammar for an ordinary immutable Data Sculptor-governed artifact is: __DS__CCC__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.<extension> CCC is the governed semantic artifact class. YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ is the artifact's governed UTC creation/publication timestamp at millisecond precision: four-digit year, two-digit month/day/hour/minute/second, exactly three millisecond digits, and literal T / Z . <uuid-v4> is a canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID v4. The extension is governed by the artifact's serialization contract. The token order is normative: namespace, semantic class, UTC timestamp, UUID, extension. UTC precedes UUID for every ordinary immutable class. Canonical UTC tokens with different values sort chronologically within the same class. UUID provides uniqueness and physical identity only; it must not be interpreted as a chronology tie-breaker when two artifacts share the same timestamp. When one governed all-or-refuse Store-state publication transaction creates multiple new analytical state artifacts, Data Sculptor establishes one canonical UTC millisecond publication-transaction timestamp before final identity allocation and uses that same UTC token for every newly published RID , COL , and MAP artifact created by that transaction. Each artifact receives its own UUID. Thus a first Store materialization gives the new RID, every newly materialized COL, and the successor MAP one shared transaction UTC; a later materialization gives only its newly created COL artifacts and successor MAP the new transaction UTC while the inherited RID and inherited COL artifacts retain their earlier identities. The shared transaction UTC is not the Work Order's authoring timestamp and does not require the Receipt filename UTC to match. RCP remains governed by W002-RCP-002 and carries its own receipt creation/publication timestamp. A shared transaction UTC expresses common publication membership, but MAP binding—not timestamp equality—remains authoritative for Store membership/current state. Source identity, source filename, run identity, parent identity, lineage, hashes, aliases, supersession, column identity, and other relationships must not be appended as ordinary identity tokens merely to make the filename descriptive; those facts belong in governed metadata and provenance. P2-03 successor-state UTC rule: when an operation will publish a successor Store MAP or successor WKO MAP, the transaction UTC remains a truthful observation of host UTC and must be strictly greater than the applicable chronology predecessor MAP UTC. Data Sculptor must not synthesize, increment, round forward, or otherwise fabricate a later UTC merely to satisfy chronology. UUID remains identity only and is never a chronology tie-breaker. The first MAP in a genuinely new Store lineage, and the first WKO MAP when no structurally valid WKO MAP exists, has no chronology predecessor and therefore uses the observed host UTC normally.",PARTIAL,PORTION_VERIFIED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,CP-004; CP-005,"CP004 and CP005 T-ACCEPTED, BANKED; full normative requirement remains partial",12c02a0f2ff51fae72599adc09332f50fed62ce8; cedd5d54506b8f3f879b96c5e64fefc9365b6eb0,Evidence/CP-004/CP004_RED_Test_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-004/CP004_Post_Format_Test_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-004/CP004_WASM_Build_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-004/CP004_Hash_Inventory_Verification.txt; Evidence/CP-005/CP005_RED_Test_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-005/CP005_Post_Format_Test_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-005/CP005_WASM_Build_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-005/CP005_Hash_Inventory_Verification.txt,"CP004: Immutable filename envelope, UTC and UUID syntax only. Native tests 12/12 passed; wasm32-target compilation succeeded; inventory 19/19 file hashes and sizes verified; 15 source/test/evidence files committed. Full requirement also governs true UTC millisecond identity, creation chronology, publication timestamp sharing, UUID identity semantics, and successor MAP chronology; none are implemented in CP004. Independent QA pending. CP005: CP005 now validates the timestamp token as a real Gregorian calendar date and ordinary UTC clock time (four-digit years 0001–9999, leap years, month lengths, 00–23 hours, 00–59 minutes/seconds, millisecond precision preserved lexically). Actual UTC issuance/publication, timestamp allocation, chronological truth, common transaction timestamp and identity authority are not implemented. Three integration tests with 40 timestamp cases and 12 prior regressions: 15/15 native tests PASS after Rustfmt; wasm32 compile PASS; 19/19 SHA-256+byte integrity PASS; 14 files committed. UTC leap-second 60 rejection is PROVISIONAL implementation assumption requiring QA/spec clarification; no browser runtime demonstrated. Independent Claude implementation QA pending.",Day065,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
PB-STOR-014,Store-state publication transactions share UTC but never UUID identity,PB-STOR,PB-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within one all-or-refuse Store-state publication transaction, every newly created RID , COL , and MAP final identity must carry the exact same canonical UTC millisecond transaction token and a distinct canonical UUID v4. UUID collision retry under PB-STOR-011 changes only the affected not-yet-created artifact UUID; it must not advance or alter the shared transaction UTC. Artifacts merely inherited or referenced by the transaction are not renamed, retimestamped, or assigned replacement UUIDs. A valid MAP may therefore bind artifacts created under several earlier transaction timestamps. Timestamp equality is evidence that artifacts were newly published by the same transaction; timestamp inequality is not evidence that artifacts belong to different Stores. P2-03 publication guard: for a successor Store-state transaction, the shared transaction UTC is established from truthful observed host UTC and is checked against the Store lineage's chronology predecessor before any newly created RID/COL/MAP artifact is promoted into its final governed class. If the observed transaction UTC is less than or equal to the chronology predecessor UTC, the publication refuses; the prior current MAP remains authoritative and no successor Store state commits.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-STOR-011,"Store, row-universe, and future Boolean-selection-column rule",W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Same-row derived columns and later aligned Boolean selection/filter columns remain within the same logical Store when row identity, row order, and cardinality are preserved. W002-RCP-005,Canonical Receipt TXT serialization is deterministic,W002-RCP,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The WASM-002 Receipt is UTF-8 without BOM and uses LF ( 0x0A ) line endings. Every Receipt ends with exactly one final LF. No serialized line carries trailing spaces, and no blank physical lines are emitted unless a later operation-specific grammar explicitly freezes them. It is a deterministic line-oriented KEY: VALUE document with a frozen core-key order followed by operation-specific fact sections in deterministic order. KEY is an uppercase ASCII field name. The separator is exactly one ASCII colon followed by exactly one ASCII space. KEY=VALUE is not valid canonical Receipt serialization. Fixed machine tokens and non-negative decimal integers are serialized unquoted. Human-authored text, filenames, aliases, headers, and other free text are serialized as double-quoted UTF-8 strings. Inside a quoted value, a literal double quote is represented by doubling it as """" . CR and LF are not permitted inside a single serialized value; each fact remains exactly one physical line. Enumerated values use the exact uppercase tokens frozen by the applicable requirement. Non-negative integers use ungrouped ASCII base-10 digits. This shared text rule is normative for all Receipt free-text values and is acceptance-tested byte-for-byte.",PARTIAL,PORTION_VERIFIED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,CP-016; CP-017; CP-018,"CP016 T-accepted, Git-banked: pure field-line formatting; CP017 T-accepted, Git-banked: caller-ordered field sequence; CP018 T-accepted, Git-banked: exactly ten ordered mandatory core keys in a core-only in-memory fragment. W002-RCP-006,Every Receipt records the fixed core execution facts and exact WKO lineage,W002-RCP,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every canonical WASM-002 Receipt begins with the following common envelope keys in exactly this order: RECEIPT_VERSION RECEIPT_FILENAME RECEIPT_UTC WORK_ORDER_FILENAME OPERATION RUN_STARTED_UTC RUN_FINISHED_UTC RESULT DIAGNOSTIC_ID IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES Day 060 H-02 version freeze: RECEIPT_VERSION is the unquoted integer 1 for the WASM-002 Receipt contract. RECEIPT_FILENAME is the exact physical governed RCP filename. RECEIPT_UTC is exactly the canonical UTC timestamp embedded in that filename and is distinct from the run start/finish timestamps. WORK_ORDER_FILENAME is the exact physical immutable WKO identity invoked and is the authoritative WKO→RCP lineage link. Day 060 H-09 / BM-06 truthful run-timestamp semantics RUN_STARTED_UTC and RUN_FINISHED_UTC are governed truthful host-UTC observations at millisecond precision. They are not decorative labels and are not synthesized from artifact filenames. RUN_STARTED_UTC is observed only after the exact saved WKO has been resolved and found eligible to Run, and immediately before operation-specific validation/execution begins. It therefore brackets operation validation, analytical work, publication attempts, refusal processing, and any governed rollback/cleanup performed by that Run. RUN_FINISHED_UTC is observed only after the operation has reached its final SUCCESS or REFUSED analytical outcome and all non-Receipt governed effects are settled: successful artifacts are committed, refusal state is established, and required rollback/cleanup or retained non-authoritative evidence classification is complete. Receipt publication begins only after this observation. For one Run, the truthful temporal invariant is: WKO_UTC ≤ RUN_STARTED_UTC ≤ each successfully published run-artifact UTC ≤ RUN_FINISHED_UTC ≤ RECEIPT_UTC where WKO_UTC is the governed UTC token embedded in the exact WORK_ORDER_FILENAME , and “run-artifact UTC” means the governed UTC embedded in each non-Receipt artifact successfully published by that Run, including a shared materialization transaction UTC where applicable. An operation that publishes no non-Receipt artifact simply has no middle artifact-UTC comparison. Equality is permitted because the canonical timestamp precision is milliseconds. Data Sculptor must not fabricate, increment, decrement, or reorder UTC values merely to make this invariant appear true. Receipt fixtures and retained acceptance evidence must use physically possible timelines under this rule. The existing rule that WKO and Receipt filename timestamps are not required to match remains unchanged: they are distinct events, but a WKO invoked by a Run must already exist as a governed artifact before that Run begins. RESULT is a closed WASM-002 vocabulary containing exactly SUCCESS and REFUSED . No other RESULT token is valid. DIAGNOSTIC_ID: NONE is used for an ordinary successful run; a refused run carries the exact governed diagnostic identity. The shared governed absence-state vocabulary is closed to these four tokens, with these exact meanings: NONE — the fact is applicable and definitively has no value in this event; NOT_RUN — the owning stage or operation was not executed; NOT_AVAILABLE — the fact is applicable or potentially applicable, but its value could not be obtained; NOT_APPLICABLE — the fact does not apply to this event, diagnostic, operation, or artifact. These states are semantically distinct and must not be substituted for one another. A count that was actually established as zero is serialized as the integer 0 , never as an absence token. The refusal-serialization matrix for every present operation-specific key is deterministic: State of the key's owning fact/stage at refusal Required serialization The fact was authoritatively established before refusal Serialize the exact governed value. The owning stage was never entered NOT_RUN . The owning stage ran and definitively produced no value/artifact for this event NONE . The fact applies but could not be obtained NOT_AVAILABLE . The fact does not apply to this event NOT_APPLICABLE . An applicable count was authoritatively established as zero 0 . A publication identity whose publication stage was never entered NOT_RUN , except where an earlier frozen operation-specific rule explicitly fixes another token. A publication identity whose publication stage was entered but no artifact of that identity successfully published NONE . A publication identity that successfully published The exact physical governed filename. For this contract, a fact is established only when its owning validation/stage has deterministically fixed the value and later execution cannot revise that fact. Candidate allocation, partial bytes, or an uncommitted publication does not establish a published-artifact identity. If parsing/validation refuses before one of the seven governed WASM-002 operations can be identified, the Receipt uses OPERATION: UNKNOWN_OPERATION , RESULT: REFUSED , and the applicable DIAGNOSTIC_ID . After the common envelope there is no operation-specific section; the Receipt proceeds directly to CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: 0 . UNKNOWN_OPERATION is not an executable operation. After all operation-specific facts and indexed lists, every Receipt ends with: CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: <N>
CREATED_ARTIFACT_001: ""...""
...
CREATED_ARTIFACT_N: ""..."" The created-artifact list contains only exact physical governed filenames successfully published by the run, excluding the Receipt itself. For this accounting, an artifact is successfully published only if it remains a committed governed artifact when the Run finishes; an artifact promoted and then rolled back, or left only as non-authoritative failure residue under All-or-Refuse, is excluded from CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT and its indexed list. Indexed suffixes are one-based decimal with a minimum width of three digits and no maximum width: 001 through 999 are zero-padded and 1000 onward uses the ordinary full ungrouped decimal form. When a count is zero, no indexed lines for that list appear. IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES is always present and is 0 when no governed filename-allocation retry occurred. Receipt/WKO filename timestamps are not required to match. One immutable WKO may be run multiple times, each producing a distinct Receipt that points back to the same exact WORK_ORDER_FILENAME . F-08 DS-STEPS / Receipt token separation. Human-authored Work Orders use the readable terminal clauses below; the Receipt serializes the corresponding machine token in OPERATION . The two columns are not interchangeable spellings: DS-STEPS terminal clause Receipt OPERATION MATERIALIZE MATERIALIZE INVENTORY INVENTORY UPDATE ALIASES UPDATE_ALIASES REPAIR MAP REPAIR_MAP REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY REPAIR_WORK_ORDER_REGISTRY CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 CONVERT_WINDOWS_1252_TO_UTF_8 CATALOG STORES CATALOG_STORES For example, REPAIR_MAP is not valid DS-STEPS syntax and REPAIR MAP is not the serialized Receipt token. UNKNOWN_OPERATION remains a refusal-only Receipt value when validation cannot identify one of these seven operations; it is not an executable operation.",PARTIAL,PORTION_VERIFIED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,CP-018,CP018 T-accepted and Git-banked: exact mandatory ten-core-key count and order in an in-memory formatting fragment only; no verified WKO lineage semantics or real execution facts.,75620f17649a5d38d5357960bb99e9ac39ae354f,Evidence/CP-018/ZIP/CP018_RED_StdErr.txt.zip; Evidence/CP-018/ZIP/CP018_GREEN_StdOut.txt.zip; Evidence/CP-018/ZIP/CP018_PostFormat_Regression_StdOut.txt.zip; Evidence/CP-018/ZIP/CP018_WASM_Build_Run_Record.txt.zip; Evidence/CP-018/ZIP/CP018_Custody_Seal_Record.txt.zip; CP018_Git_Banking_Record.txt (external after-commit record),"CP018 Day074: T-approved and locally Git-banked pure serialize_canonical_receipt_core_envelope enforces exactly the ten frozen header keys in order, calls existing CP017/CP016 serializer, refuses invalid count/order/value; nine targeted tests and 94/94 full native test regression pass, Rustfmt and WASM library compile pass. Does NOT prove correct data lineage, actual timestamps or vocabularies, operation-specific facts, durable writing or publication; independent Claude review and browser runtime not performed.",Day074,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RCP-007,"Materialization Receipts record Store, RID, Stage 1, Stage 2, and output facts",W002-RCP,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For a WASM-002 MATERIALIZE run, after the common envelope the Receipt serializes these operation-specific keys in exactly this order: SOURCE_FILENAME BASE_MAP_FILENAME RID_FILENAME RID_ACTION STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME CERTIFIED_SOURCE_BYTE_COUNT STAGE1_ELAPSED_MS UTF8_FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET UTF8_STOP_REASON WINDOWS_1252_COMPATIBILITY_OUTCOME WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET STAGE2_LOGICAL_ROW_COUNT STAGE2_ELAPSED_MS CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL REQUESTED_COLUMN_COUNT RESOLVED_COLUMN_COUNT PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT zero or more indexed published-COL filename lines whose exact key form is PUBLISHED_COL_<INDEX>_FILENAME (for example PUBLISHED_COL_001_FILENAME , PUBLISHED_COL_002_FILENAME ) SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_COUNT zero or more indexed fallback triplets: OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_001_COLUMN_ORDINAL , OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_001_ASSIGNED_NAME , OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_001_REASON , continuing under the common indexed-key rule. BASE_MAP_FILENAME: NONE denotes a newly established Store with no predecessor Store MAP. Day 060 H-11 / BM-08 RID_ACTION ownership and establishment RID_ACTION is a governed execution fact describing what this Run actually established for the Store RID path. It is never an intention, plan, or prediction. RID_ACTION: REUSED is established when routing has selected an existing Store, the exact inherited RID filename is known, and that inherited RID has passed the validation required to proceed. Because the RID already exists, this fact may be established before Stage 1 or Stage 2 completes. RID_ACTION: CREATED is established only when a new-Store RID candidate has successfully completed governed promotion into its final RID identity. Merely planning, allocating, writing, closing, validating, or naming an SCR candidate does not establish CREATED . Until either of those facts is established, the common refusal matrix governs RID_ACTION . For a new-Store path that refuses before successful RID promotion, RID_ACTION is NOT_RUN . If an existing-Store route is identified but the required inherited RID fact cannot be validly established, RID_ACTION is NOT_AVAILABLE . RID_FILENAME is a separate fact: for REUSED , it is the exact already-published inherited RID filename as soon as reuse is established; for CREATED , it is the exact governed final RID filename only after successful RID promotion; before new-RID promotion succeeds, no candidate/SCR filename may be serialized as though it were a published RID. With RID_ACTION: CREATED , RID_FILENAME records the RID identity successfully promoted during the Run even if that RID is later rolled back under All-or-Refuse; rollback does not erase the already-established RID_ACTION / RID_FILENAME execution facts. The refusal-boundary matrix is therefore: Materialization state RID_ACTION RID_FILENAME Validation/routing refuses before a Store/RID path is established NOT_RUN NOT_RUN or NOT_AVAILABLE only when an applicable routing fact could not be obtained under the common matrix New Store; Stage 1 refusal NOT_RUN NOT_RUN New Store; Stage 2 refusal NOT_RUN NOT_RUN New Store; post-Stage-2 gate refusal before RID promotion NOT_RUN NOT_RUN New Store; RID candidate/promotion has not successfully completed NOT_RUN NOT_RUN New Store; RID promotion succeeds CREATED exact published RID filename Existing Store; exact inherited RID selected and validated REUSED exact inherited RID filename Existing Store; later Stage 1, Stage 2, gate, or publication refusal after reuse was established REUSED exact inherited RID filename Existing lineage identified but required inherited RID cannot be validly established NOT_AVAILABLE NOT_AVAILABLE A refusal Receipt that says RID_ACTION: CREATED while RID_FILENAME is NONE or NOT_RUN and no RID was successfully promoted is invalid evidence. STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME has exactly two completed Stage-1 values: PASS and FAIL . If Stage 1 never ran, the value is NOT_RUN . If Stage 1 began but a separate failure prevented a governed PASS/FAIL determination, the value is NOT_AVAILABLE . NOT_APPLICABLE is not valid for this key. UTF8_FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET and UTF8_STOP_REASON are refusal-only Stage-1 evidence. On STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: FAIL , the offset is mandatory and is the exact zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first byte of the invalid sequence, and the stop reason is mandatory and exactly INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE . Neither field may be NOT_AVAILABLE when the Stage-1 outcome is FAIL . On PASS , both fields are NOT_APPLICABLE . If Stage 1 never ran, both are NOT_RUN . If Stage 1 began but no UTF-8 PASS/FAIL conclusion was established because of a separate failure, both refusal-only fields are NOT_APPLICABLE . WINDOWS_1252_COMPATIBILITY_OUTCOME and WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET are the governed F-16 follow-on facts. They are evaluated only after STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: FAIL . When the complete second pass reaches EOF with every byte mappable, the outcome is COMPATIBLE and the offset is NOT_APPLICABLE . When the pass encounters one of the undefined bytes frozen in W002-CONV-002.4, the outcome is INCOMPATIBLE and the offset is the exact zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first such byte. If the pass begins but an independent failure prevents a conclusion, both fields are NOT_AVAILABLE . If Stage 1 did not conclude FAIL , the compatibility pass does not run and both fields are NOT_RUN . The five exact CSV refusal keys CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION , CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET , CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE , CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD , and CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL carry the exact structural CSV refusal condition and location oracle frozen in W002-MAT-002.8. If Stage 2 never ran, all five are NOT_RUN ; if Stage 2 completed without an applicable CSV refusal, all five are NOT_APPLICABLE ; on a CSV refusal, each established location fact is serialized and any applicable fact that could not be obtained is NOT_AVAILABLE . The MATERIALIZE refusal-stage matrix is: Refusal boundary Validation/routing and request facts Stage 1 facts Stage 2 facts Publication facts Validation, before Stage 1 Serialize each fact already established; an applicable fact that validation could not obtain is NOT_AVAILABLE . REQUESTED_COLUMN_COUNT is the actual count when the KEEP list parsed completely; otherwise NOT_AVAILABLE . RESOLVED_COLUMN_COUNT and fallback records are NOT_RUN until name/ordinal resolution has run. NOT_RUN for all Stage 1-owned facts. NOT_RUN for all Stage 2-owned facts. PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 ; no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NOT_RUN . Stage 1 refusal Established validation/routing facts are exact values. Serialize the exact Stage 1 outcome/timing and established refusal evidence; incomplete applicable facts are NOT_AVAILABLE . The Windows-1252 compatibility fields then serialize the exact complete assessment result under the rule above; if an independent assessment failure prevents a conclusion, they are NOT_AVAILABLE . NOT_RUN for all Stage 2-owned facts. PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 ; no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NOT_RUN . Stage 2 refusal Established validation/routing facts are exact values. Completed Stage 1 facts are exact values; UTF-8 refusal fields are NOT_APPLICABLE when no UTF-8 refusal occurred. Because Stage 1 passed, both Windows-1252 compatibility fields are NOT_RUN . STAGE2_ELAPSED_MS is the actual elapsed time when obtained; STAGE2_LOGICAL_ROW_COUNT is NOT_AVAILABLE unless the complete accepted logical row count was established; CSV refusal facts follow the rule above. PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 ; no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NOT_RUN . Post-Stage-2 gate refusal before publication All facts established through the gate are serialized exactly; non-applicable UTF-8/CSV refusal fields are NOT_APPLICABLE . Both Windows-1252 compatibility fields are NOT_RUN because Stage 1 passed. PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 ; no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NOT_RUN . Publication refusal before the successor-MAP publication stage is entered All facts established before refusal are serialized exactly. This row includes a new-Store RID/COL identity-allocation or promotion refusal that occurs before the successor-MAP publication stage is entered. Completed Stage 1 and Stage 2 facts remain exact; non-applicable UTF-8/CSV refusal fields use their governed absence tokens, and both Windows-1252 compatibility fields are NOT_RUN because Stage 1 passed. A candidate filename is never serialized as a published identity. Publication refusal after the successor-MAP publication stage is entered All facts established before refusal are serialized exactly. Completed Stage 1 and Stage 2 facts remain exact; non-applicable UTF-8/CSV refusal fields use their governed absence tokens, and both Windows-1252 compatibility fields are NOT_RUN because Stage 1 passed. Under All-or-Refuse publication, PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 and no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NONE because the successor-MAP publication stage was entered but no successor MAP successfully published. A candidate filename is never serialized as a published identity. Success All applicable facts are exact values; refusal-only UTF-8/CSV fields are NOT_APPLICABLE . W002-RCP-009,"Receipt truth is execution evidence, not presentation authority",W002-RCP,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The Receipt records what Data Sculptor actually attempted, observed, refused, and successfully published. It must not reinterpret the analyst's WKO, replace the Store MAP, or become a second analytical command surface. The WKO remains the durable authorization record; Store MAP/RID/COL artifacts remain the governed analytical state; diagnostic events remain the refusal/help truth; the Receipt cross-references those facts as the durable run ledger. The body of published canonical RCP artifacts is the authoritative evidence substrate for the Flight Recorder logical view defined in W002-STOR-012.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RCP-010,Receipt-publication failure is itself a governed evidence failure,W002-RCP,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Data Sculptor must never claim that a durable Receipt exists until the RCP file has been successfully written and closed in the Suitcase. If host or filesystem failure prevents Receipt publication, the browser must surface a canonical diagnostic through the Help Engine stating that receipt evidence could not be persisted. A receipt-publication failure does not retroactively falsify analytical artifacts that were already successfully committed under their own publication contracts, but the user-facing run summary must clearly distinguish analytical outcome from receipt-persistence failure. Data Sculptor must not invent, backdate, or silently reconstruct a Receipt and present it as the original run artifact. F-14 publication path, reconciled by F-33: the RCP itself is first written as the corresponding SCR candidate under W002-STOR-023.1, closed, reopened and validated against the exact Receipt serialization/key contract before the class-token rename to RCP . If final RCP promotion fails, the candidate remains non-authoritative SCR evidence. Help may identify the exact retained SCR filename when that fact was established, but it must still state that the canonical Receipt was not persisted. WASM-002 does not emit an RCV artifact for this failure.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RCP-ACC-001,Successful materialization Receipt and WKO-lineage acceptance,W002-RCP-ACC,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A Store-establishing materialization fixture must run one saved WKO, publish exactly one canonical TXT RCP, and prove that the Receipt identifies the exact WKO through WORK_ORDER_FILENAME , source, RID_ACTION: CREATED , new RID, Stage 1 result/bytes/time, Stage 2 row count/time, all requested COL artifacts in resolved KEEP order, successor Store MAP, published-artifact count, timestamps, and RESULT: SUCCESS . The RCP filename UTC must represent the Receipt artifact's own creation/publication event and must not be required to equal the WKO filename UTC. The same immutable WKO must then be executable again in an appropriate fixture, producing a second distinct RCP with its own Receipt/run timestamps while both Receipts contain the same exact WORK_ORDER_FILENAME . A later same-Store materialization fixture must additionally prove RID_ACTION: REUSED and the original RID filename. The Store-establishing fixture must also prove that the newly created RID, every newly created COL, and the successor MAP carry one identical publication-transaction UTC token while each has a distinct UUID; the RCP filename UTC remains its own Receipt publication timestamp and is not required to equal that analytical transaction UTC. A later same-Store materialization must prove that newly created COLs and its successor MAP share the later transaction UTC while the inherited RID retains its original timestamp/UUID. F-07 Stage-1 success fixture: a successful materialization Receipt must serialize STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: PASS , with UTF8_FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET: NOT_APPLICABLE and UTF8_STOP_REASON: NOT_APPLICABLE . Separate refusal fixtures under W002-RCP-ACC-002 must prove FAIL plus the mandatory exact offset and INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE . F-20 maximum-width Receipt acceptance: a successful full-width materialization fixture must prove that published-COL indexed keys continue through PUBLISHED_COL_16384_FILENAME using the minimum-three-digit/no-maximum suffix rule. Oversized-header fixtures must prove the exact fallback count, source ordinal, assigned operational name, and SOURCE_HEADER_EXCEEDS_1024_SCALARS reason without embedding the oversized source-header text in the Receipt merely as fallback evidence. F-23 additional successful-Receipt coverage: acceptance must include a successful INVENTORY run whose RCP carries the exact governed INVENTORY operation-specific facts and a successful UPDATE_ALIASES run whose RCP carries the exact BASE_MAP_FILENAME and SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME while reporting only actually published artifacts in the common created-artifact tail. F-23 UUID-collision seam: using a controlled UUID sequence, acceptance must force one or more governed filename collisions before successful allocation. Every pre-existing colliding artifact must remain byte-for-byte unchanged; allocation must retain the originally established governed UTC context while changing only the not-yet-created UUID as permitted; and the published Receipt must report the exact retry count in IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES . Day 060 H-09 success-timeline acceptance Every retained successful Receipt fixture must satisfy the W002-RCP-006 temporal invariant using its actual embedded UTC tokens. Acceptance must mechanically prove: the invoked WKO UTC is less than or equal to RUN_STARTED_UTC ; every non-Receipt governed artifact successfully published by that Run has a governed artifact/transaction UTC between RUN_STARTED_UTC and RUN_FINISHED_UTC , inclusive; RUN_FINISHED_UTC is less than or equal to the Receipt filename/ RECEIPT_UTC ; and no fixture relies on an artifact timestamp that occurs after the Receipt that claims it, or before the Run that created it. A controlled-clock acceptance seam may be used to make equality and strict-order cases deterministic, but the fixture generator must not alter timestamps after the fact merely to satisfy the checker. Day 060 H-11 successful RID_ACTION acceptance A successful new-Store materialization Receipt may report RID_ACTION: CREATED only because the RID was actually promoted into its final governed RID identity during that Run. Acceptance must prove the W002-RCP-010 boundary exactly: no final RCP is fabricated or claimed, any retained candidate evidence follows the governed SCR retention/non-authority rules in W002-STOR-023.1, no RCV artifact is emitted, the user-facing diagnostic distinguishes analytical outcome from Receipt-persistence failure, and already committed analytical artifacts are not retroactively falsified solely because RCP persistence failed. F-23 ultimate identity-allocation failure fixture: with Receipt publication itself still available, a controlled identity-allocation seam must force a governed operation artifact to exhaust/fail safe allocation. Day 060 H-02 fixture binding: the retained golden corpus must use RECEIPT_VERSION: 1 and the fixture-pinned diagnostic allocations in W002-HELP-001.8. The corpus must contain one success Receipt for each of the seven executable operations, one refusal Receipt for every distinct refusal-boundary row in W002-RCP-007/W002-RCP-008, the three additional Stage-1 compatibility variants needed to cover COMPATIBLE , INCOMPATIBLE , and NOT_AVAILABLE after UTF-8 failure, and one UNKNOWN_OPERATION Receipt.
