Independent QA pending. CP005: CP005 now validates the timestamp token as a real Gregorian calendar date and ordinary UTC clock time (four-digit years 0001–9999, leap years, month lengths, 00–23 hours, 00–59 minutes/seconds, millisecond precision preserved lexically). Actual UTC issuance/publication, timestamp allocation, chronological truth, common transaction timestamp and identity authority are not implemented. Three integration tests with 40 timestamp cases and 12 prior regressions: 15/15 native tests PASS after Rustfmt; wasm32 compile PASS; 19/19 SHA-256+byte integrity PASS; 14 files committed. PB-STOR-014,Store-state publication transactions share UTC but never UUID identity,PB-STOR,PB-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within one all-or-refuse Store-state publication transaction, every newly created RID , COL , and MAP final identity must carry the exact same canonical UTC millisecond transaction token and a distinct canonical UUID v4. UUID collision retry under PB-STOR-011 changes only the affected not-yet-created artifact UUID; it must not advance or alter the shared transaction UTC. Artifacts merely inherited or referenced by the transaction are not renamed, retimestamped, or assigned replacement UUIDs. A valid MAP may therefore bind artifacts created under several earlier transaction timestamps. Timestamp equality is evidence that artifacts were newly published by the same transaction; timestamp inequality is not evidence that artifacts belong to different Stores. P2-03 publication guard: for a successor Store-state transaction, the shared transaction UTC is established from truthful observed host UTC and is checked against the Store lineage's chronology predecessor before any newly created RID/COL/MAP artifact is promoted into its final governed class. W002-RCP-005,Canonical Receipt TXT serialization is deterministic,W002-RCP,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The WASM-002 Receipt is UTF-8 without BOM and uses LF ( 0x0A ) line endings. Every Receipt ends with exactly one final LF. No serialized line carries trailing spaces, and no blank physical lines are emitted unless a later operation-specific grammar explicitly freezes them. It is a deterministic line-oriented KEY: VALUE document with a frozen core-key order followed by operation-specific fact sections in deterministic order. KEY is an uppercase ASCII field name. The separator is exactly one ASCII colon followed by exactly one ASCII space. KEY=VALUE is not valid canonical Receipt serialization. Fixed machine tokens and non-negative decimal integers are serialized unquoted. Human-authored text, filenames, aliases, headers, and other free text are serialized as double-quoted UTF-8 strings. Inside a quoted value, a literal double quote is represented by doubling it as """" . CR and LF are not permitted inside a single serialized value; each fact remains exactly one physical line. Enumerated values use the exact uppercase tokens frozen by the applicable requirement. Non-negative integers use ungrouped ASCII base-10 digits. This shared text rule is normative for all Receipt free-text values and is acceptance-tested byte-for-byte.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RCP-006,Every Receipt records the fixed core execution facts and exact WKO lineage,W002-RCP,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every canonical WASM-002 Receipt begins with the following common envelope keys in exactly this order: RECEIPT_VERSION RECEIPT_FILENAME RECEIPT_UTC WORK_ORDER_FILENAME OPERATION RUN_STARTED_UTC RUN_FINISHED_UTC RESULT DIAGNOSTIC_ID IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES Day 060 H-02 version freeze: RECEIPT_VERSION is the unquoted integer 1 for the WASM-002 Receipt contract. RECEIPT_FILENAME is the exact physical governed RCP filename. RECEIPT_UTC is exactly the canonical UTC timestamp embedded in that filename and is distinct from the run start/finish timestamps. WORK_ORDER_FILENAME is the exact physical immutable WKO identity invoked and is the authoritative WKO→RCP lineage link. Day 060 H-09 / BM-06 truthful run-timestamp semantics RUN_STARTED_UTC and RUN_FINISHED_UTC are governed truthful host-UTC observations at millisecond precision. They are not decorative labels and are not synthesized from artifact filenames. RUN_STARTED_UTC is observed only after the exact saved WKO has been resolved and found eligible to Run, and immediately before operation-specific validation/execution begins. It therefore brackets operation validation, analytical work, publication attempts, refusal processing, and any governed rollback/cleanup performed by that Run. RUN_FINISHED_UTC is observed only after the operation has reached its final SUCCESS or REFUSED analytical outcome and all non-Receipt governed effects are settled: successful artifacts are committed, refusal state is established, and required rollback/cleanup or retained non-authoritative evidence classification is complete. Receipt publication begins only after this observation. For one Run, the truthful temporal invariant is: WKO_UTC ≤ RUN_STARTED_UTC ≤ each successfully published run-artifact UTC ≤ RUN_FINISHED_UTC ≤ RECEIPT_UTC where WKO_UTC is the governed UTC token embedded in the exact WORK_ORDER_FILENAME , and “run-artifact UTC” means the governed UTC embedded in each non-Receipt artifact successfully published by that Run, including a shared materialization transaction UTC where applicable. An operation that publishes no non-Receipt artifact simply has no middle artifact-UTC comparison. Equality is permitted because the canonical timestamp precision is milliseconds. Data Sculptor must not fabricate, increment, decrement, or reorder UTC values merely to make this invariant appear true. Receipt fixtures and retained acceptance evidence must use physically possible timelines under this rule. The existing rule that WKO and Receipt filename timestamps are not required to match remains unchanged: they are distinct events, but a WKO invoked by a Run must already exist as a governed artifact before that Run begins. RESULT is a closed WASM-002 vocabulary containing exactly SUCCESS and REFUSED . No other RESULT token is valid. DIAGNOSTIC_ID: NONE is used for an ordinary successful run; a refused run carries the exact governed diagnostic identity. The shared governed absence-state vocabulary is closed to these four tokens, with these exact meanings: NONE — the fact is applicable and definitively has no value in this event; NOT_RUN — the owning stage or operation was not executed; NOT_AVAILABLE — the fact is applicable or potentially applicable, but its value could not be obtained; NOT_APPLICABLE — the fact does not apply to this event, diagnostic, operation, or artifact. These states are semantically distinct and must not be substituted for one another. A count that was actually established as zero is serialized as the integer 0 , never as an absence token. The refusal-serialization matrix for every present operation-specific key is deterministic: State of the key's owning fact/stage at refusal Required serialization The fact was authoritatively established before refusal Serialize the exact governed value. The owning stage was never entered NOT_RUN . The owning stage ran and definitively produced no value/artifact for this event NONE . The fact applies but could not be obtained NOT_AVAILABLE . The fact does not apply to this event NOT_APPLICABLE . An applicable count was authoritatively established as zero 0 . A publication identity whose publication stage was never entered NOT_RUN , except where an earlier frozen operation-specific rule explicitly fixes another token. A publication identity whose publication stage was entered but no artifact of that identity successfully published NONE . A publication identity that successfully published The exact physical governed filename. For this contract, a fact is established only when its owning validation/stage has deterministically fixed the value and later execution cannot revise that fact. Candidate allocation, partial bytes, or an uncommitted publication does not establish a published-artifact identity. If parsing/validation refuses before one of the seven governed WASM-002 operations can be identified, the Receipt uses OPERATION: UNKNOWN_OPERATION , RESULT: REFUSED , and the applicable DIAGNOSTIC_ID . After the common envelope there is no operation-specific section; the Receipt proceeds directly to CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: 0 . UNKNOWN_OPERATION is not an executable operation. After all operation-specific facts and indexed lists, every Receipt ends with: CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: <N>
CREATED_ARTIFACT_001: ""...""
...
CREATED_ARTIFACT_N: ""..."" The created-artifact list contains only exact physical governed filenames successfully published by the run, excluding the Receipt itself. For this accounting, an artifact is successfully published only if it remains a committed governed artifact when the Run finishes; an artifact promoted and then rolled back, or left only as non-authoritative failure residue under All-or-Refuse, is excluded from CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT and its indexed list. Indexed suffixes are one-based decimal with a minimum width of three digits and no maximum width: 001 through 999 are zero-padded and 1000 onward uses the ordinary full ungrouped decimal form. When a count is zero, no indexed lines for that list appear. IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES is always present and is 0 when no governed filename-allocation retry occurred. Receipt/WKO filename timestamps are not required to match. One immutable WKO may be run multiple times, each producing a distinct Receipt that points back to the same exact WORK_ORDER_FILENAME . F-08 DS-STEPS / Receipt token separation. Human-authored Work Orders use the readable terminal clauses below; the Receipt serializes the corresponding machine token in OPERATION . The two columns are not interchangeable spellings: DS-STEPS terminal clause Receipt OPERATION MATERIALIZE MATERIALIZE INVENTORY INVENTORY UPDATE ALIASES UPDATE_ALIASES REPAIR MAP REPAIR_MAP REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY REPAIR_WORK_ORDER_REGISTRY CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 CONVERT_WINDOWS_1252_TO_UTF_8 CATALOG STORES CATALOG_STORES For example, REPAIR_MAP is not valid DS-STEPS syntax and REPAIR MAP is not the serialized Receipt token. UNKNOWN_OPERATION remains a refusal-only Receipt value when validation cannot identify one of these seven operations; it is not an executable operation.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RCP-007,"Materialization Receipts record Store, RID, Stage 1, Stage 2, and output facts",W002-RCP,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For a WASM-002 MATERIALIZE run, after the common envelope the Receipt serializes these operation-specific keys in exactly this order: SOURCE_FILENAME BASE_MAP_FILENAME RID_FILENAME RID_ACTION STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME CERTIFIED_SOURCE_BYTE_COUNT STAGE1_ELAPSED_MS UTF8_FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET UTF8_STOP_REASON WINDOWS_1252_COMPATIBILITY_OUTCOME WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET STAGE2_LOGICAL_ROW_COUNT STAGE2_ELAPSED_MS CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL REQUESTED_COLUMN_COUNT RESOLVED_COLUMN_COUNT PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT zero or more indexed published-COL filename lines whose exact key form is PUBLISHED_COL_<INDEX>_FILENAME (for example PUBLISHED_COL_001_FILENAME , PUBLISHED_COL_002_FILENAME ) SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_COUNT zero or more indexed fallback triplets: OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_001_COLUMN_ORDINAL , OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_001_ASSIGNED_NAME , OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_001_REASON , continuing under the common indexed-key rule. BASE_MAP_FILENAME: NONE denotes a newly established Store with no predecessor Store MAP. Day 060 H-11 / BM-08 RID_ACTION ownership and establishment RID_ACTION is a governed execution fact describing what this Run actually established for the Store RID path. It is never an intention, plan, or prediction. RID_ACTION: REUSED is established when routing has selected an existing Store, the exact inherited RID filename is known, and that inherited RID has passed the validation required to proceed. Because the RID already exists, this fact may be established before Stage 1 or Stage 2 completes. RID_ACTION: CREATED is established only when a new-Store RID candidate has successfully completed governed promotion into its final RID identity. Merely planning, allocating, writing, closing, validating, or naming an SCR candidate does not establish CREATED . Until either of those facts is established, the common refusal matrix governs RID_ACTION . For a new-Store path that refuses before successful RID promotion, RID_ACTION is NOT_RUN . If an existing-Store route is identified but the required inherited RID fact cannot be validly established, RID_ACTION is NOT_AVAILABLE . RID_FILENAME is a separate fact: for REUSED , it is the exact already-published inherited RID filename as soon as reuse is established; for CREATED , it is the exact governed final RID filename only after successful RID promotion; before new-RID promotion succeeds, no candidate/SCR filename may be serialized as though it were a published RID. With RID_ACTION: CREATED , RID_FILENAME records the RID identity successfully promoted during the Run even if that RID is later rolled back under All-or-Refuse; rollback does not erase the already-established RID_ACTION / RID_FILENAME execution facts. The refusal-boundary matrix is therefore: Materialization state RID_ACTION RID_FILENAME Validation/routing refuses before a Store/RID path is established NOT_RUN NOT_RUN or NOT_AVAILABLE only when an applicable routing fact could not be obtained under the common matrix New Store; Stage 1 refusal NOT_RUN NOT_RUN New Store; Stage 2 refusal NOT_RUN NOT_RUN New Store; post-Stage-2 gate refusal before RID promotion NOT_RUN NOT_RUN New Store; RID candidate/promotion has not successfully completed NOT_RUN NOT_RUN New Store; RID promotion succeeds CREATED exact published RID filename Existing Store; exact inherited RID selected and validated REUSED exact inherited RID filename Existing Store; later Stage 1, Stage 2, gate, or publication refusal after reuse was established REUSED exact inherited RID filename Existing lineage identified but required inherited RID cannot be validly established NOT_AVAILABLE NOT_AVAILABLE A refusal Receipt that says RID_ACTION: CREATED while RID_FILENAME is NONE or NOT_RUN and no RID was successfully promoted is invalid evidence. STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME has exactly two completed Stage-1 values: PASS and FAIL . If Stage 1 never ran, the value is NOT_RUN . If Stage 1 began but a separate failure prevented a governed PASS/FAIL determination, the value is NOT_AVAILABLE . NOT_APPLICABLE is not valid for this key. UTF8_FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET and UTF8_STOP_REASON are refusal-only Stage-1 evidence. On STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: FAIL , the offset is mandatory and is the exact zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first byte of the invalid sequence, and the stop reason is mandatory and exactly INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE . Neither field may be NOT_AVAILABLE when the Stage-1 outcome is FAIL . On PASS , both fields are NOT_APPLICABLE . If Stage 1 never ran, both are NOT_RUN . If Stage 1 began but no UTF-8 PASS/FAIL conclusion was established because of a separate failure, both refusal-only fields are NOT_APPLICABLE . WINDOWS_1252_COMPATIBILITY_OUTCOME and WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET are the governed F-16 follow-on facts. They are evaluated only after STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: FAIL . When the complete second pass reaches EOF with every byte mappable, the outcome is COMPATIBLE and the offset is NOT_APPLICABLE . When the pass encounters one of the undefined bytes frozen in W002-CONV-002.4, the outcome is INCOMPATIBLE and the offset is the exact zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first such byte. If the pass begins but an independent failure prevents a conclusion, both fields are NOT_AVAILABLE . If Stage 1 did not conclude FAIL , the compatibility pass does not run and both fields are NOT_RUN . The five exact CSV refusal keys CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION , CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET , CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE , CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD , and CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL carry the exact structural CSV refusal condition and location oracle frozen in W002-MAT-002.8. If Stage 2 never ran, all five are NOT_RUN ; if Stage 2 completed without an applicable CSV refusal, all five are NOT_APPLICABLE ; on a CSV refusal, each established location fact is serialized and any applicable fact that could not be obtained is NOT_AVAILABLE . The MATERIALIZE refusal-stage matrix is: Refusal boundary Validation/routing and request facts Stage 1 facts Stage 2 facts Publication facts Validation, before Stage 1 Serialize each fact already established; an applicable fact that validation could not obtain is NOT_AVAILABLE . REQUESTED_COLUMN_COUNT is the actual count when the KEEP list parsed completely; otherwise NOT_AVAILABLE . RESOLVED_COLUMN_COUNT and fallback records are NOT_RUN until name/ordinal resolution has run. NOT_RUN for all Stage 1-owned facts. NOT_RUN for all Stage 2-owned facts. PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 ; no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NOT_RUN . Stage 1 refusal Established validation/routing facts are exact values. Serialize the exact Stage 1 outcome/timing and established refusal evidence; incomplete applicable facts are NOT_AVAILABLE . The Windows-1252 compatibility fields then serialize the exact complete assessment result under the rule above; if an independent assessment failure prevents a conclusion, they are NOT_AVAILABLE . NOT_RUN for all Stage 2-owned facts. PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 ; no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NOT_RUN . Stage 2 refusal Established validation/routing facts are exact values. Completed Stage 1 facts are exact values; UTF-8 refusal fields are NOT_APPLICABLE when no UTF-8 refusal occurred. Because Stage 1 passed, both Windows-1252 compatibility fields are NOT_RUN . STAGE2_ELAPSED_MS is the actual elapsed time when obtained; STAGE2_LOGICAL_ROW_COUNT is NOT_AVAILABLE unless the complete accepted logical row count was established; CSV refusal facts follow the rule above. PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 ; no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NOT_RUN . Post-Stage-2 gate refusal before publication All facts established through the gate are serialized exactly; non-applicable UTF-8/CSV refusal fields are NOT_APPLICABLE . Both Windows-1252 compatibility fields are NOT_RUN because Stage 1 passed. PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 ; no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NOT_RUN . Publication refusal before the successor-MAP publication stage is entered All facts established before refusal are serialized exactly. This row includes a new-Store RID/COL identity-allocation or promotion refusal that occurs before the successor-MAP publication stage is entered. Completed Stage 1 and Stage 2 facts remain exact; non-applicable UTF-8/CSV refusal fields use their governed absence tokens, and both Windows-1252 compatibility fields are NOT_RUN because Stage 1 passed. Under All-or-Refuse publication, PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 and no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NOT_RUN because the successor-MAP publication stage was never entered. A candidate filename is never serialized as a published identity. Publication refusal after the successor-MAP publication stage is entered All facts established before refusal are serialized exactly. Any RID fact already established before this later refusal remains governed by the RID_ACTION/RID_FILENAME matrix above. Completed Stage 1 and Stage 2 facts remain exact; non-applicable UTF-8/CSV refusal fields use their governed absence tokens, and both Windows-1252 compatibility fields are NOT_RUN because Stage 1 passed. Under All-or-Refuse publication, PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT: 0 and no indexed published-COL filename lines; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME: NONE because the successor-MAP publication stage was entered but no successor MAP successfully published. A candidate filename is never serialized as a published identity. Success All applicable facts are exact values; refusal-only UTF-8/CSV fields are NOT_APPLICABLE . Both Windows-1252 compatibility fields are NOT_RUN because Stage 1 passed. PUBLISHED_COL_COUNT is the actual count; indexed keys are exactly PUBLISHED_COL_001_FILENAME onward in resolved KEEP order; SUCCESSOR_MAP_FILENAME is the exact published successor MAP filename. Day 060 H-24 / BM-08 publication-boundary split: these two MATERIALIZE publication-refusal rows apply the common W002-RCP-006 ownership rule to the successor-MAP publication stage. NOT_RUN means that stage was never entered; NONE means it was entered but no successor MAP successfully published. The early boundary is exercised by the RID identity-allocation exhaustion fixture; the later boundary has its own byte-exact golden fixture. OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_COUNT is NOT_RUN until operational-name resolution has run; afterward it is the established non-negative count, including literal 0 . Fallback records are ordered by ascending physical source-column ordinal. the exact fallback key OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_<INDEX>_REASON is exactly SOURCE_HEADER_EXCEEDS_1024_SCALARS . For successful Store-establishing materialization, the common created-artifact list is ordered RID first, newly published COLs in resolved KEEP order, then successor MAP. For successful existing-Store materialization, the inherited RID is not newly created; the list contains newly published COLs in resolved KEEP order followed by the successor MAP. P3-09 Receipt oracle: when Stage 2 refuses because the certified source contains no logical CSV record, the five CSV refusal fields must serialize exactly as CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION: NO_HEADER_RECORD , CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET: <exact source byte length> , CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE: 1 , CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD: 1 , and CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL: 1 . Day 060 H-13 / BM-10 clarification: within those five governed CSV refusal fields, the zero-byte and UTF-8-BOM-only cases differ only in CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET : 0 versus 3 . Their complete Receipt bytes also differ wherever the underlying source identity, certified source byte count, Work Order identity, run/Receipt timestamps, Receipt filename/UUID, or other fixture-specific governed facts differ. The complete Receipts must never be described as differing only by one field. F-20 operational-name Receipt oracle: OPERATIONAL_NAME_FALLBACK_COUNT counts selected/materialized columns whose exact source header exceeded 1,024 Unicode scalar values. Each corresponding ..._ASSIGNED_NAME stores the final deterministic operational/default-alias name after any permitted fallback collision disambiguation; ..._REASON remains exactly SOURCE_HEADER_EXCEEDS_1024_SCALARS . The Receipt does not copy the oversized exact source header merely to explain the fallback. The common indexed-key rule from W002-RCP-006 applies without a maximum width. W002-RCP-010,Receipt-publication failure is itself a governed evidence failure,W002-RCP,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Data Sculptor must never claim that a durable Receipt exists until the RCP file has been successfully written and closed in the Suitcase. A receipt-publication failure does not retroactively falsify analytical artifacts that were already successfully committed under their own publication contracts, but the user-facing run summary must clearly distinguish analytical outcome from receipt-persistence failure. Data Sculptor must not invent, backdate, or silently reconstruct a Receipt and present it as the original run artifact. F-14 publication path, reconciled by F-33: the RCP itself is first written as the corresponding SCR candidate under W002-STOR-023.1, closed, reopened and validated against the exact Receipt serialization/key contract before the class-token rename to RCP . If final RCP promotion fails, the candidate remains non-authoritative SCR evidence. Help may identify the exact retained SCR filename when that fact was established, but it must still state that the canonical Receipt was not persisted. WASM-002 does not emit an RCV artifact for this failure.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RCP-ACC-001,Successful materialization Receipt and WKO-lineage acceptance,W002-RCP-ACC,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A Store-establishing materialization fixture must run one saved WKO, publish exactly one canonical TXT RCP, and prove that the Receipt identifies the exact WKO through WORK_ORDER_FILENAME , source, RID_ACTION: CREATED , new RID, Stage 1 result/bytes/time, Stage 2 row count/time, all requested COL artifacts in resolved KEEP order, successor Store MAP, published-artifact count, timestamps, and RESULT: SUCCESS . The RCP filename UTC must represent the Receipt artifact's own creation/publication event and must not be required to equal the WKO filename UTC. The same immutable WKO must then be executable again in an appropriate fixture, producing a second distinct RCP with its own Receipt/run timestamps while both Receipts contain the same exact WORK_ORDER_FILENAME . A later same-Store materialization fixture must additionally prove RID_ACTION: REUSED and the original RID filename. The Store-establishing fixture must also prove that the newly created RID, every newly created COL, and the successor MAP carry one identical publication-transaction UTC token while each has a distinct UUID; the RCP filename UTC remains its own Receipt publication timestamp and is not required to equal that analytical transaction UTC. A later same-Store materialization must prove that newly created COLs and its successor MAP share the later transaction UTC while the inherited RID retains its original timestamp/UUID. F-07 Stage-1 success fixture: a successful materialization Receipt must serialize STAGE1_UTF8_OUTCOME: PASS , with UTF8_FIRST_INVALID_BYTE_OFFSET: NOT_APPLICABLE and UTF8_STOP_REASON: NOT_APPLICABLE . Separate refusal fixtures under W002-RCP-ACC-002 must prove FAIL plus the mandatory exact offset and INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE . F-20 maximum-width Receipt acceptance: a successful full-width materialization fixture must prove that published-COL indexed keys continue through PUBLISHED_COL_16384_FILENAME using the minimum-three-digit/no-maximum suffix rule. Oversized-header fixtures must prove the exact fallback count, source ordinal, assigned operational name, and SOURCE_HEADER_EXCEEDS_1024_SCALARS reason without embedding the oversized source-header text in the Receipt merely as fallback evidence. Every pre-existing colliding artifact must remain byte-for-byte unchanged; allocation must retain the originally established governed UTC context while changing only the not-yet-created UUID as permitted; and the published Receipt must report the exact retry count in IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES . Day 060 H-09 success-timeline acceptance Every retained successful Receipt fixture must satisfy the W002-RCP-006 temporal invariant using its actual embedded UTC tokens. A controlled-clock acceptance seam may be used to make equality and strict-order cases deterministic, but the fixture generator must not alter timestamps after the fact merely to satisfy the checker. W002-RCP-ACC-002,Refusal Receipt acceptance,W002-RCP-ACC,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A saved WKO that is actually Run and deterministically refuses must still produce one canonical TXT Receipt when Receipt publication itself remains available. The emitted bytes must conform to the closed RESULT vocabulary, the four governed absence tokens, the exact operation-specific key spelling/order, and the refusal matrix in W002-RCP-006 through W002-RCP-008. Acceptance must include byte-exact golden Receipt fixtures for every distinct refusal-boundary row required to exercise the serialization matrix for each of the seven executable WASM-002 operations: MATERIALIZE , INVENTORY , UPDATE_ALIASES , REPAIR_MAP , REPAIR_WORK_ORDER_REGISTRY , CONVERT_WINDOWS_1252_TO_UTF_8 , and CATALOG_STORES . Multiple Diagnostic IDs that map to the same refusal boundary and the same serialization row do not require duplicate byte fixtures merely because the Diagnostic ID differs. Acceptance must additionally include one byte-exact UNKNOWN_OPERATION refusal fixture proving the common envelope, OPERATION: UNKNOWN_OPERATION , RESULT: REFUSED , the exact diagnostic ID, absence of any operation-specific section, and immediate CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: 0 . Fixtures must prove that NONE , NOT_RUN , NOT_AVAILABLE , and NOT_APPLICABLE retain distinct meanings; an established zero count is serialized as 0 ; no candidate filename is reported as a published identity; and every indexed key uses its complete frozen name and the minimum-three-digit/no-maximum suffix rule. An unsaved WIP must be proven unable to Run and therefore must not create an execution Receipt. F-16 materialization-refusal fixtures: byte-exact MATERIALIZE refusal Receipts must exercise the new compatibility pair in all four applicable states: NOT_RUN when Stage 1 did not fail; COMPATIBLE plus NOT_APPLICABLE offset; INCOMPATIBLE plus the exact first undefined-byte offset; and NOT_AVAILABLE / NOT_AVAILABLE when an independent compatibility-read failure prevents a conclusion. F-23 Receipt-publication failure fixture, reconciled by F-33: a controlled filesystem-fault seam must make canonical RCP publication fail after the underlying analytical/refusal outcome has been established. Acceptance must prove the W002-RCP-010 boundary exactly: no final RCP is fabricated or claimed, any retained candidate evidence follows the governed SCR retention/non-authority rules in W002-STOR-023.1, no RCV artifact is emitted, the user-facing diagnostic distinguishes analytical outcome from Receipt-persistence failure, and already committed analytical artifacts are not retroactively falsified solely because RCP persistence failed. F-23 ultimate identity-allocation failure fixture: with Receipt publication itself still available, a controlled identity-allocation seam must force a governed operation artifact to exhaust/fail safe allocation. The operation must refuse without overwriting or mutating any colliding pre-existing artifact, and the refusal Receipt/diagnostic evidence must preserve the established collision/allocation-failure facts under PB-STOR-011 and W002-STOR-007.3. Day 060 H-02 fixture binding: the retained golden corpus must use RECEIPT_VERSION: 1 and the fixture-pinned diagnostic allocations in W002-HELP-001.8. The corpus must contain one success Receipt for each of the seven executable operations, one refusal Receipt for every distinct refusal-boundary row in W002-RCP-007/W002-RCP-008, the three additional Stage-1 compatibility variants needed to cover COMPATIBLE , INCOMPATIBLE , and NOT_AVAILABLE after UTF-8 failure, and one UNKNOWN_OPERATION Receipt. Publication-refusal fixtures may use the operation-specific H-02 publication diagnostic and a non-zero IDENTITY_COLLISION_RETRIES value to satisfy the ultimate identity-allocation-failure acceptance boundary without inventing a second diagnostic solely for the same serialization row. Day 060 H-09 refusal-timeline acceptance Every retained refusal Receipt fixture must also satisfy the W002-RCP-006 temporal invariant. For a refusal with no successfully published non-Receipt artifact, acceptance proves WKO_UTC ≤ RUN_STARTED_UTC ≤ RUN_FINISHED_UTC ≤ RECEIPT_UTC . If a refusal legitimately leaves one or more successfully committed non-Receipt artifacts from an already-completed stage, each such artifact UTC must fall between Run start and Run finish and must be listed truthfully under the governing created-artifact rules. Day 060 H-11 / BM-08 RID_ACTION refusal acceptance Byte-exact MATERIALIZE refusal acceptance must distinguish new-Store and existing-Store RID paths: new-Store validation, Stage 1, Stage 2, and post-Stage-2 gate refusals before successful RID promotion serialize RID_ACTION: NOT_RUN and do not serialize a candidate as a published RID; a controlled new-Store refusal after RID promotion has successfully completed may serialize RID_ACTION: CREATED together with the exact published RID filename, but only if that RID was actually promoted and the remaining refusal/rollback evidence is truthful under the publication rules; an existing-Store refusal after the inherited RID has been selected and validated serializes RID_ACTION: REUSED and the exact inherited RID filename even when Stage 1, Stage 2, a later gate, or publication subsequently refuses; an existing lineage whose required inherited RID cannot be validly established serializes RID_ACTION: NOT_AVAILABLE and RID_FILENAME: NOT_AVAILABLE rather than claiming reuse. Acceptance must specifically reject the historical H-02 fixture pattern that reported RID_ACTION: CREATED while no RID existed and CREATED_ARTIFACT_COUNT: 0 . Day 060 H-12 H-02 publication-diagnostic scope The H-02 operation-specific publication diagnostics whose required facts are artifact_class and collision_retry_count are acceptance pins for governed filename identity-allocation collision exhaustion. They are not catch-all Diagnostic IDs for unrelated publication failures such as chronology guards, write/close/rename failures, or malformed predecessor state. Those distinct conditions use their own registry allocations; DS-UTC-001 is independently frozen for the strict monotonic-UTC guard. Day 060 H-13 / BM-10 zero-byte and BOM-only NO_HEADER_RECORD Receipt fixtures The retained golden corpus must contain two distinct byte-exact MATERIALIZE refusal Receipts for the P3-09 no-header boundary: Zero-byte source: the bound source has exact certified byte count 0 ; Stage 1 passes; Stage 2 refuses with CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION: NO_HEADER_RECORD ; CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET: 0 ; CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE: 1 ; CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD: 1 ; and CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL: 1 . UTF-8-BOM-only source: the bound source consists exactly of bytes EF BB BF and has exact certified byte count 3 ; Stage 1 passes; Stage 2 refuses with CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION: NO_HEADER_RECORD ; CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET: 3 ; CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE: 1 ; CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD: 1 ; and CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL: 1 . These two Receipt fixtures must carry their own truthful source filenames, Work Order identities, run timestamps, Receipt identities, and other governed facts. Only the five-field CSV refusal tuple has the narrower relationship stated in W002-RCP-007; the complete Receipt files are not otherwise required to be byte-identical. Day 060 H-14 / BM-11 CONVERT undefined-byte Receipt binding The coordinated golden Receipt corpus must include the byte-exact CONVERT_WINDOWS_1252_TO_UTF_8 refusal fixture from W002-CONV-ACC-002 using source bytes 41 81 42 . Its Receipt must carry UNDEFINED_WINDOWS_1252_BYTE_OFFSET: 1 and the exact pre-transcoding refusal values frozen in W002-RCP-008.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RCP-ACC-003,Receipt TXT is invariant to presentation state in WASM-002,W002-RCP-ACC,W002-RCP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,The same governed run must be exercised under materially different permitted browser presentation states. W002-RID-001,A Suitcase may contain multiple Stores and each current Store state binds exactly one RID,W002-RID,W002-RID,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The Suitcase is a workspace and may contain zero, one, or multiple logical Stores. Every committed Store state binds exactly one governed current RID artifact. RID values are unique only within their Store row universe; they are not Suitcase-global identifiers. Ordinary same-row-universe work reuses that RID unchanged. In WASM-002, a missing, unreadable, or invalid current RID makes the Store INVALID ; no executable WASM-002 operation regenerates or substitutes that RID. Read-only Help/evidence may explain analyst-owned restoration or lineage-retirement choices, but Data Sculptor does not publish a replacement RID. The stable logical row reference in WASM-002 is conceptually (Store lineage, RID value) ; the current physical RID identity is the exact rid_filename bound by the authoritative MAP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RID-002,The Store RID is generated automatically once and reused unchanged in WASM-002,W002-RID,W002-RID,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"When the first successful materialization establishes a new Store, Data Sculptor must automatically generate that Store's initial RID artifact as part of the same Stage 2 operation and the same all-or-refuse publication boundary. The analyst does not separately request ordinary RID generation. Before the RID SCR candidate is created, Data Sculptor establishes the materialization publication-transaction UTC under PB-STOR-013/PB-STOR-014 and allocates a RID-specific UUID. The canonical RID byte stream is then written as the visible governed SCR candidate whose filename already carries that exact UTC, UUID, and .csv extension intended for the final RID identity. Requested materialized columns likewise begin as governed SCR candidates whose distinct COL-specific UUIDs are allocated before those candidates are opened under the same transaction UTC. The new RID candidate and all requested COL candidates must reach EOF, reconcile to the same accepted Store row count N, and pass their required final validation before any candidate is promoted. After complete-set validation, Data Sculptor promotes the RID candidate first by host rename that changes only the three-letter semantic class token from SCR to RID . The candidate bytes, UTC token, UUID, and .csv extension must remain unchanged across that promotion. Requested COL candidates are promoted only after RID promotion succeeds. If later promotion or successor-MAP publication prevents transaction commit, the newly promoted RID is not committed Store state merely because an RID-looking file exists; it must be rolled back where safely possible or retained as attributable recovery evidence under the materialization failure contract. A first Store-establishing materialization commits exactly one RID regardless of how many requested COLs are materialized. Later ordinary materializations and other same-row-universe WASM-002 operations must reuse that RID unchanged. They must not create a new RID candidate, regenerate, replace, renumber, or silently supersede the inherited RID. RID reconstruction/replacement is not an executable WASM-002 operation. Any future governed RID-recovery design remains deferred and must be reintroduced by an explicit later PRD freeze.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RID-003,RID physical identity uses the governed RID filename grammar,W002-RID,W002-RID,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The physical RID filename must be: __DS__RID__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv The filename contains governed physical identity only. A Store name or friendly analyst alias must not be inserted into, substituted for, or used to rename this immutable physical RID filename.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RID-004,RID is a canonical one-column CSV containing the exact sequence 1 through N,W002-RID,W002-RID,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The RID artifact must serialize as a canonical one-column UTF-8 CSV with: exactly one UTF-8 BOM at byte zero; a structural first logical record exactly N=<value> , where <value> is the canonical unsigned base-10 representation of the Store's total logical data-row count N ; uppercase N , exactly one equals sign, no spaces, no sign, no leading zeroes except the single digit 0 , and no separators or locale formatting; LF ( 0x0A ) record terminators on every supported host; exactly N data records after the header, containing the consecutive unquoted decimal integers 1 through N in order; no zero RID data value, negatives, signs, thousands separators, decimal points, exponent notation, or leading zeroes; and a final LF after the last record. For N=0 , the canonical bytes are the UTF-8 BOM followed by N=0 and LF, with no data records. The N=<value> record is structural metadata and does not consume a Store row. The governed RID artifact class/filename and Store MAP binding identify the artifact as a RID; the literal header RID is not used by the frozen WASM-002 serialization.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RID-005,RID cardinality and order define same-Store column alignment,W002-RID,W002-RID,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"If a Store RID contains N data records, every governed column claimed to be aligned to that Store must contain exactly N data records in the same RID order. Data Sculptor must not describe a shorter, longer, reordered, duplicated, or row-shifted column as aligned to that Store. This invariant applies to materialized source columns in WASM-002 and is the stable contract that later calculated, Boolean-selection, verification, or left-join enrichment columns may rely upon.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RID-006,A different row universe requires a different Store and a new RID,W002-RID,W002-RID,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,An operation that changes which rows exist or changes their governed order does not mutate the existing Store RID. It establishes a different row universe and therefore requires a new logical Store identity and a new RID artifact beginning again at 1 for that new Store. Filtering that is represented only as a same-length aligned Boolean/selection column does not itself change the row universe; building a new reduced/reordered row set later would.,NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-RID-007,The Store MAP gives RID a friendly alias without changing RID identity,W002-RID,W002-RID,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The physical RID artifact remains identified by its immutable governed filename and semantic RID class. W002-RID-008,Ordinary RID generation is implicit Store infrastructure; RID reconstruction is deferred,W002-RID,W002-RID,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WASM-002 materialization Work Orders specify the analyst's requested source columns and aliases. W002-INV-002,Suitcase Inventory uses the governed INV artifact class and canonical filename grammar,W002-INV,W002-INV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A successful inventory produces exactly one visible flat TXT artifact whose physical filename is: __DS__INV__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.txt The UTC and UUID tokens follow the existing governed artifact-identity rules. W002-INV-003,"The lightweight inventory records filename, exact byte length, and last-modified metadata",W002-INV,W002-INV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For every regular file present in the authorized flat Suitcase root at snapshot time, the inventory must record: the exact visible filename; the exact byte length reported by the host file object; and the host/browser-reported last-modified value rendered in the canonical UTC millisecond form when available. If usable last-modified metadata is unavailable, the inventory must represent that fact explicitly rather than invent a timestamp. P3-10 last-modified availability test: host/browser last-modified metadata is usable only when the host supplies a finite, non-negative whole-number millisecond value that can be represented in the canonical UTC millisecond timestamp form. If that test fails, the inventory must serialize the governed unavailable value rather than infer, round, substitute, or fabricate a timestamp.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-INV-004,INVENTORY does not read file contents or compute content hashes,W002-INV,W002-INV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The lightweight inventory must be produced from directory enumeration and file metadata only. Data Sculptor must not open and stream the contents of each listed file merely to create the inventory, and it must not compute SHA-256 or another content fingerprint as an implicit side effect. Its cost should therefore scale primarily with the number of directory entries and metadata calls, not with the aggregate byte size of the files. A 7 GB CSV and a 7 KB CSV each contribute one metadata entry rather than requiring their contents to be read.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-INV-005,Inventory scope is the authorized flat Suitcase root,W002-INV,W002-INV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WASM-002 inventories regular files and immediate child directory entries in the directory denoted by SUITCASE: . . Data Sculptor must not recursively inspect, enumerate, size, hash, or otherwise inventory the contents of a child directory in this build. Each immediate child directory is recorded as a directory entry by its exact visible name only. Its nested contents and aggregate size are outside the WASM-002 Inventory contract. This rule preserves the flat-Suitcase storage model while making the presence of user-created directories explicit rather than silently omitting them. F-26 SOURCE distinction: inclusion in an Inventory is evidence that an entry was physically visible to the Inventory operation; it does not make that entry eligible for a Work Order SOURCE . SOURCE eligibility is the narrower contract in W002-WKO-009.1.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-INV-006,Inventory serialization is deterministic UTF-8 TXT,W002-INV,W002-INV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The INV artifact is a deterministic human-readable TXT document encoded as UTF-8 without BOM, using LF ( 0x0A ) line endings, the same KEY: VALUE line grammar, and the same quoted-text escaping rule frozen by W002-RCP-005. Every INV ends with exactly one final LF, contains no trailing spaces, and contains no blank physical lines. The exact V1 Inventory serialization order is: INVENTORY_VERSION INVENTORY_UTC WORK_ORDER_FILENAME SUITCASE ENTRY_COUNT for each regular-file entry in deterministic ascending exact-filename UTF-8 byte order, one contiguous indexed triplet: FILE_<INDEX> , FILE_<INDEX>_BYTE_LENGTH , FILE_<INDEX>_LAST_MODIFIED_UTC DIRECTORY_COUNT exactly DIRECTORY_COUNT directory-name records using contiguous indexed keys DIRECTORY_<INDEX> , ordered by ascending exact-directory-name UTF-8 bytes. INVENTORY_VERSION is the unquoted integer 1 for this contract. WORK_ORDER_FILENAME , SUITCASE , each FILE_<INDEX> filename, and each DIRECTORY_<INDEX> name use the common double-quoted UTF-8 text serialization. FILE_<INDEX>_BYTE_LENGTH is the exact non-negative ungrouped ASCII base-10 byte length. FILE_<INDEX>_LAST_MODIFIED_UTC is either the exact canonical UTC millisecond token governed by W002-INV-003 or the unquoted governed absence token NOT_AVAILABLE . Indexed suffixes are one-based decimal with a minimum width of three digits and no maximum width: 001 through 999 are zero-padded and 1000 onward uses the full ungrouped decimal form. When ENTRY_COUNT or DIRECTORY_COUNT is zero, no indexed lines for that list appear. ENTRY_COUNT remains the regular-file count. Directory records contain the exact immediate child directory name only and do not imply recursive inspection or a computed directory size. Filename and directory-name representations remain unambiguous even when a name contains whitespace, quotes, or delimiter-like characters because the common quote-doubling rule applies. P3-10 inventory timestamp binding: INVENTORY_UTC must equal the exact canonical UTC token embedded in the final governed __DS__INV__<UTC>__<uuid-v4>.txt filename, just as RECEIPT_UTC is bound to the governed Receipt filename UTC. The INV body and filename therefore cannot claim different capture times.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-INV-007,The current inventory describes the pre-publication Suitcase state and excludes itself,W002-INV,W002-INV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,Data Sculptor must enumerate and fix the inventory snapshot before publishing the new INV artifact. The INV artifact being created is therefore not one of its own listed entries. Any older INV artifact that already existed at snapshot time is an ordinary Suitcase file and is included like any other file. This pre-publication rule prevents recursive self-reference while preserving an accurate snapshot of the state that existed immediately before the new inventory evidence was added.,NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-INV-008,"Help describes INVENTORY as a quick continuity aid, not byte-level proof",W002-INV,W002-INV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Help must explain that an INV snapshot is useful for ordinary closeout and later orientation: it can reveal additions, removals, renames, size changes, or last-modified changes when snapshots or current metadata are compared. Help must also state that unchanged filename/size/last-modified metadata does not prove that file contents or row order are identical. When stronger assurance is warranted because files may change unexpectedly, Help may recommend the explicit later/deeper content-fingerprinting workflow; INVENTORY itself must never imply forensic or cryptographic assurance.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-INV-ACC-001,Large-file inventory acceptance proves metadata-only behavior,W002-INV-ACC,W002-INV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An acceptance fixture must place at least one multi-gigabyte file plus several small files in the authorized Suitcase, execute INVENTORY , and prove that the resulting INV records the correct filename, exact byte length, and last-modified metadata without reading the multi-gigabyte file contents. P3-10 metadata determinism: acceptance must include at least one file with usable host last-modified metadata and one test double/fixture in which the last-modified value fails the governed availability test. The accepted INV must also prove that INVENTORY_UTC exactly matches the UTC token in its final INV filename. The INV snapshot is taken before publication of the new INV artifact and before its Receipt publication. Therefore the INV being created and the Receipt for that Run do not appear as pre-existing entries in their own inventory snapshot. A later implementation fixture may use different exact governed filenames/UUIDs while preserving the same reachable-state requirement and deterministic ordering.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-STOR-016,Work Order filenames use the governed immutable identity grammar,W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"When Data Sculptor saves a new Work Order as a WKO, it shall assign the physical TXT filename.
