W002-CAT-ACC-001,CAT acceptance proves collection-scale orientation without centralizing Store authority,W002-CAT-ACC,W002-CAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must include a MusicBrainz-scale fixture containing 177 routable CSV Store lineages, each with its own authoritative current Store MAP. One explicit analyst-run CATALOG STORES Work Order must publish exactly one CAT snapshot containing exactly 177 data rows under the frozen five-column schema store_alias,source_filename,rid_filename,map_filename,store_health and deterministic MAP-filename ordering. The fixture must include Stores that evaluate VALID , DEGRADED , and INVALID while retaining structurally valid current MAPs, and the CAT must record the exact health observed for each Store when the catalog run occurs. The CAT must not expose a separate MAP-health field. The existing Suitcase Directory must surface CAT and MAP artifacts ahead of ordinary files; the analyst must be able to open CAT, inspect the collection, select and view MAP artifacts, sort/filter the directory, and inspect other Suitcase files without a Work Order. No direct GUI mutation path may be exposed. Acceptance must alter authoritative MAP/Store state after the first CAT publication and prove that the earlier CAT is neither rewritten nor automatically refreshed. It remains visible and becomes stale/inconsistent where appropriate. Only a later explicit CATALOG STORES Work Order may reconstruct the collection and publish a new immutable CAT snapshot. The linked WASM-003 DIR behavior remains outside the WASM-002 implementation scope: later DIR requirements auto-populate human-readable CAT/MAP descriptions, but those descriptions never become authority over CAT, MAP, or Store semantics.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STOR-020,"Store, RID, and COL aliases remain human-facing metadata separate from physical identity",W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Aliases are governed human-facing metadata. Creating, changing, clearing, or replacing an alias must not rename or rewrite the underlying artifact. Within one Store MAP, every non-empty COL alias and the non-empty rid_alias must be unambiguous within the row-addressable artifact alias namespace under the exact Unicode scalar-value comparison rule in PB-STOR-010. F-15 publication-time shadowing boundary: alias uniqueness and physical-name shadowing are validated when a candidate successor Store MAP is being published, against the comparison domain applicable to that one Store snapshot and the then-visible governed physical targets it makes row-addressable. If an alias would exactly collide with another addressable alias or physical filename in that publication domain, publication refuses. After a Store MAP has been validly published, the later appearance, disappearance, rename, or copying-in of an unrelated Suitcase file does not retroactively make that immutable MAP structurally invalid or ineligible. A later textual reference can still become ambiguous at resolution time under W002-STOR-021; that ambiguity causes the later operation to refuse rather than changing the historical MAP's validity. The store_alias names the Store as a whole and is separate from the field/COL alias namespace. Alias mutation occurs through a governed Work Order, not through an editable GUI field. Exact cross-Store Store-alias uniqueness and future selection-by-Store-alias syntax remain outside this freeze.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STOR-021,Work Order resolution binds one exact Store MAP and physical targets,W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A saved Work Order may refer to governed materialized columns by exact physical filename or by a unique COL alias from one selected Store MAP. The canonical explicit Store-MAP selector is MAP ""<exact Store MAP filename>"" under W002-STOR-019.3 and W002-WKO-012.3. If that clause is present and valid, exactly that Store snapshot is used. Otherwise Data Sculptor applies the Store-aware source-qualified selection rule in W002-STOR-019.2. All textual physical-filename and COL-alias comparisons in this resolution step use exact Unicode scalar-value sequence equality under PB-STOR-010: no case folding, Unicode normalization, trimming, locale equivalence, or filesystem enumeration heuristic is permitted. Resolution is bounded to the selected Store snapshot and the physical targets/aliases that are addressable through that snapshot. If the supplied text has no exact target, resolution refuses. If it has more than one exact possible target in that domain—for example because a currently visible physical filename and a current alias are both exact matches—resolution also refuses. Data Sculptor must not choose filename over alias, alias over filename, first-found entry, directory order, modified time, UUID, or any other tie-break heuristic. Before execution, Data Sculptor must record the exact physical Store MAP identity when one is used, bind the run to its exact rid_filename , and resolve aliases deterministically to physical COL artifacts. The selected Store MAP must remain fixed for the run even if a newer MAP is created during that same run. This protects Store/selection continuity but does not by itself claim that bytes stored under an analyst-owned source filename are cryptographically identical across different runs.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STOR-022,Each successful Suitcase validation publishes one retained governed CER HTML certificate,W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A selected directory becomes a validated Suitcase only when Data Sculptor successfully creates, completely writes, and closes one governed CER HTML Suitcase Validation Certificate in that directory. The certificate itself is the validation artifact and remains visible in the flat Suitcase as durable evidence. No validation-only delete or rename is required. Failure to create, completely write, or close the certificate means the directory has not passed Suitcase validation and analytical execution remains locked. F-14 CER exception: the CER is deliberately not staged as SCR . Suitcase validation is specifically the direct create/write/close test of the final canonical CER identity in the selected directory. Inserting an SCR-to-CER rename would test a different publication path and is therefore forbidden for this validation step. A successful CER does not pre-certify later SCR-to-final renames for other artifact classes. F-24 CER lifecycle: every successful explicit Suitcase selection and validation publishes exactly one fresh immutable CER with a new governed UTC+UUID identity. Data Sculptor must not satisfy a new validation event by reusing an earlier CER. Every prior valid CER remains a standalone historical artifact under its original governed filename and exact bytes. WASM-002 performs no automatic CER deletion, replacement, compaction, or CER-history ZIP packaging. Historical CERs are not housekeeping candidates merely because a newer CER exists. Any later archival or packaging capability must be separately governed and explicitly invoked; it is not part of the WASM-002 validation lifecycle.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STOR-022.1,Suitcase Validation Certificate physical identity and longest-name path gate,W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The exact certificate filename is __DS__CER__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.html , using the canonical UTC millisecond token and canonical lowercase hyphenated UUID v4. Data Sculptor chooses the filename; the analyst does not supply or edit it. The CER create/write/close test begins only after the browser host has satisfied the required user-selected writable-directory capability in W002-PLAT-001. A browser that cannot expose that capability produces a host-capability refusal before folder validation; that condition is not evidence that any particular directory is unwritable or filename-incompatible. WASM-002 path/filename acceptance must derive the maximum filename length from every governed final-artifact filename form and every governed SCR staging form that this build can actually emit. Under the current contract, the maximum is 73 ASCII bytes/characters : the governed .html CER/HLP final forms and an SCR candidate reserved for a .html final artifact have that length. The canonical CER filename therefore exercises the current maximum emitted filename length during the create/write/close validation test. On a supported host, successful create/write/close of this canonical governed HTML filename is the WASM-002 folder filename/path compatibility test for the current emitted-name maximum. Data Sculptor does not maintain a product-level table of operating-system numeric path maxima and must not truncate, abbreviate, hash-shorten, or otherwise mutate a governed filename to fit a host path limitation. If the certificate cannot be created under its canonical name after a directory has actually been selected through the supported-host contract, the selected directory does not pass validation. If a future PRD revision introduces an emitted final or staging filename longer than the current CER/HLP/SCR-HTML maximum, acceptance must detect that change and explicitly exercise the new maximum before the build may rely on this path-compatibility claim.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STOR-022.2,Suitcase Validation Certificate semantic content,W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The HTML certificate uses the canonical built-in Data Sculptor presentation and must visibly contain, at minimum: SUITCASE VALIDATION CERTIFICATE RESULT: PASS SUITCASE: . UTC: <canonical certificate UTC> UUID: <certificate UUID> ARTIFACT: <full governed certificate filename> TEST: CREATE_WRITE_CLOSE It must state that Data Sculptor successfully created, completely wrote, and closed this governed HTML certificate in the selected Suitcase. It must state that this establishes that the selected directory was writable by Data Sculptor at the recorded UTC and accepted the governed artifact filename used for the certificate. It must also state that the certificate does not certify available disk capacity, guarantee success of future analytical operations, or certify later SCR -to-final-class publication/rename operations. The semantic record uses SUITCASE: . and must not persist an absolute machine-specific path merely to prove validation.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STOR-022.3,Suitcase Validation Certificate uses the canonical built-in presentation in WASM-002,W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The certificate is a human-facing HTML CER artifact and uses the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation in WASM-002. Presentation must never change RESULT , SUITCASE , UTC, UUID, artifact identity, TEST , validation meaning, or limitation facts. Configurable Brand Manifest application to CER artifacts is deferred to V1-BACKLOG / a future build and is not required for WASM-002 Suitcase validation.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STOR-023,Non-Store governed artifacts use class-specific all-or-refuse publication profiles,W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Except for the deliberate CER Suitcase-validation path below, WASM-002 does not place a newly generated durable artifact into its final semantic class merely because candidate bytes exist. The complete candidate is first written under the governed SCR identity defined by W002-STOR-023.1, closed, reopened, and validated against the target class contract. Only a candidate that passes its class-specific publication predicate may be renamed into the intended final class. A final-class filename therefore records successful class publication, not broader authority where a separate MAP/registry relationship governs authority. F-33 reserved-class boundary: DGN , RCV , BRD , and LCK are registered but not emitted by WASM-002, so they do not appear as publication profiles in this table and have no WASM-002 producer here. Final class Final serialization / identity Publication predicate Authority boundary WKO __DS__WKO__<UTC>__<UUID>.txt The complete candidate obeys the saved-Work-Order lifecycle and parses completely under exactly one WASM-002 executable operation grammar with the required SUITCASE: . , exactly one non-whitespace WORK ORDER AS alias, and the governed lexical/comment rules. Applicable save-time alias/registry gates must also pass before the save transaction may commit. Promotion proves a valid immutable WKO artifact. Alias-registry authority is not committed until the complete successor WKO MAP is successfully published under W002-STOR-018.3. RCP __DS__RCP__<UTC>__<UUID>.txt The complete candidate validates against W002-RCP-005 through W002-RCP-008: exact deterministic TXT serialization, common envelope, applicable operation-specific key table, governed absence semantics, and created-artifact tail. Publication creates durable run evidence only. It does not retroactively create or change analytical state. HLP __DS__HLP__<UTC>__<UUID>.html The complete self-contained HTML satisfies the HLP disclosure, presentation, provenance, embedded-JSON, lineage and semantic-parity rules in W002-HELP-009 and related Help requirements. Publication creates durable Help/support evidence. It does not override the underlying diagnostic event or analytical state. CVT __DS__CVT__<UTC>__<UUID>.csv The bounded Windows-1252 conversion completes, the original analyst-owned source remains unchanged, the converted bytes pass the governed strict UTF-8 requirement, and the candidate closes/reopens successfully. Structural CSV interpretation remains a later certification/materialization concern. The published exact CVT filename is a new immutable governed source identity for later routing under W002-CONV-004. INV __DS__INV__<UTC>__<UUID>.txt The complete inventory scan has established the governed entry set and the candidate validates the deterministic INV serialization, count, metadata availability and ordering rules. Publication creates an immutable inventory snapshot; it is evidence/orientation, not Store authority. CAT __DS__CAT__<UTC>__<UUID>.csv The authoritative MAP discovery/evaluation pass has completed and the candidate validates the exact five-column CAT schema, row count, row ordering and deterministic CSV rules. Publication creates an immutable collection-level orientation snapshot. MAP remains authoritative for each Store. CER __DS__CER__<UTC>__<UUID>.html Deliberate exception: Suitcase validation directly creates, completely writes and successfully closes the final CER identity under W002-STOR-022 through W002-STOR-022.3. No SCR staging/rename is inserted into this test. The CER proves that canonical governed create/write/close succeeded in the selected directory at that recorded moment. It does not pre-certify later SCR-to-final publication. RID, COL, Store MAP and WKO MAP publication retain their specialized transaction/commit rules elsewhere in this PRD. W002-STOR-023 does not replace those state-publication contracts; W002-STOR-023.1 supplies the shared SCR candidate identity and retained-failure-evidence boundary they may reference.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STOR-023.1,SCR candidates preserve intended final identity; retained failure evidence remains non-authoritative,W002-STOR,W002-STOR,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The canonical candidate filename for a staged governed artifact is: __DS__SCR__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.<final-extension> The SCR candidate uses the exact UTC token, UUID and extension reserved for its intended final artifact. Successful publication changes only the three-letter semantic class token from SCR to the intended final class. For example, an RCP candidate __DS__SCR__20261006T190000000Z__<uuid>.txt may become __DS__RCP__20261006T190000000Z__<uuid>.txt only after the complete candidate has been closed, reopened and validated against the RCP publication predicate. The rename must not alter candidate bytes, UTC, UUID or extension. An SCR filename never by itself confers final-class validity, Store membership, registry authority, execution authority, or durable final-class evidence status. A retained SCR whose bytes happen to satisfy a target validator after an interrupted or refused transaction must not be auto-promoted, silently adopted, or treated as if the missing publication step occurred. F-33 retained-failure-evidence boundary: when a handled failure leaves one or more SCR candidates or other staged bytes that cannot be safely removed or restored, they must remain visible only as non-authoritative SCR evidence. WASM-002 does not publish an RCV recovery manifest. Retention must not complete or simulate the failed publication step, and the governed diagnostic/Help path must report the failure using only facts actually established. A retained or orphaned SCR remains non-authoritative even if its bytes later validate. Data Sculptor must not infer an intended final class solely from extension or byte content, must not rename or promote the SCR merely because it survives a later scan, and must not create a replacement RCV sidecar to manufacture attribution that the failed transaction did not durably preserve.",PARTIAL,PORTION_VERIFIED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,CP-011; W002-ENC-006,Measured evidence inherited from WASM-001b,W002-ENC,W002-ENC,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The following measurements are non-normative evidence explaining why WASM-002 begins with the ASCII-first inline algorithm. They are not WASM-002 acceptance results and must not be represented as such. EVID-W001B-UTF8-001 On the 7,250,808,204-byte Statistics Canada source, the Day 039 distribution experiment observed 659,103 non-ASCII bytes, approximately 0.009090063% of the file, across 329,551 non-ASCII runs/sequences; the maximum observed non-ASCII run was three bytes. EVID-W001B-UTF8-002 The Day 039 non-ASCII-only experiment submitted only 659,103 bytes to strict UTF-8 validation and completed in 12.664716 seconds at 545.998 MiB/s; it proved the source valid but still incurred 329,551 strict validation calls. EVID-W001B-UTF8-003 A 1 GiB A/B test showed that reducing validated bytes alone was not enough: the selective per-run strategy submitted 115,839 bytes in 57,919 strict calls but took 503.7536 ms, while the baseline submitted 113,246,208 bytes in 27 strict calls and took 411.3590 ms. UNRESOLVED SOURCE DAMAGE: preserved authoritative text continues “This supported removing per-run general-validator call overhead rather than merely shrinking” but the remainder has not been recovered. No missing words are inferred or supplied. EVID-W001B-UTF8-004 The final native inline scan certified all 7,250,808,204 bytes in 10.377870 seconds at 666.313 MiB/s, observed 329,551 non-ASCII sequences and 659,103 non-ASCII bytes, and made zero std::str::from_utf8 calls. EVID-W001B-UTF8-005 The same inline design was exercised in Microsoft Edge/WASM with 4 MiB transfers: the valid 7,250,808,204-byte source completed with 1,729 pushes, UTF8_VALID=true, and EOF_ALL_BYTES_VALID. That experimental run took 30.5858 seconds including file I/O, JS-to-WASM copy, and WASM validation. EVID-W001B-UTF8-006 A full-size deliberately invalid Edge/WASM fixture stopped early after 2,936,012,800 bytes and 700 pushes with UTF8_VALID=false and STOP_REASON=INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE rather than reading to EOF. W002-MAT-001.7,Stage 2 parses the header once and then continues directly into the data-record scan,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within the Stage 2 forward source scan, Data Sculptor must parse the complete first logical CSV record as the source header, construct ordered header metadata including exact decoded header text and 1-based source ordinal, resolve and validate all Work Order selectors/aliases, and then continue from the first data record without restarting the source. Header resolution therefore does not add a third whole-file pass. A header-only valid CSV yields a zero-row materialization; a source with no valid header record refuses. P3-09 no-header-record refusal: after Stage 1 has certified the source, if Stage 2 reaches end-of-source without establishing any logical CSV record from which a header could be parsed, materialization must refuse with CSV_REFUSAL_CONDITION: NO_HEADER_RECORD . This is the eighth governed Stage-2 structural CSV refusal token in the canonical oracle defined by W002-MAT-002.8. Its governed location facts are: CSV_SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET = exact source byte length; CSV_PHYSICAL_LINE: 1 ; CSV_LOGICAL_RECORD: 1 ; CSV_FIELD_ORDINAL: 1 . Therefore a zero-byte source reports offset 0 , and a source containing only the UTF-8 BOM bytes EF BB BF reports offset 3 . A first logical record that exists but is blank remains governed by the already-frozen BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD condition and must not be reclassified as NO_HEADER_RECORD . F-20 source-width boundary: the established header record may contain at most 16,384 physical source columns. Exactly 16,384 is valid; a header record containing 16,385 or more fields must refuse deterministically during header resolution before the first data record is consumed. The bound applies to the complete physical source width, not merely the requested KEEP set. Header processing must remain bounded. Exact decoded source-header text is authoritative source evidence and must be preserved for every selected/materialized column, but the implementation is not required to retain the complete decoded text of every unselected header after selector resolution when bounded metadata is sufficient.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-MAT-002.2,All selected columns are emitted from one forward data-record scan,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"After header/selector resolution, Stage 2 must traverse the source data records once regardless of whether the Work Order selects one column or many. W002-MAT-002.3,One 1-based logical row ordinal aligns every selected output,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The header is not a data row. The first accepted logical data record is row identity 1, the next is 2, and so on through N. The row counter advances exactly once per accepted logical CSV data record, not per physical line. W002-MAT-002.5,Multiple active COL outputs use bounded staging and explicit backpressure,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Each active materialized-column writer, or an equivalent shared multiplexed output structure, must have bounded staging capacity. The aggregate kernel-owned staging state for all active writers must remain inside the governed WASM memory budget and must not grow with source row count or total output size. If a required output writer cannot accept additional canonical bytes without exceeding its governed staging capacity, source consumption must pause while pending output is drained/written. When more than one writer requires service, drain priority follows resolved KEEP order. After sufficient space is available, parsing resumes from the same structural state. The exact tuned staging-buffer size is an implementation/benchmark constant rather than an analytical semantic constant; changing it must not change output bytes, row identity, selection results, or diagnostics for the same governed input. F-20 writer-resource bound: KEEP width and simultaneously active writable resources are distinct. The accepted build must declare a finite implementation bound on simultaneously active writable-output resources and retain acceptance evidence of both that configured bound and the observed peak. The engine may satisfy a wide selection by bounded shared/multiplexed staging or a Data-Sculptor-owned spool followed by bounded finalization passes, but it must not require one simultaneously open writer per selected column. Changing the writer-resource bound must not change final bytes, row order, selection identity, aliases, Receipts, or diagnostics for the same governed input.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-002.6,Partial output sets are never published as a successful materialization,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"All requested materialized-column outputs begin as visible governed SCR candidates, not COL artifacts. On first materialization of a new Store, the automatically generated RID likewise begins as a governed SCR candidate. Before any new RID/COL SCR candidate is opened, Data Sculptor establishes one publication-transaction UTC under PB-STOR-013/PB-STOR-014 and allocates a distinct artifact-specific UUID for each new candidate. Each candidate filename therefore already carries the exact UTC, UUID, and final extension intended for that RID or COL identity. A materialization transaction may begin promotion only when every required RID/COL candidate reaches EOF successfully, all selected outputs reconcile to the same accepted data-row count N, and all required candidate finalization/validation succeeds. F-04 existing-Store cardinality gate: when materialization targets an existing VALID Store, after Stage 2 establishes the complete candidate logical data-row count N and before any requested COL candidate is promoted, Data Sculptor must read the expected N from the already-valid inherited RID header and compare the two values. If candidate N equals RID-header N , the cardinality gate passes and ordinary publication may continue. If candidate N differs, the Run must refuse before any SCR -to- COL promotion and before successor-MAP publication. The inherited RID, current MAP, and existing COL artifacts remain unchanged, and the existing Store remains VALID. Equal N proves cardinality compatibility only; it does not prove source-byte continuity, row-semantic identity, or permission for a different SOURCE to enter the lineage. Exact SOURCE/Store compatibility rules are prior gates. For a new Store, Data Sculptor promotes the validated RID candidate first by host rename that changes only the class token from SCR to RID ; the candidate bytes, shared transaction UTC, RID-specific UUID, and extension remain unchanged. That successful SCR-to-RID promotion is the event that establishes RID_ACTION: CREATED and the published RID_FILENAME fact for the Run. Before that promotion succeeds, the Run has not created a governed RID even if a candidate identity has been allocated. For an existing Store, the inherited RID is reused unchanged and no RID candidate/promotion occurs. Once routing has selected and validated that exact inherited RID, that event establishes RID_ACTION: REUSED and the exact inherited RID_FILENAME ; later refusal does not erase the already-established reuse fact. After the required RID state is established, Data Sculptor promotes each requested COL candidate in deterministic resolved KEEP order by changing only the class token from SCR to COL ; each candidate's bytes, shared transaction UTC, COL-specific UUID, and extension remain unchanged. If RID or COL promotion fails, Data Sculptor must refuse the run and roll any newly promoted RID/COL names back out of their final namespaces where safely possible. Candidate or rollback bytes that cannot be safely restored or removed must be retained visibly as non-authoritative SCR failure evidence. The existence of an unreferenced RID- or COL-looking file after interruption does not by itself make that artifact committed Store state. After all required RID/COL promotions succeed, Data Sculptor allocates a MAP-specific UUID before opening the complete successor-MAP SCR candidate. That candidate uses the same publication-transaction UTC, the allocated MAP UUID, and the final .csv extension, and is constructed using the exact final RID/COL filenames. It is closed successfully, reopened, and validated completely while it remains SCR . Only then may the MAP candidate be promoted by changing only the class token from SCR to MAP ; its bytes, UTC, UUID, and extension remain unchanged. The successful SCR -to- MAP rename is the materialization commit point. Until that commit point, the prior valid MAP remains authoritative for an existing Store; for a new Store, no committed Store state exists yet. If MAP validation or MAP rename fails, Data Sculptor must refuse and roll the newly promoted RID/COL set back out of the final namespaces where safely possible; otherwise affected bytes remain attributable recovery evidence and are not committed Store membership. Governed Store membership/current state is established by a valid MAP binding, not by a final-class filename or timestamp equality alone. Revision BB preserves the Revision AY staging/promotion mechanics and Revision AZ shared transaction-UTC rule for newly published RID/COL/MAP artifacts. Selected-folder support for the canonical governed filename/path form is established by the Suitcase Validation Certificate under W002-STOR-022 through W002-STOR-022.3 rather than by a frozen numeric host path-length table. Operation-specific host rename or publication failure remains a governed refusal under this requirement and is not pre-certified by Suitcase validation. F-14 shared candidate grammar, reconciled by F-33: every RID/COL/MAP SCR candidate in this transaction follows W002-STOR-023.1: its SCR name already carries the UTC, UUID and extension intended for the final RID/COL/MAP identity, and successful promotion changes only the class token. Any retained SCR candidates after a handled publication/rollback failure remain visible non-authoritative failure evidence under W002-STOR-023.1 and are reported through the governed diagnostic/Help path; WASM-002 does not emit an RCV manifest. An orphaned SCR remains non-authoritative even if its bytes later validate.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-002.7,Successful materialization publishes one complete Store MAP,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A successful governed materialization that creates one or more COL artifacts must also publish exactly one new complete immutable Store MAP under W002-STOR-019 through W002-STOR-019.12. For a new Store, that MAP binds the automatically generated and promoted RID to the Store metadata and all newly materialized COL mappings. For an existing Store, it preserves the inherited RID binding and complete prior Store state while applying the successful materialization updates. All required RID/COL SCR candidates must complete and validate before promotion begins. On a new Store, RID promotion occurs first; on an existing Store, the inherited RID is reused unchanged. All requested COL promotions must then succeed before successor-MAP candidate construction begins. The complete successor MAP is written as SCR , closed, reopened, and fully validated before entering the MAP namespace. Its final host rename from SCR to the governed MAP filename occurs last and is the materialization commit point. The materialization run is not reported as successfully committed until that MAP rename succeeds. If MAP candidate validation or MAP rename fails after RID/COL promotion, the run must refuse and the newly promoted artifacts must be rolled back out of their final namespaces where safely possible. Any failure residue that cannot safely be removed or restored is governed by W002-STOR-023.1 and remains non-authoritative retained failure evidence; its survival must not be used to infer or manufacture attribution or to simulate the failed publication step. The prior valid MAP remains authoritative for an existing Store; no committed Store is established for a first materialization without a valid successor MAP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-002.8,Stage 2 enforces deterministic source-record shape,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The parsed header establishes the expected source field count. Every nonblank logical data record must contain exactly that many fields after CSV parsing. A nonblank ragged record with fewer or more fields must refuse rather than pad, truncate, or shift later values. An explicit empty field is valid data and preserves its ordinal. A bare blank logical data record occurring outside a quoted field must refuse and must not be silently skipped or converted into one empty field. A physical blank line inside a valid quoted multiline field is field content, not a blank record. F-06 canonical malformed-CSV refusal facts Every structural CSV refusal records these governed facts: REFUSAL_CONDITION
SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET
PHYSICAL_LINE
LOGICAL_RECORD
FIELD_ORDINAL SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET is the zero-based absolute byte offset from the first physical byte of the source file. A leading UTF-8 BOM, when present, occupies offsets 0–2 and therefore counts in subsequent absolute byte locations. PHYSICAL_LINE is one-based and equals one plus the number of LF bytes strictly before the governed refusal location. LF bytes inside quoted multiline fields still increment physical-line count. LOGICAL_RECORD is one-based CSV logical-record ordinal and includes the header as logical record 1. The first data record is therefore logical record 2. FIELD_ORDINAL is the one-based field position within that logical record. These facts describe the same first structural refusal regardless of permitted streaming-window size or boundary placement. Canonical structural refusal tokens The seven frozen F-06 malformed-CSV tokens are: UNEXPECTED_QUOTE_IN_UNQUOTED_FIELD
INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE
BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD
EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD
BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD
TOO_FEW_FIELDS
TOO_MANY_FIELDS P3-09 adds NO_HEADER_RECORD as the eighth governed Stage-2 structural CSV refusal token. Parser-library names, host exceptions, crate-specific error enums, or localized descriptions must not replace these governed tokens. Governed refusal location by condition Condition Governed refusal location UNEXPECTED_QUOTE_IN_UNQUOTED_FIELD Offset of the offending "" byte. INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE Offset of the first prohibited byte after the closing quote. BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD Offset of the CR byte itself. EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD One-past-end offset, equal to the physical source byte length. BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD First byte of the record terminator that proves the blank record: LF for LF termination; CR for CRLF termination. TOO_FEW_FIELDS First byte of the record terminator that closes the short record; at EOF, one-past-end offset equal to source byte length. TOO_MANY_FIELDS The comma delimiter that begins the first field beyond the expected header width. NO_HEADER_RECORD One-past-end offset equal to the exact physical source byte length, with physical line 1, logical record 1, and field ordinal 1, as frozen by W002-MAT-001.7. Field ordinal rules For TOO_FEW_FIELDS , FIELD_ORDINAL is the first missing field ordinal: expected-width position immediately after the last field actually present. For TOO_MANY_FIELDS , FIELD_ORDINAL is the first extra field ordinal: header-width + 1. For quote/CR/EOF structural conditions, FIELD_ORDINAL is the current field ordinal in which the malformed condition is established. For BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD , FIELD_ORDINAL is 1. For NO_HEADER_RECORD , FIELD_ORDINAL is 1. Bare CR scope A bare CR outside a quoted field is malformed CSV and refuses with BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD . CR inside a valid quoted field is ordinary field content. LF inside a valid quoted field is ordinary field content. CRLF inside a valid quoted field is ordinary field content. Outside quoted fields, CRLF is one accepted logical-record terminator and LF is one accepted logical-record terminator. Outside quoted fields, a CR not immediately followed by LF is malformed. EOF while quoted If EOF is reached while the parser remains inside an open quoted field, the source refuses with EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD . Data Sculptor must not synthesize a closing quote, truncate the field, reinterpret prior bytes as unquoted content, or otherwise repair the source. First-condition precedence Stage 2 evaluates structural CSV input in absolute source-byte order and reports the earliest refusal condition that becomes deterministically established. CSV grammar errors take precedence over later row-shape errors. BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD takes precedence over TOO_FEW_FIELDS for a physically blank logical record. BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD takes precedence over INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE when the post-quote offending byte is a CR that is not followed by LF. At EOF while still inside a quoted field, EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD takes precedence over field-count evaluation. No implementation may choose a different error merely because of parser buffering, window boundaries, library behavior, or host platform. Delimiter boundary Comma remains the only WASM-002 field delimiter. Automatic delimiter detection is outside the WASM-002 CSV contract. A file whose rows contain semicolons, tabs, or other non-comma separators may still be valid under the comma-only grammar as a one-column CSV. Data Sculptor must not invent a malformed-CSV refusal merely because another application would treat those bytes as delimiters. When a requested HEADER cannot be resolved, Help may explain that WASM-002 uses comma as the CSV delimiter and that semicolon/tab exports may therefore be interpreted as one field per row. Interaction with UTF-8 diagnostics This structural CSV refusal oracle applies only after the source has passed the applicable encoding-certification boundary. Invalid UTF-8 remains governed by the separately frozen UTF-8 diagnostic contract. Its zero-based absolute source-byte orientation is intentionally aligned with SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET so WASM-002 does not have competing byte-coordinate systems.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-002.9,Unselected field contents are not retained,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Stage 2 must parse every field sufficiently to preserve CSV structure, field count, row boundaries, and governed safety checks, but it must not retain complete contents for unselected fields after those bytes are no longer structurally needed. The engine must not materialize a complete source row, complete table, or complete unselected column in memory merely to emit selected columns. Selected-field content may use bounded accumulation required by the frozen field-size/output rules.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-002.10,Individual decoded CSV fields are limited to 16 MiB,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WASM-002 carries forward the established Data Sculptor field-buffer safety boundary: an individual CSV field may contain at most 16 MiB (16,777,216 bytes) of decoded UTF-8 field content. This is an engineering safety limit, not a semantic statement about CSV or an Excel cell limit. The limit must be enforced incrementally for header and data fields. The parser must not first accumulate an arbitrarily large field and then check it. If a field would exceed the limit, the run must refuse without truncating, repairing, discarding the remainder, or finalizing the candidate materialization. For an unselected field, Data Sculptor may count decoded field bytes without retaining the field value; the safety limit still applies so malformed unterminated fields cannot turn the structural scan into unbounded growth. F-20 operational column-name boundary: after an exact source header field is decoded, Data Sculptor measures its length in Unicode scalar values, not UTF-8 bytes or grapheme clusters. If the exact decoded source header contains at most 1,024 Unicode scalar values, its operational column name is that exact header text. If it contains more than 1,024 scalar values, the operational column name begins from the deterministic physical-ordinal fallback Column <LETTERS> , where the letters are the Excel-style 1-based source ordinal ( A through XFD for the WASM-002 width bound). This operational name is a bounded human-facing/default-alias construct; it does not replace or truncate the authoritative exact source header.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-002.11,Materialized COL artifacts use canonical one-column UTF-8 CSV serialization,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Each finalized materialized COL artifact is a one-column CSV. It begins with exactly one UTF-8 BOM ( EF BB BF ) and uses LF ( 0x0A ) as the record terminator on every supported host. The first logical record contains the exact decoded source header text for that physical source column; an alias assigned with AS lives in the governed MAP and does not rewrite the physical COL header. A deliberately empty source header is serialized as one explicit empty header field rather than as absence of a header record. Header and data fields use deterministic minimal CSV quoting: quote when the field contains comma, double quote, CR, or LF; double embedded double quotes; otherwise write the field without quotes. Embedded CR/LF that belong to a quoted field remain field content. For a one-column data record whose decoded value is the empty string, serialize the value explicitly as """" so the row cannot be confused with a bare blank logical record. For fixed source bytes and fixed governed semantics, changing input/output window boundaries must not change the finalized COL bytes. F-20 source-fidelity rule: the physical COL header record always serializes the exact decoded source header, even when that header exceeds the 1,024 -scalar operational-name boundary and the Store MAP/default alias therefore uses an operational fallback. The fallback name must never be substituted into the COL header record or into the MAP source_header field.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-003,Stage 2 processes the source through bounded reusable windows,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,Structural materialization must process the certified source through bounded reusable input windows compatible with browser/WASM memory constraints. Source size and row count must not require proportional WASM memory growth.,NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-003.1,"The 4 MiB WASM-001b window is a proven reference point, not a frozen production constant",W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The 4 MiB source window used successfully during the WASM-001b browser experiments is an evidence-backed starting/reference size. WASM-002 may tune the production input-window size using benchmark evidence, provided the governed memory budget and all window-invariance requirements remain satisfied.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-003.2,Changing source-window size or boundary placement must not change results,W002-MAT,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For the same certified source and Work Order, permitted changes in bounded Stage 2 input-window size or boundary placement must not change CSV interpretation, resolved headers/ordinals, accepted row count, row identity, aliases, canonical COL bytes, successor MAP contents apart from newly allocated physical identities/timestamps, or the first deterministic refusal condition. P3-09 window invariance: for a Stage-1-certified source containing no logical CSV record, every permitted Stage 2 window size and boundary placement must produce the same NO_HEADER_RECORD refusal and the same governed location tuple: source-byte offset equal to the exact source byte length, physical line 1, logical record 1, field ordinal 1. F-06 full refusal-oracle window invariance: for the same certified source bytes, changing any permitted Stage 2 input-window size or boundary placement must not change whether the source is accepted or refused; the first REFUSAL_CONDITION ; SOURCE_BYTE_OFFSET ; PHYSICAL_LINE ; LOGICAL_RECORD ; or FIELD_ORDINAL . W002-CONV-001,Conversion is a separate governed operation,W002-CONV,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Windows-1252-to-UTF-8 conversion is a distinct governed Work Order operation, separate from UTF-8 certification and separate from analytical materialization. The analyst must explicitly authorize it. The canonical WASM-002 form is: SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS ""Convert legacy source to UTF-8""
SOURCE ""legacy_source.csv""
CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 is the terminal operation clause. Exactly one SOURCE is permitted. The same WKO must not contain KEEP , MATERIALIZE , Store/RID/COL alias mutation, MAP , Inventory, repair, cataloging, Work Order composition, or another operation terminal clause. F-10 conversion entry precondition Before CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 may begin character transcoding, Data Sculptor must validate the complete bound source as strict UTF-8 under the same deterministic whole-source certification rules used elsewhere in WASM-002. If the complete source is already valid strict UTF-8, the conversion refuses as unnecessary and publishes no CVT . Only after complete strict UTF-8 validation reaches governed FAIL may Data Sculptor assess the same complete bound source against the frozen Windows-1252 compatibility mapping. Only a source that fails strict UTF-8 and passes the complete Windows-1252 compatibility assessment may proceed to conversion. A failed analytical Work Order, UTF-8 certification, or materialization never silently invokes this operation. The analyst must explicitly authorize the separate conversion WKO.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-CONV-002,Windows-1252 compatibility assessment,W002-CONV,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"After strict whole-source UTF-8 certification returns FAIL , the current analytical operation remains refused and Stage 2 must not start. As refusal handling, Data Sculptor performs one separate read-only Windows-1252 compatibility assessment from physical byte offset 0 of the same run-local bound source instance. The compatibility assessment scans the complete source sequentially under W002-CONV-002.1 through W002-CONV-002.5. It does not transcode, publish a CVT, modify the analyst-owned source, resume materialization, or claim that Windows-1252 is the historical encoding. Its sole governed result is whether the entire byte stream is mappable by the frozen WASM-002 Windows-1252 converter. If strict UTF-8 certification returned PASS , or did not reach a governed FAIL conclusion, this compatibility assessment is not run. F-10 conversion classification gate The conversion operation itself repeats/executes the complete classification gate on its bound source before transcoding: validate the complete source as strict UTF-8; if strict UTF-8 passes, refuse conversion as unnecessary; only after strict UTF-8 fails, scan the complete source against the frozen Windows-1252 mapping; if any source byte is undefined or unsupported by that mapping, refuse rather than guess; and begin transcoding only when strict UTF-8 has failed and the complete Windows-1252 compatibility assessment has succeeded. An undefined/unsupported Windows-1252 byte is therefore a pre-transcoding compatibility-assessment refusal . No CVT candidate may be represented as successfully converted from a source whose compatibility scan found an undefined byte. The compatibility assessment must not substitute U+FFFD , reinterpret an undefined Windows-1252 byte as ISO-8859-1, or use permissive host/library decoder behavior to make an incompatible source convertible.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-CONV-002.1,Compatibility means that the supported deterministic converter can map the observed source bytes under the frozen Windows-1252 rules.,W002-CONV,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Compatibility means that every physical source byte can be mapped deterministically by the complete normative WASM-002 Windows-1252 mapping in W002-CONV-002.4 . Successful EOF produces the governed outcome COMPATIBLE . No statistical detector, locale rule, browser guess, replacement character, ISO-8859-1 substitution, best-effort decoder, or PRODUCT-scoped glossary text participates as normative authority in this determination.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-CONV-002.2,Compatibility must not be described as proof that Windows-1252 was historically or authoritatively the file's original encoding.,W002-CONV,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"COMPATIBLE means only that the complete byte stream is convertible under Data Sculptor's frozen Windows-1252 mapping. It must not be described as proof that Windows-1252 was historically, authoritatively, or intentionally the source file's original encoding.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-CONV-002.3,Bytes undefined by the frozen Windows-1252 mapping must cause the compatibility assessment or conversion task to refuse rather than guess.,W002-CONV,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"If the compatibility pass encounters a byte that W002-CONV-002.4 defines as undefined, the assessment stops at the first such byte and returns INCOMPATIBLE . Data Sculptor must not substitute a replacement character, reinterpret the byte under another code page, or continue as though conversion were safe. A later explicit conversion Work Order must apply the same complete WASM-002 mapping and the same refusal rule.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-CONV-002.4,Complete normative WASM-002 Windows-1252 byte mapping,W002-CONV,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"This requirement is the complete normative Windows-1252 mapping authority for WASM-002 . It covers all 256 possible byte values. No PRODUCT-scoped glossary entry or host/library decoder is required to interpret compatibility or conversion. 0x00–0x7F Every byte 0x00 through 0x7F maps one-to-one to Unicode U+0000 through U+007F . 0x80–0x9F Byte Windows-1252 mapping Unicode 0x80 EURO SIGN U+20AC 0x81 UNDEFINED — 0x82 SINGLE LOW-9 QUOTATION MARK U+201A 0x83 LATIN SMALL LETTER F WITH HOOK U+0192 0x84 DOUBLE LOW-9 QUOTATION MARK U+201E 0x85 HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS U+2026 0x86 DAGGER U+2020 0x87 DOUBLE DAGGER U+2021 0x88 MODIFIER LETTER CIRCUMFLEX ACCENT U+02C6 0x89 PER MILLE SIGN U+2030 0x8A LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S WITH CARON U+0160 0x8B SINGLE LEFT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK U+2039 0x8C LATIN CAPITAL LIGATURE OE U+0152 0x8D UNDEFINED — 0x8E LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Z WITH CARON U+017D 0x8F UNDEFINED — 0x90 UNDEFINED — 0x91 LEFT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK U+2018 0x92 RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK U+2019 0x93 LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK U+201C 0x94 RIGHT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK U+201D 0x95 BULLET U+2022 0x96 EN DASH U+2013 0x97 EM DASH U+2014 0x98 SMALL TILDE U+02DC 0x99 TRADE MARK SIGN U+2122 0x9A LATIN SMALL LETTER S WITH CARON U+0161 0x9B SINGLE RIGHT-POINTING ANGLE QUOTATION MARK U+203A 0x9C LATIN SMALL LIGATURE OE U+0153 0x9D UNDEFINED — 0x9E LATIN SMALL LETTER Z WITH CARON U+017E 0x9F LATIN CAPITAL LETTER Y WITH DIAERESIS U+0178 0xA0–0xFF Every byte 0xA0 through 0xFF maps one-to-one to Unicode U+00A0 through U+00FF . Undefined-byte rule The only undefined byte values in this frozen WASM-002 mapping are exactly 0x81 , 0x8D , 0x8F , 0x90 , and 0x9D . Encountering any one of them makes the complete compatibility assessment INCOMPATIBLE at the first such byte and causes an explicitly run conversion Work Order to refuse before transcoding rather than guess. These three ranges plus the 32-position table above exhaust the byte domain 0x00–0xFF . No unlisted byte value exists.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-CONV-002.5,The compatibility check must itself be bounded and deterministic.,W002-CONV,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The compatibility check is one bounded-memory deterministic sequential pass from physical source byte offset 0 to EOF unless the first undefined Windows-1252 byte is encountered earlier. On INCOMPATIBLE , WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET is the zero-based absolute physical source-byte offset of the first undefined byte. On COMPATIBLE , that offset is NOT_APPLICABLE . If the assessment begins but an independent read/host failure prevents a governed compatibility conclusion, the outcome is NOT_AVAILABLE and the first-undefined-byte offset is NOT_AVAILABLE . The assessment itself publishes no converted output.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-CONV-004,Canonical conversion output,W002-CONV,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A successful Windows-1252 conversion task must produce canonical UTF-8 output suitable for later submission to the normal UTF-8 certification and materialization path. P3-08 lineage consequence: the successful conversion output is a new immutable governed CVT artifact with its own exact physical filename. That CVT filename is the source identity used by later Store routing. A later conversion, including one made from a refreshed analyst-owned legacy source with the same original filename, publishes a different CVT and therefore does not refresh, replace, or continue an earlier CVT-backed Store lineage merely by name association. On first materialization, each distinct CVT begins a new Store lineage unless that exact CVT filename already routes to an existing lineage under the normal Store rules. F-14 CVT identity and publication: the final converted-source filename is exactly __DS__CVT__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv . Conversion writes first to the corresponding W002-STOR-023.1 SCR identity with the same UTC, UUID and .csv extension. Only after bounded conversion completes, the candidate closes/reopens successfully, and the converted bytes satisfy the governed strict UTF-8 requirement may the class token be renamed to CVT . CSV structural interpretation remains governed by the later normal certification/materialization path; CVT publication does not assert that the converted source is structurally valid CSV. F-10 conversion semantics — encoding conversion only The conversion operation performs deterministic character transcoding only. It does not parse, repair, normalize, or reinterpret CSV structure. Commas remain commas. Double quotes remain double quotes. Ordinary ASCII bytes retain the same byte value. LF remains LF. CR remains CR. CRLF remains CRLF. Embedded CR/LF bytes are preserved in place; the converter does not decide whether they are record terminators or field content. Canonical UTF-8 output therefore means deterministic UTF-8 encoding of the accepted source characters, not normalization of line endings, quoting, delimiters, records, headers, or fields. F-10 BOM rule The published CVT is UTF-8 without a BOM ; Data Sculptor does not prepend EF BB BF . If the source failed strict UTF-8 classification, a leading source byte sequence EF BB BF is not blindly stripped as though it were a UTF-8 BOM. Under the Windows-1252 conversion path those source bytes are source data and are mapped according to the frozen Windows-1252 mapping. BOM interpretation remains subordinate to encoding classification rather than acting as a blind prefix-removal rule.",PARTIAL,PORTION_VERIFIED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,CP-010; CP-011,"CP010 T-ACCEPTED, GIT BANKED — lexical CVT candidate only; complete requirement remains open; CP011 T-ACCEPTED, GIT BANKED — CVT-to-SCR lexical staging-name pairing only; complete conversion requirement remains open",b7c515faa9bd000369d7656e09437310261290ae; e84ae5baeee05f9d5d30284c65b86eebba3c0f6a,"Evidence/CP-010/CP010_Scope_Lock.txt; Evidence/CP-010/CP010_RED_Test_Output_CMD_Corrected.txt; Evidence/CP-010/CP010_GREEN_Test_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-010/CP010_Post_Format_Regression_Test_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-010/CP010_WASM_Build_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-010/CP010_Post_Format_Check_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-010/CP010_Hash_Inventory_Verification.txt; Evidence/CP-010/CP010_Supplementary_Hash_Verification.txt; Evidence/CP-010/CP010_Closing_Git_Review.txt; CP010_Git_Banking_Output.txt (post-commit; separately archived); Evidence/CP-011/CP011_Scope_Lock.txt; Evidence/CP-011/CP011_RED_Test_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-011/CP011_GREEN_Test_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-011/CP011_Post_Format_Regression_Test_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-011/CP011_Rustfmt_Recheck_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-011/CP011_Post_Format_WASM_Build_Output.txt; Evidence/CP-011/CP011_Hash_Inventory_Verification.txt; Evidence/CP-011/CP011_Supplementary_Hash_Verification.txt; Evidence/CP-011/CP011_Closing_Git_Review.txt; CP011_Git_Banking_Output.txt (post-commit, separately preserved)","CP010 Day066 first-touches ONLY the F-14 canonical final CVT output filename grammar subconstraint: is_governed_cvt_source_filename_candidate(&str)->bool recognizes exact canonical __DS__CVT__<UTC>__<UUIDv4>.csv lexical form by reusing existing envelope validation. W002-HELP-001,Canonical diagnostic truth,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every governed user-visible failure or warning produced by WASM-002 must originate as a canonical diagnostic event. W002-HELP-001.1,Canonical diagnostic IDs use the frozen DS-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> grammar,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every canonical diagnostic event must carry one stable identifier using the exact form DS-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> . DOMAIN is exactly three uppercase ASCII letters A through Z. NNN is exactly three decimal digits, zero-padded, in the range 001 through 999 . Examples include DS-ENC-001 , DS-WKO-001 , DS-STO-001 , DS-MAT-001 , and DS-HLP-001 . A diagnostic ID is permanent after allocation and must never be reused for a different diagnostic meaning. Severity, host, build/release, source filename, path, UUID, byte offset, row/column number, count, timestamp, occurrence ID, and other run-specific facts must not be encoded into the diagnostic ID; those values belong in structured diagnostic fields. The identifier is the canonical lookup key used by the Help message catalog. Day 060 H-04 pre-freeze identifier normalization: the Windows-1252 compatibility suggestion diagnostic is DS-CNV-001 . It follows the same exact three-letter DOMAIN grammar as every other diagnostic ID. No four-letter DOMAIN exception exists in the current WASM-002 contract. Any pre-H-04 draft spelling of this diagnostic is superseded and is not valid build-registry input.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-HELP-001.3,Diagnostic phase uses a stable uppercase token,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every canonical diagnostic event must identify the governed operation or phase using an uppercase ASCII snake-case token matching [A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:_[A-Z0-9]+)* . Examples include WORK_ORDER_VALIDATION , SOURCE_CERTIFICATION , MATERIALIZATION , STORE_PUBLICATION , and HELP_REPORT . These examples do not constitute a closed global phase list; the fixed phase for each allocated diagnostic is declared by that diagnostic's registry entry.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-001.4,Structured diagnostic facts are declared per diagnostic,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The canonical event carries diagnostic-specific evidence in a structured facts object. Fact keys use lowercase ASCII snake case matching [a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:_[a-z0-9]+)* . Each diagnostic registry entry declares disjoint required_facts and optional_facts sets. Every required fact must be present when that diagnostic is emitted. An optional fact key may be omitted when that fact is not emitted for the event, but omission itself has no governed absence-state meaning : it must not be interpreted as NONE , NOT_RUN , NOT_AVAILABLE , NOT_APPLICABLE , false , zero, or an empty string. An emitted fact key that is not declared for that diagnostic is invalid. For structured JSON diagnostic facts, an established ordinary value retains its native JSON type. When a present diagnostic fact must express one of the shared governed absence states, its value is the exact JSON string ""NONE"" , ""NOT_RUN"" , ""NOT_AVAILABLE"" , or ""NOT_APPLICABLE"" , with the meaning frozen by F-18. JSON null is not a generic encoding for diagnostic-fact absence; it is permitted only where a specific JSON schema explicitly declares a nullable field and defines what that null means, as W002-HELP-009 does for HLP lineage. A required diagnostic fact may not be silently omitted, defaulted, converted to null , guessed, or replaced by a Help-layer value. If Data Sculptor attempts to establish a registered diagnostic but cannot produce one or more facts declared required for that diagnostic, the intended diagnostic is not emitted . Instead the engine emits DS-HLP-001 under W002-HELP-001.8. The replacement event records the intended diagnostic ID and the complete sorted set of missing required fact names. No partially populated copy of the intended diagnostic may be presented beside it. This fail-closed substitution is a diagnostic-contract integrity rule, not a presentation fallback. It preserves the F-17 boundary that diagnostics own facts and Help renders only complete governed diagnostic truth.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-001.5,Execution behavior is explicitly CONTINUE or REFUSE,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every canonical diagnostic event must carry exactly one execution-behavior token: CONTINUE or REFUSE . This field is the governed continue/refuse decision for the event. Help wording, severity, UI color, or presentation must not independently weaken, strengthen, or reinterpret it.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-001.6,Safe next action uses a stable token rather than Help prose,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every canonical diagnostic event must carry a next_action token using uppercase ASCII snake case matching [A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:_[A-Z0-9]+)* . NONE is the canonical value when no safe governed next action applies. The token expresses stable machine-readable intent; Casual, Office Speak, and Technical wording for that action belongs to the Help layer. Run-specific values such as timestamps, paths, UUIDs, byte offsets, filenames, counts, or occurrence IDs remain structured facts and do not change the diagnostic identity or fixed next-action meaning. Damaged-Store guidance is part of the safe-next-action contract. When ordinary materialization refuses because exact source routing identifies an INVALID Store lineage, or a DEGRADED lineage whose every mapped COL is broken and therefore cannot be reduced to a non-empty successor by REPAIR MAP , the selected Help voice must preserve the same frozen choices and consequences rather than inventing a recovery operation. The explanation must identify the blocked lineage/current MAP and distinguish: external restoration under the original governed physical filename followed by the required governed validation tier; source rename to deliberately begin a separate new Store lineage; and analyst retirement of the damaged lineage by moving all of that lineage's Store MAPs out of the active Suitcase root. For retirement, Help must warn that moving only the latest MAP can expose an older structurally valid MAP as current. Help must not claim that matching the original filename proves historical byte identity, and must not describe any of these analyst filesystem actions as Data Sculptor-authored repair, deletion, RID regeneration, or silent lineage replacement. P3-07 malformed-MAP routing guard: when ordinary materialization refuses because no routable Store lineage can be established while one or more structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifacts are present in the active Suitcase, Help must identify the malformed MAP artifact or artifacts and state that new-Store/RID creation was blocked to prevent a silent lineage fork. Help must not describe the missing structurally valid MAP as proof that the prior Store never existed, and must not invent a Data Sculptor repair or replacement operation for this condition. P3-10 delimiter-hint clarification: when Stage 2 refuses with INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE and the offending byte is semicolon ( 0x3B ) or horizontal TAB ( 0x09 ), Help may include the governed delimiter-mismatch hint even though the refusal occurred before header-delimiter resolution. The hint is explanatory only: it must not change the canonical refusal condition, location facts, behavior, or safe-action boundary. F-16 conversion-suggestion boundary: strict UTF-8 refusal diagnostic DS-ENC-001 has fixed next_action: NONE . UTF-8 failure alone does not establish that any converter is safe. Only the separate compatibility diagnostic DS-CNV-001 , emitted after the complete governed Windows-1252 compatibility assessment returns COMPATIBLE , may carry next_action: RUN_WINDOWS_1252_CONVERSION . That token identifies a safe separately authorized option; it never resumes or rewrites the refused analytical Work Order. Day 060 H-12 damaged-lineage diagnostic binding ordinary MATERIALIZE refusal for a routed INVALID Store uses DS-MAT-014 and its declared facts; ordinary MATERIALIZE refusal for a DEGRADED Store whose every mapped COL is broken uses DS-MAT-015 and its declared facts; the no-routable-lineage / malformed-Store-MAP guard uses DS-MAT-016 and its declared facts. These specialized allocations are what permit closed-world Help to identify the blocked lineage/current MAP or malformed MAP artifacts without adding unrelated facts to the ordinary DS-MAT-010 validation diagnostic. Day 060 H-26 / BM-09 ordinary DEGRADED routing binding. When ordinary MATERIALIZE exact-source routing identifies a DEGRADED Store whose RID is valid and at least one mapped non-RID COL remains valid, the refusal uses DS-MAT-017 . Its fixed next_action is RUN_REPAIR_MAP because REPAIR MAP is the safe governed Store mutation for this repairable DEGRADED state. Help must use the diagnostic's declared current_map_filename as the exact MAP identity the analyst must name in the separate governed REPAIR MAP Work Order. The token does not run repair automatically and does not mutate the refused MATERIALIZE Work Order.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-001.7,"The governed engine emits the diagnostic semantic core, not voice-authored prose",W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The shared Rust/WASM diagnostic path must provide the canonical semantic core required by Help: diagnostic_id , severity , phase , behavior , facts , and next_action . The fixed values and permitted fact-key sets for an allocated diagnostic are governed by diagnostics.json . Casual, Office Speak, and Technical prose belongs to the Help rendering layer rather than being duplicated as authored message sets inside the governed engine. Host/build/occurrence metadata may be carried by surrounding governed execution evidence, but it must not redefine the diagnostic semantic core. F-16 closed-world Help rule: Help may recommend the WASM-002 Windows-1252 conversion Work Order only when the governed engine emitted DS-CNV-001 . Help must not infer compatibility from DS-ENC-001 , byte appearance, file extension, locale, browser behavior, heuristic encoding detection, or prose outside the diagnostic facts.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-001.8,diagnostics.json is the canonical WASM-002 diagnostic registry build resource,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The human-inspectable development/build source for the WASM-002 diagnostic registry is exactly diagnostics.json , encoded as UTF-8 without BOM. It is Data Sculptor product/build content, not a Suitcase artifact; it must not use the __DS__ namespace, consume an artifact-class token, or be copied into an analyst's Suitcase merely because Data Sculptor runs. The top-level JSON object has exactly two fields: registry_version and diagnostics . registry_version is the string ""1"" . diagnostics is an array written in ascending UTF-8 byte order of diagnostic_id . Each diagnostic entry has exactly seven fields: diagnostic_id , severity , phase , behavior , next_action , required_facts , and optional_facts . Diagnostic IDs must be unique and satisfy W002-HELP-001.1. Severity, phase, behavior, and next-action values must satisfy W002-HELP-001.2 through W002-HELP-001.6. required_facts and optional_facts are arrays of canonical fact-key strings sorted in ascending UTF-8 byte order; keys must be unique within each array and the two arrays must be disjoint. {
  ""registry_version"": ""1"",
  ""diagnostics"": [
    {
      ""diagnostic_id"": ""DS-CNV-001"",
      ""severity"": ""INFO"",
      ""phase"": ""SOURCE_CERTIFICATION"",
      ""behavior"": ""CONTINUE"",
      ""next_action"": ""RUN_WINDOWS_1252_CONVERSION"",
      ""required_facts"": [""source_filename"", ""windows_1252_compatibility_outcome""],
      ""optional_facts"": []
    },
    {
      ""diagnostic_id"": ""DS-ENC-001"",
      ""severity"": ""ERROR"",
      ""phase"": ""SOURCE_CERTIFICATION"",
      ""behavior"": ""REFUSE"",
      ""next_action"": ""NONE"",
      ""required_facts"": [""first_invalid_byte_offset"", ""source_filename"", ""stop_reason""],
      ""optional_facts"": [""analytical_outputs_published"", ""materialization_started"", ""source_modified_by_data_sculptor"", ""store_state_committed""]
    },
    {
      ""diagnostic_id"": ""DS-HLP-001"",
      ""severity"": ""ERROR"",
      ""phase"": ""DIAGNOSTIC_ASSEMBLY"",
      ""behavior"": ""REFUSE"",
      ""next_action"": ""NONE"",
      ""required_facts"": [""intended_diagnostic_id"", ""missing_required_facts""],
      ""optional_facts"": []
    }
  ]
} The PRD does not need to enumerate every allocated WASM-002 diagnostic row. The complete registry delivered with the build is retained acceptance evidence. A diagnostic ID becomes permanent once allocated and must not later be reused for a different meaning. Build validation must fail on malformed JSON; extra/missing entry fields; duplicate or noncanonical diagnostic IDs; invalid fixed tokens; unsorted, duplicate, overlapping, or invalid fact-key declarations; engine diagnostic definitions whose fixed semantics disagree with the registry; engine diagnostic definitions absent from the registry; Help-catalog IDs absent from the registry; or Help placeholders that name facts not declared as required or optional by the matching diagnostic. F-07 DS-ENC-001 fact mapping: the canonical lower-case diagnostic facts for strict UTF-8 refusal are first_invalid_byte_offset , source_filename , and stop_reason . For this diagnostic, stop_reason is exactly INVALID_UTF8_SEQUENCE . The generic fact name byte_offset is retired for this UTF-8 refusal diagnostic. P2-03 clock-order diagnostic facts: whichever stable WASM-002 Diagnostic ID is allocated to refusal because a successor Store MAP or WKO MAP cannot satisfy the strict monotonic UTC publication guard must declare these exact lower-case required facts in its diagnostic-registry entry: map_profile , observed_host_utc , predecessor_map_filename , and predecessor_utc . map_profile has exactly two permitted values: STORE for a Store-MAP chronology guard and WKO for a Work-Order-registry-MAP chronology guard. These facts identify both the governed MAP profile, the blocking predecessor artifact, and the truthful clock observation that caused refusal. F-16 DS-CNV-001 allocation: DS-CNV-001 is emitted only when the complete read-only compatibility assessment under W002-CONV-002 through W002-CONV-002.5 reaches EOF with outcome COMPATIBLE . Its required fact windows_1252_compatibility_outcome is therefore exactly the JSON string ""COMPATIBLE"" . behavior: CONTINUE means this informational diagnostic introduces no additional refusal; it does not reverse the already-established DS-ENC-001 refusal or resume Stage 2. F-17 DS-HLP-001 allocation: DS-HLP-001 is the canonical fail-safe event when the engine cannot satisfy the complete required-fact contract of an intended registered diagnostic. intended_diagnostic_id is the exact canonical ID that was being assembled. missing_required_facts is a JSON array of every missing required fact-key string, sorted in ascending UTF-8 byte order with no duplicates. The intended diagnostic is suppressed rather than emitted incompletely. DS-HLP-001 always refuses and has next_action: NONE . F-22 QA-independence boundary: diagnostics.json is authoritative for the fixed semantic contract of an allocated Diagnostic ID — its ID, severity, phase, behavior, next action, and permitted required/optional fact keys — but the implementation-delivered registry is not, by itself, an independent oracle proving that every arbitrary runtime condition was mapped to the correct Diagnostic ID. WASM-002 does not require a second QA-owned registry duplicating every implementation allocation. Where this PRD independently freezes a condition-to-diagnostic mapping or exact required facts — including the named DS-ENC-001 , DS-CNV-001 , and DS-HLP-001 contracts and other explicitly pinned diagnostic facts — that PRD text remains normative and acceptance must test the mapping independently of the implementation registry. For allocations not independently pinned by the PRD, WASM-002 accepts the validated build registry as the build allocation while retaining all registry-shape, permanence, semantic-agreement, fact-discipline, and Help cross-validation gates. This is an explicit accepted QA-scope risk, not a claim of independent condition-to-ID verification. W002-HELP-002.8,One validated Help message catalog is the source of truth for all three voices,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The Help layer resolves a canonical diagnostic ID through one validated catalog that associates an authored ID with Casual, Office Speak, and Technical templates. It must not use the __DS__ governed artifact namespace, consume a semantic artifact-class token, or be copied into an analyst's Suitcase merely because Data Sculptor runs. W002-HELP-002.9,WASM-002 may use mechanically generated placeholder voice text to prove Help wiring,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WASM-002 acceptance does not require the complete production Help corpus. Authored catalog entries may use unmistakable placeholder strings, and placeholder entries may be generated mechanically from the validated diagnostics.json registry; no production prose authorship is required. Deterministic Generic Technical Help fallback. When a complete registered canonical diagnostic has no matching entry in help_messages.json , all selected Help voices fall back visibly to one Generic Technical rendering. The rendering must show, in this exact conceptual order, the diagnostic ID, severity, phase, behavior, next-action token, and then every emitted governed fact ordered by ascending UTF-8 byte order of fact key. It must state that no diagnostic-specific authored explanation is available. It must not infer cause beyond the diagnostic, invent remediation, default missing facts, inspect undeclared external state, or substitute prose for governed fact values. The Generic Technical fallback preserves the original diagnostic unchanged. Catalog incompleteness is therefore distinct from diagnostic incompleteness: a valid event can always be rendered generically, while inability to satisfy the event's own required_facts contract suppresses that intended event and produces DS-HLP-001 under W002-HELP-001.4 and W002-HELP-001.8. Acceptance must prove correct diagnostic-ID lookup, selected-voice resolution, structured-fact interpolation where a template exists, voice switching, deterministic Generic Technical fallback for a deliberately absent catalog entry, and semantic parity across authored voices. Final authored Help wording, examples, editorial polishing, and production-corpus quality remain deferred to a later Help-content milestone.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-002.10,help_messages.json has one deterministic WASM-002 source schema,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The top-level JSON object has exactly two fields: catalog_version and messages . catalog_version is the string ""1"" . messages is an array written in ascending UTF-8 byte order of diagnostic_id . Each message entry has exactly four fields: diagnostic_id , casual , office_speak , and technical . diagnostic_id must satisfy the canonical DS-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> grammar and must be unique in the catalog. Each voice field is a JSON string. A voice string may contain zero or more structured-fact placeholders using the exact form {fact_name} . Each catalog diagnostic_id must exist in the validated diagnostics.json registry, and each referenced placeholder must be declared in that diagnostic's required_facts or optional_facts . Duplicate IDs, missing voice fields, null voice values, malformed JSON, noncanonical or unregistered diagnostic IDs, or undeclared fact placeholders make catalog validation fail. The catalog is intentionally allowed to be non-exhaustive. A registered diagnostic with no message entry is rendered through the deterministic Generic Technical fallback in W002-HELP-002.9. Therefore a missing catalog entry for a registered diagnostic is not a build-validation failure and must not cause the engine to synthesize an authored entry or suppress the diagnostic. WASM-002 therefore does not require one global exhaustive fact-name table in the PRD. Fact-key authority is per diagnostic: the validated registry declares which fact names are legal for each stable diagnostic meaning. {
  ""catalog_version"": ""1"",
  ""messages"": [
    {
