W002-HELP-002.11,The validated Help catalog is embedded into the released HTML build and supplied to the shared core,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Before a WASM-002 browser build is accepted, the build must parse and validate help_messages.json , then serialize the validated catalog directly into the Data Sculptor HTML itself as one non-executable application/json payload with the exact element ID ds-help-catalog . The embedded JSON must be HTML-safe so catalog text cannot terminate the containing script element; at minimum, literal less-than characters in JSON string content must be escaped during embedding. At runtime, the browser host obtains this embedded payload and supplies the validated catalog to the shared Rust/WASM Help core. Browser JavaScript must not implement a competing template-selection, fact-interpolation, fallback, escaping, or HLP-semantic engine. The browser host must not fetch a Help catalog from the network, the filesystem, the Suitcase, or an adjacent deployment file. The released HTML therefore remains one offline portable front door for the browser Help catalog. A later native host may supply the same governed catalog semantics to the same shared core from its own build-bundled resource; host packaging may differ, but Help semantics must not fork.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-HELP-004.11,Four canonical Boolean facts describe the WASM-002 execution boundary.,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"When the governed diagnostic context can determine the execution boundary, the canonical fact names are exactly: source_modified_by_data_sculptor materialization_started analytical_outputs_published store_state_committed When one of these facts has an established Boolean value, the JSON/structured value is the native Boolean true or false , never the strings ""TRUE"" or ""FALSE"" . source_modified_by_data_sculptor states only whether Data Sculptor modified the analyst-owned source in place; it must not imply knowledge that no external process or analyst changed the source between sessions. materialization_started records whether the governed analytical materialization phase began. analytical_outputs_published records whether governed analytical outputs were successfully published for user use; transient SCR candidates or abandoned/uncommitted debris do not make this fact true. store_state_committed records whether the successor Store MAP commit point was crossed. If a present boundary fact must express governed absence rather than an established Boolean, its JSON/structured value is the exact applicable shared absence-state string ""NONE"" , ""NOT_RUN"" , ""NOT_AVAILABLE"" , or ""NOT_APPLICABLE"" . JSON null is not a valid encoding for these four boundary facts because it would discard the reason for absence. A boundary fact that is optional for a particular diagnostic may instead be omitted under W002-HELP-001.4; that omission carries no absence-state meaning. A missing, omitted, unavailable, or not-run fact must never be interpreted as false . If one of these facts is declared required for an intended diagnostic and the required value cannot be produced, it must not be silently defaulted; the intended diagnostic is suppressed and the fail-safe DS-HLP-001 contract in W002-HELP-001.4/W002-HELP-001.8 applies.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

A future configurable Brand Manifest may add another governed presentation input, but it is not part of the WASM-002 rendering contract.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-HELP-009,"WASM-002 establishes HLP identity, lineage, multiplicity, and one canonical embedded provenance payload.",W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A durable generated Help Report is an immutable governed HLP artifact whose physical filename is: __DS__HLP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.html The UTC token is the HLP's own governed generation/publication time. The report is the final self-contained HTML artifact using the canonical built-in Red5Sorcery/Data Sculptor presentation; no unstyled intermediate is the canonical HLP. Report-request multiplicity: one explicit Help Report request publishes exactly one HLP. The request may be bound to one active governed diagnostic, including a diagnostic that is not associated with a Run, or to one governed Run containing one or more canonical diagnostic events. A Run-level report includes the governed diagnostic events selected by that request in deterministic event order. HLP generation is never an automatic one-artifact-per-diagnostic side effect. Every HLP must expose a visible deterministic Provenance section and exactly one embedded non-executable application/json payload whose element ID is exactly ds-hlp-provenance . F-34 supersedes the earlier draft schema version ""1"" . For schema version ""2"" , the JSON top-level object contains exactly these ten fields: {
  ""schema_version"": ""2"",
  ""hlp_filename"": ""__DS__HLP__20260922T191500123Z__<uuid-v4>.html"",
  ""hlp_generation_utc"": ""20260922T191500123Z"",
  ""diagnostic_ids"": [""DS-ENC-001"", ""DS-MAT-004""],
  ""originating_wko_filename"": ""__DS__WKO__...txt"",
  ""originating_rcp_filename"": null,
  ""selected_help_voice"": ""technical"",
  ""presentation_id"": ""red5sorcery-data-sculptor"",
  ""presentation_version"": ""1"",
  ""data_sculptor_build"": ""<exact-build-id>""
} hlp_generation_utc must use the canonical fixed-width millisecond UTC form YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ . diagnostic_ids is a non-empty JSON array containing one canonical diagnostic ID for each diagnostic event included in the report, in the same deterministic event order used by the report. Repeated IDs are permitted when distinct included events legitimately share one diagnostic type. selected_help_voice is exactly one of casual , office_speak , or technical , matching the Help catalog keys. For WASM-002 the built-in presentation identity is exactly red5sorcery-data-sculptor and its presentation version is exactly ""1"" . data_sculptor_build must contain the exact running build identifier used for the tested/released build; the literal scope label WASM-002 alone is not sufficient unless it is also the exact build identifier. originating_wko_filename and originating_rcp_filename are schema-declared nullable lineage fields . When the relationship exists and the exact physical filename is known, the value is that filename as a JSON string. When the relationship itself does not apply to this Help event/report request, the machine-readable value is JSON null . That null has one schema-defined meaning: the nullable relationship has no value, equivalent to Rust Option<T>::None and to the governed semantic state NOT_APPLICABLE . The visible Provenance section renders it as NOT APPLICABLE . If the lineage relationship does apply but the exact filename cannot be obtained, JSON null must not be used; the field value is the exact string ""NOT_AVAILABLE"" and the visible Provenance section renders NOT AVAILABLE . Empty strings, invented lineage, N/A , UNKNOWN , or another substitute are forbidden. For these two lineage fields, null and ""NOT_AVAILABLE"" are deliberately non-interchangeable. A non-run HLP may therefore legitimately carry JSON null for both lineage fields when neither relationship applies. This nullable-field rule is a schema-specific serialization choice, not a fifth absence state and not a generic JSON encoding rule. Other diagnostic JSON facts follow W002-HELP-001.4 and W002-HELP-004.11. The visible and machine-readable HLP provenance must express the same governed semantics even where their physical representations differ; a semantic mismatch is an HLP-generation failure and must not be silently tolerated. The embedded JSON must be HTML-safe so provenance text cannot terminate the containing script element; at minimum literal less-than characters in JSON string content must be escaped during embedding. The provenance payload remains subject to W002-HELP-010 and must not introduce source rows, source values, absolute local paths, arbitrary Work Order content, or other context excluded by the fixed HLP disclosure policy. WASM-002 does not automatically compute or embed a SHA-256 of the HLP, and saving an HLP must not create, refresh, or verify an LCK . The final HLP bytes remain eligible for exact-byte integrity evidence under the later explicit FINGERPRINT/LCK workflow. Configurable Brand Manifest provenance remains deferred to V1-BACKLOG / a future build. F-14 HLP publication: the complete self-contained report is first written as the corresponding SCR candidate under W002-STOR-023.1. It must close, reopen, and validate the required visible Provenance section, exact schema-version-2 embedded JSON shape, HTML-safe serialization, self-contained presentation and visible/machine semantic parity before the class token may be renamed from SCR to HLP . A partial or semantically mismatched candidate never becomes a canonical HLP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-010,Help Report disclosure uses one fixed WASM-002 allowlist.,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Generating a Help Report must not silently become a data-export path. WASM-002 therefore uses one deterministic allowlist rather than collecting broad context and attempting to redact it afterward. There are no disclosure checkboxes, permissive export modes, or per-report overrides in WASM-002. Always eligible when present and applicable: diagnostic ID; severity/classification; governed operation/phase; continue/refuse decision; safe next action; selected Help voice; HLP identity and generation UTC; relevant governed artifact filenames; and the four canonical boundary facts from W002-HELP-004.11. Eligible only when necessary to explain the diagnostic: the exact source filename but not an absolute OS path; a relevant source column header only when Data Sculptor has structurally established an actual CSV header record; the relevant 1-based column number; a relevant governed Store/RID/COL alias only when that alias itself is necessary to explain the diagnostic, such as an alias collision, ambiguity, or governed alias mutation; byte offset, row/count, or byte-length evidence; Store/RID/COL/MAP/WKO physical filenames; and only the minimum executable Work Order clause or clauses needed to establish intent and the diagnostic trigger. If that minimum Work Order excerpt necessarily contains a governed alias, that alias is disclosed and counts as alias text included. Headerless boundary: record position alone never establishes a source header. If the governed parser has not established a valid header record, including a headerless-source refusal, HLP generation must not treat any field from the first data row or any later data record as header text. Structural evidence such as 1-based column ordinal, governed diagnostic/location facts, or an applicable operational fallback name must be used instead. Never included automatically: source rows; source field values or arbitrary data samples; field data mislabeled as header text; absolute local paths; unrelated source headers, aliases, or column names; the complete Work Order; Work Order comments; unrelated Suitcase contents; browser/environment internals not governed as diagnostic evidence; or raw ungoverned stack traces. Every generated HLP must contain a visible Disclosure section stating, at minimum: Source rows included: NO ; Source values included: NO ; Source header text included: YES or NO ; Governed alias text included: YES or NO ; Absolute local paths included: NO ; Work Order comments included: NO ; and Work Order excerpt: RELEVANT EXECUTABLE CLAUSES ONLY . The two YES/NO declarations must truthfully reflect the actual HLP bytes. A genuine established source header does not count as a source field value; this distinction applies only after the governed parser has established the header record. The renderer must not weaken any declaration when the underlying policy has not changed. This durable-HLP allowlist does not prohibit transient local Help from showing a relevant governed alias or a genuinely established source header when useful to explain the same canonical diagnostic event. Local presentation does not enlarge what the portable HLP may disclose.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-011,Help owns the cross-session source-continuity edge-case explanation,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"When an unexpected analytical result, row-alignment concern, or support question raises the possibility that an analyst-owned source changed between sessions, Data Sculptor-controlled guidance must flow through the Help Engine. Help must not imply that the engine monitored or cryptographically protected the source when it did not. The explanation must distinguish ordinary analyst-controlled workflow from stronger optional evidence. It may ask whether the analyst edited, replaced, sorted, re-exported, synchronized, copied over, or otherwise changed the source after the Store was established.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-011.1,Help presents continuity evidence in explicit assurance levels,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For a suspected cross-session source change, Help must distinguish at least these evidence levels: No continuity evidence: state that cross-session byte continuity cannot be independently verified from filename/Store metadata alone. INVENTORY available: use filename, exact byte length, and last-modified metadata as lightweight clues; changed metadata may indicate that the source changed, while unchanged metadata must not be presented as proof of unchanged bytes. Explicit fingerprint evidence available: exact-byte SHA-256 evidence may establish whether the compared file bytes match or differ under the later governed FINGERPRINT workflow. Help must not collapse these levels into one generic statement of certainty.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-HELP-011.2,WASM-002 does not impose automatic cross-session hashing or Suitcase surveillance,W002-HELP,W002-HELP,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Ordinary WASM-002 materialization and Store inheritance must not automatically SHA-256 the source, recursively fingerprint the Suitcase, or maintain hidden whole-Suitcase surveillance merely to guard against the possibility that an analyst-owned file changed between sessions. This is an intentional product boundary for the lone-office-analyst model. The product assumes the analyst normally controls the Suitcase, provides lightweight explicit INVENTORY evidence in WASM-002, preserves a later explicit FINGERPRINT path for stronger assurance, and relies on Help to explain unusual cross-session continuity questions proportionately. WASM-002 must not create, refresh, or silently verify an LCK Suitcase Lock as a side effect of Work Order save, materialization, Store inheritance, INVENTORY, alias maintenance, or ordinary project use. LCK publication belongs to the explicit later-V1 FINGERPRINT workflow. F-13 single-writer Help boundary: Help must distinguish cross-session continuity from concurrent writing. WASM-002 does not claim that two Data Sculptor tabs/windows can safely write the same Suitcase at once. User guidance must say to use one writing Data Sculptor context per Suitcase; read-only viewing is not itself a governed write. When a pre-commit guard detects that relevant governed state changed underneath an operation, Help must identify the changed authority where available and direct the analyst to refresh or reopen current state and rerun deliberately. It must not imply that Data Sculptor acquired a cross-tab lock, merged the competing work, or automatically rebased the refused transaction.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-PRETTY-001,Separation of truth and presentation,W002-PRETTY,W002-PRETTY,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,The PRETTY Engine must not decide analytical truth or reinterpret diagnostic meaning. A future build may replace the built-in presentation source with a governed Brand Manifest without changing the analytical or diagnostic truth supplied to PRETTY.,NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-QA-001,Governed test-only seams and acceptance coverage,W002-QA,W002-QA,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Every material frozen WASM-002 behavior must have retained acceptance evidence sufficient to exercise the governed success, refusal, mutation, publication, or recovery boundary that makes the behavior meaningful. Related cases may share one fixture when the shared fixture proves each required condition explicitly; acceptance coverage must not rely on a behavior being difficult to reproduce under an uncontrolled host environment. Permitted deterministic test-only seams. WASM-002 acceptance may use controlled clock values; controlled UUID sequences and collision outcomes; controlled filesystem create/write/close/rename/promotion failures; and controlled run-local source-handle reread/substitution conditions. A seam supplies only the external condition required to reach the governed behavior. It must not bypass validation, alter the normative semantic result, change governed serialization, relax publication rules, rewrite diagnostic truth, or create a second analytical execution model. Release boundary. Test-only controls must not be invocable through the ordinary Data Sculptor UI, DS-STEPS, saved Work Orders, URL/query parameters, Suitcase configuration, or another analyst-facing product path. Compile-time exclusion, test-build configuration, or an isolated acceptance harness are permitted implementation techniques. Retained acceptance evidence must identify any seam used and must separately demonstrate that the accepted release surface cannot invoke that seam as a user feature. Named storage acceptance gaps. Acceptance must include a case-variant governed namespace/class fixture proving that Data Sculptor does not silently normalize the variant spelling into canonical governed identity; an unknown syntactically valid governed-class fixture proving that the file remains byte-for-byte unchanged while a canonical INFO diagnostic and INVENTORY surface the unknown/unrecognized class; and at least one known-but-not-emitted-class fixture drawn from DGN , RCV , BRD , or LCK proving the same preserve-and-report behavior without activating a producer, lifecycle, or interpretation path. Carried feature gates remain feature-owned. Mechanisms whose normative lifecycle is integrated in another package — including the F-02 Work Order-registry/alias-replacement behavior, the F-04 existing-Store cardinality refusal, and the F-24 CER-history decision — cannot be considered accepted without their corresponding feature acceptance gates. This requirement does not invent those feature semantics. If a proposed mechanism is removed from WASM-002 rather than integrated, no acceptance gate for that removed mechanism is required.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-MAT-ACC-001,Multi-column one-pass Stage 2 materialization,W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Using a valid UTF-8 source and a Work Order requesting at least four source columns through a mixture of HEADER and COLUMN selectors, acceptance must prove that Stage 1 completes first, Stage 2 restarts at byte zero of the same run-local source instance, parses the header once, resolves all selectors before the first data row, and reads the source data records only once while producing all requested columns. W002-MAT-ACC-002,"Automatic Store MAP creation, inheritance, and rematerialization continuity",W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An acceptance fixture must materialize four previously unseen source columns in one Store-establishing Work Order and prove that one successor Store MAP is created with four mapping rows. A later Work Order using the same exact SOURCE without explicitly naming a MAP must route under W002-STOR-019.2 . If exactly one routable Store lineage exists for that exact source filename and its current Store state permits materialization, the Work Order must inherit that lineage’s current structurally valid Store MAP, preserve the Store/RID metadata and four prior mappings, add a fifth default COL alias, and publish one new complete Store MAP. A later rematerialization of one earlier logical column must preserve its inherited COL alias while updating its column_filename . An explicit older MAP selection must instead use that historical Store state. Equal-latest-timestamp ambiguity within one routed lineage, malformed-newer-MAP fallback within the same Store lineage, no-routable-Store-lineage creation, and multiple-routable-Store-lineages-for-the-same-source refusal must also be exercised.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

P3-06 validation-tier fixtures: acceptance must distinguish Store-health Tier 1 from full Tier 2 validation. P2-04 closure fixtures: acceptance must include (1) a RID that satisfies Tier 1 but fails Tier 2 because the body does not contain the exact declared 1..N sequence; (2) a COL that satisfies Tier 1 but fails Tier 2 because its complete CSV body or logical-record count is invalid; (3) an externally supplied same-named RID/COL that passes the required governed tier without any assertion that it is the historical original bytes; and (4) a REPAIR MAP case with a mixture of Tier-2-valid and Tier-2-invalid COLs proving that the successor removes exactly the failing bindings. Repeating the same fixture bytes must yield the same repair set and successor mapping.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

W002-MAT-ACC-003,Stage 2 structural window-invariance matrix,W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance fixtures must force input boundaries at structurally difficult positions including before/after delimiters, before/after opening and closing quotes, between doubled quote bytes, between CR and LF, inside quoted multiline field content, at empty fields, and inside already-certified multi-byte UTF-8 sequences. Across permitted window sizes and boundary placements, the logical row count, selected values, canonical COL bytes, first refusal location/condition, and resolved mapping semantics must remain invariant. P3-09 fixtures: acceptance must include both byte forms identified by the Pass 3 finding: (1) an exactly zero-byte source and (2) a source containing only the three UTF-8 BOM bytes EF BB BF . Both must pass the applicable Stage 1 UTF-8 gate and then refuse in Stage 2 with NO_HEADER_RECORD . The exact expected location tuples are respectively (offset 0, physical line 1, logical record 1, field ordinal 1) and (offset 3, physical line 1, logical record 1, field ordinal 1) . The fixtures must also distinguish this case from an existing-but-blank first logical record, which remains BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD . P3-10 delimiter-help fixture: acceptance must include a quoted semicolon-delimited form such as ""a"";""b"" and an equivalent TAB-delimited quoted form that reach INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE . The canonical refusal condition and location facts must remain unchanged, while the Help rendering is permitted to surface the delimiter-mismatch hint for offending byte 0x3B or 0x09 . F-06 structural-refusal acceptance matrix An unexpected quote in an unquoted field must report the quote byte and UNEXPECTED_QUOTE_IN_UNQUOTED_FIELD . A prohibited byte after a closing quote must report that byte and INVALID_BYTE_AFTER_CLOSING_QUOTE . A bare CR outside quoted content must report the CR byte and BARE_CR_OUTSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD . CR, LF, and CRLF inside valid quoted values must remain field content and must not trigger the bare-CR rule. EOF in an open quoted field must report the one-past-end source offset and EOF_INSIDE_QUOTED_FIELD . A blank logical record must report BLANK_LOGICAL_RECORD , not TOO_FEW_FIELDS . A short record must report the terminator/EOF location and the first missing field ordinal. A wide record must report the comma delimiter opening the first extra field and that extra field ordinal. All five refusal facts must remain identical across permitted source-window sizes and boundary placements. Fixtures must force boundaries around commas, opening and closing quotes, doubled-quote pairs, CR/LF pairs, quoted multiline content, empty fields, and already-certified multibyte UTF-8 sequences. A semicolon-separated file must not refuse solely because it uses semicolons; Help may explain comma-only interpretation when header selection fails. Day 060 H-13 Receipt-corpus binding for P3-09 The two analytical P3-09 source fixtures above must each have a corresponding byte-exact refusal Receipt under W002-RCP-ACC-002. The zero-byte and BOM-only cases therefore prove both the parser/refusal oracle and the Receipt serialization oracle independently.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-ACC-004,Canonical one-column COL serialization acceptance,W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Golden-byte fixtures must cover ordinary ASCII, non-ASCII UTF-8, commas, embedded double quotes, CR, LF, CRLF inside quoted values, explicit empty data values, empty source headers, and header-only zero-row input. W002-MAT-ACC-005,"Field-limit, ragged-record, blank-record, and failure-publication acceptance",W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must include decoded field sizes exactly 16 MiB and 16 MiB + 1 byte, malformed runaway quoted-field cases, nonblank records with too few and too many fields, a bare blank logical data record, explicit empty fields, and a physical blank line inside a valid quoted multiline field. The first invalid case must refuse without truncation or silent repair. Publication evidence must additionally exercise both a new-Store multi-column materialization and a later existing-Store materialization. For the new Store, the shared publication-transaction UTC must be established before any new RID/COL SCR candidate is opened, and each candidate-specific UUID must be allocated before its candidate is created. RID and COL outputs must remain governed SCR until the complete candidate set validates; the RID must then promote first, requested COLs must promote in deterministic KEEP order, the successor MAP UUID must be allocated before its MAP SCR candidate is opened, that MAP candidate must be written/closed/reopened/validated while still SCR , and its final SCR -to- MAP rename must occur last. For every successfully promoted RID, COL, and MAP artifact, acceptance must prove that the candidate and final identity have the exact same UTC, UUID, extension, and bytes and differ in the governed filename only by the three-letter semantic class token. For the existing Store, the inherited RID must remain byte-for-byte and filename-identical with no new RID candidate. F-04 existing-Store cardinality acceptance: acceptance must include two otherwise valid existing-Store materializations using the same exact governed SOURCE identity. In the equal-cardinality fixture, Stage 2 candidate N must equal the inherited RID-header N and publication may proceed under the ordinary rules. In the mismatch fixture, candidate N must differ from RID-header N ; the Run must refuse before any candidate COL is promoted into the final COL namespace and before any successor MAP is published. The inherited RID, current MAP, existing COL artifacts, and Store health must remain unchanged, with the existing Store remaining VALID. The equal-cardinality case must not be represented as proof of source-byte or row-semantic identity. Forced failure cases must cover: failure before any promotion; RID-promotion failure; failure during COL promotion after RID and at least one COL have promoted; MAP-candidate write/close/reopen/validation failure; MAP final-rename failure; and interruption after physical RID/COL promotion but before MAP commit. Each case must prove rollback where safely possible or visible non-authoritative SCR failure evidence otherwise, must prove that unreferenced final-class-looking RID/COL files are not treated as committed Store membership, and must prove that the prior valid MAP remains authoritative for an existing Store or that no committed Store exists for an uncommitted first materialization. F-20 bounded-width/name acceptance: acceptance must cover exactly 16,384 versus 16,385 source columns; KEEP widths of 1 and 16,384 ; operational-name derivation at 1,024 versus 1,025 Unicode scalar values; physical ordinals producing Column A , Column Z , Column AA , and Column XFD ; and deterministic oversized-header fallback collisions proving [ordinal] then -2 progression. A separate short-header alias collision must prove refusal rather than automatic suffixing.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-MAT-ACC-006,Large-source browser materialization evidence,W002-MAT-ACC,W002-MAT,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WASM-002 acceptance must include a browser run against the established Statistics Canada scale source or an equivalently retained scale fixture, recording source bytes, Stage 1 time, Stage 2 time, total time, selected-column count, logical row count, bytes written per COL , peak/bounded memory observations, output fingerprints, and browser/platform details. W002-CONV-ACC-001,Separate Windows-1252 conversion,W002-CONV-ACC,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A non-UTF-8 fixture compatible with the supported Windows-1252 converter must cause the analytical task to stop, permit a Help suggestion, and succeed only when the separate conversion Work Order is explicitly run. P3-08 acceptance: the fixture set must convert an analyst-owned legacy source successfully, materialize the resulting CVT, then perform a second successful conversion from a refreshed legacy source using the same analyst-owned filename. The second conversion must publish a different CVT physical filename. First materialization of that second CVT must establish a distinct Store/RID lineage rather than inherit from the first CVT-backed Store. Acceptance must also prove that Help discloses this consequence at conversion success and again when the CVT is first materialized, and that no hidden original-source identity is used to join the two CVTs into one lineage. F-16 acceptance: the compatible non-UTF-8 fixture must prove that strict UTF-8 certification first emits DS-ENC-001 with next_action: NONE ; Stage 2 does not start; Data Sculptor restarts at byte 0 of the same bound source instance and scans the complete source under the frozen mapping; the Receipt records WINDOWS_1252_COMPATIBILITY_OUTCOME: COMPATIBLE and WINDOWS_1252_FIRST_UNDEFINED_BYTE_OFFSET: NOT_APPLICABLE ; and only then is DS-CNV-001 emitted with severity: INFO , behavior: CONTINUE , and next_action: RUN_WINDOWS_1252_CONVERSION . The refused MATERIALIZE run must remain refused. A separate valid-UTF-8 fixture must prove that both Windows-1252 compatibility Receipt fields are NOT_RUN and DS-CNV-001 is not emitted. F-10 conversion-gate and byte-output acceptance A source already valid as complete strict UTF-8 must refuse CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 as unnecessary and create no CVT . A source that fails strict UTF-8 but passes the complete Windows-1252 compatibility assessment may convert only when the separate conversion WKO is explicitly run. The analyst-owned source bytes must remain unchanged. The published CVT must pass complete strict UTF-8 certification. Source CR, LF, and CRLF bytes must be preserved in place rather than normalized. The conversion must remain bounded/streaming. The published CVT must not begin with a UTF-8 BOM introduced by Data Sculptor. The successful Receipt must contain the frozen conversion operation token and required conversion facts. Frozen minimal byte oracle: Windows-1252 source bytes:
63 61 66 E9 0D 0A

UTF-8 CVT bytes:
63 61 66 C3 A9 0D 0A This is café followed by CRLF. The expected CVT begins with byte 63 ; no EF BB BF prefix is present. Day 060 H-25 / BM-04 acceptance: the already-valid-UTF-8 CONVERT fixture must use a complete source whose byte stream is valid strict UTF-8 and must produce a byte-exact refused Receipt containing: SOURCE_ENCODING: UTF-8
UNDEFINED_WINDOWS_1252_BYTE_OFFSET: NOT_RUN
MATERIALIZED_ENCODING: NOT_RUN
TRANSCODING: NOT_RUN
SOURCE_CHANGED: NO
OUTPUT_FILENAME: NONE The same fixture must prove that no Windows-1252 compatibility assessment runs, no transcoding begins, the analyst-owned source bytes remain unchanged, and no CVT file is created.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-CONV-ACC-002,Undefined Windows-1252 byte refusal,W002-CONV-ACC,W002-CONV,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A fixture containing a byte undefined by the frozen Windows-1252 mapping must not be silently converted. F-16 acceptance: use fixtures placing each of 0x81 , 0x8D , 0x8F , 0x90 , and 0x9D at controlled physical offsets, including across compatibility-buffer boundaries. The complete oracle must prove WINDOWS_1252_COMPATIBILITY_OUTCOME: INCOMPATIBLE , the exact first undefined-byte offset, no DS-CNV-001 emission, no conversion recommendation, and window-size invariance. A separate injected read-failure fixture after the compatibility pass begins must prove NOT_AVAILABLE for both compatibility Receipt fields and no conversion recommendation. F-10 conversion-operation undefined-byte acceptance The separate CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 operation must itself refuse before transcoding when its complete compatibility assessment encounters any byte undefined by the frozen Windows-1252 mapping. Such a refusal publishes no CVT . Acceptance must cover each frozen undefined byte value at a controlled absolute source offset and prove that no replacement-character, ISO-8859-1, or permissive-decoder fallback produces output. The operation must refuse before transcoding begins. The byte-exact Receipt for this fixture must include: SOURCE_ENCODING: WINDOWS-1252-INCOMPATIBLE

W002-WKO-007,Work Order syntax is the analytical contract,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"If a value, reference, option, or instruction changes what Data Sculptor analytically does, that intent must be represented in governed Work Order text or in a separately governed artifact explicitly referenced by that Work Order. Browser permission, directory selection, UI focus, a highlighted file, an alias display, or another GUI gesture must not silently become analytical intent. For WASM-002, every executable saved WKO begins with the common preamble: SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS ""<non-whitespace alias>"" Ignoring blank lines and governed comments, the WKO must then parse completely under exactly one of these seven executable operation grammars: Operation Governed DS-STEPS structure after the common preamble MATERIALIZE SOURCE ""..."" ; optional MAP ""..."" ; KEEP ; one or more selectors; terminal MATERIALIZE . INVENTORY terminal INVENTORY only. UPDATE ALIASES exactly one Store-state selector: SOURCE ""..."" or MAP ""..."" ; one or more governed alias mutations; terminal UPDATE ALIASES . REPAIR MAP exactly one MAP ""<exact current Store MAP filename>"" ; terminal REPAIR MAP . REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY terminal REPAIR WORK ORDER REGISTRY only. CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 exactly one SOURCE ""..."" ; terminal CONVERT WINDOWS-1252 TO UTF-8 . CATALOG STORES terminal CATALOG STORES only. Each operation-specific numbered requirement remains authoritative for its detailed selectors, preconditions, mutations, publication semantics, and acceptance behavior. This requirement freezes the cross-operation boundary: unknown semantic lines refuse; clauses from another operation grammar refuse unless the selected operation explicitly defines them; there is no best-effort interpretation and no silent cross-operation mixing. Lexical token separation. DS-STEPS keywords are matched ASCII case-insensitively; canonical examples render them uppercase. Wherever two adjacent lexical tokens would otherwise run together, they must be separated by one or more ASCII SPACE ( 0x20 ) or horizontal TAB ( 0x09 ) characters. Leading SPACE/TAB indentation is semantically neutral. Thus REPAIR MAP , SOURCE ""crime.csv"" , and COLUMN 7 are valid tokenizations, while REPAIRMAP , SOURCE""crime.csv"" , and UPDATE_ALIASES are not alternate DS-STEPS spellings. Quoted-string contents are never case-folded or whitespace-normalized merely because keywords are case-insensitive. The browser may authorize resources, edit text, validate, save, invoke Run, display evidence, and provide Help. Authorization to access a resource is not authorization to use that resource analytically.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

Help must not teach an absolute machine path as the normal replacement for . .",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)

A portable Work Order must not depend on an absolute machine-specific path to identify ordinary Suitcase files. Resolution must be deterministic in browser and later native hosts. W002-WKO-009.1,WASM-002 SOURCE eligibility is exact and root-bounded,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A WASM-002 SOURCE clause names exactly one physical regular file in the Suitcase root by exact filename only. It must not name an absolute path, drive or UNC path, subdirectory, path containing / or \ , traversal such as .. , URL/URI, or another external reference. Resolution uses the exact Unicode-scalar filename identity and reference-bounded rules frozen by F-15; no case-folding, normalization, trimming, or filesystem-equivalence search is permitted. The only eligible WASM-002 SOURCE kinds are: Analyst-owned CSV: a regular Suitcase-root file whose exact filename does not begin with the reserved exact prefix __DS__ and whose final extension is .csv under ASCII case-insensitive extension recognition. Thus .csv , .CSV , and mixed-case equivalents are candidate CSV extensions. This case-insensitivity applies only to extension recognition; the complete filename reference remains exact. If the physical file is crime.CSV , a differently cased full filename does not become an alternate reference to it. Governed converted source: a successfully published CVT whose exact canonical identity and class-specific publication/validity predicate satisfy W002-CONV-004, W002-STOR-023, and PB-STOR-008. A filename that merely resembles a CVT is not sufficient. No other governed semantic class is eligible as SOURCE in WASM-002, even when its physical serialization is CSV. In particular, COL , RID , MAP , CAT , INV , RCP , HLP , CER , SCR , RCV , and WKO artifacts cannot be reintroduced as SOURCE merely because their bytes or extension appear compatible. A recognized .csv extension establishes only candidate SOURCE form. It does not certify encoding or CSV structure; the normal strict UTF-8 and structural certification contracts still govern after source resolution. Conversely, CSV-like bytes stored under a non-CSV analyst-owned extension are not an eligible WASM-002 SOURCE.",PARTIAL,PORTION_VERIFIED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,CP-008; CP-009; CP-010,"T-ACCEPTED, BANKED; W002-WKO-010,WIP and WKO are distinct Work Order lifecycle states,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"WIP is the editable, non-executable Work Order state. WKO is the saved, validated, immutable Work Order artifact that may become a Run target. Validation establishes that a Work Order is structurally eligible to run; it does not guarantee that runtime conditions will succeed. Loading a WKO for inspection does not make it mutable. If its instruction text is changed, the editor must treat the edited text as a new WIP derived from the original WKO. The original WKO bytes and physical identity remain unchanged, and the derived WIP cannot Run until saved as a new WKO. F-08 Run distinction: the browser Run action invokes one selected saved immutable WKO that is eligible under the governed WKO-registry rules. No ordinary WASM-002 WKO contains a textual RUN line merely to execute itself. The DS-STEPS token RUN is reserved for future saved-Work-Order composition under W002-WKO-011 and is not repurposed as the browser execution trigger.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-013,WASM-002 executes one saved Work Order without Work Order chaining,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"For WASM-002, one saved immutable WKO is one top-level executable request. It must not invoke, include, chain, or execute another WKO. The governed RUN composition operation and equivalent nested-orchestration constructs are not executable in WASM-002. If a saved WKO contains composition syntax, validation must refuse before analytical execution begins. The canonical diagnostic and Help path must explain that Work Order composition is deferred rather than treating the syntax as arbitrary text, silently ignoring it, or partially executing surrounding instructions. This scope cut does not prohibit one Work Order from selecting and materializing multiple columns in the single Stage 2 operation defined by WASM-002.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012,Materialization COL alias assignment uses AS; standalone alias maintenance uses UPDATE ALIASES,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within the WASM-002 DS-STEPS materialization form, an analyst assigns or changes the alias of a selected materialized COL with the optional same-line clause AS ""alias"" under W002-STEPS-005. This syntax is part of the governed Work Order and is not a GUI gesture. A single KEEP block may therefore assign aliases to multiple selected columns in one governed materialization. Automatic source-header COL aliases and inherited rematerialization aliases are resolved first; explicit AS clauses then determine requested successor COL aliases before complete Store-MAP validation and publication. Revision BD freezes alias-only creation/replacement with UPDATE ALIASES and explicit historical Store-MAP selection with MAP ""<exact Store MAP filename>"" . Revision BE completes the bounded alias lifecycle with explicit CLEAR ... ALIAS and RESET ... ALIAS forms under W002-WKO-012.5 through W002-WKO-012.6. Empty-string AS """" is not the clearing syntax.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.1,Canonical standalone alias-maintenance Work Order uses UPDATE ALIASES,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The canonical alias-only Store metadata forms are: SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS ""Rename crime store""
SOURCE ""35100178.csv""
STORE AS ""Crime Statistics""
UPDATE ALIASES or, when the analyst intentionally selects one exact Store snapshot: SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS ""Rename crime store""
MAP ""__DS__MAP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv""
STORE AS ""Crime Statistics""
UPDATE ALIASES UPDATE ALIASES is the explicit terminal commitment clause for an alias-only Work Order. The WKO must identify exactly one Store-state base using either SOURCE ""..."" for ordinary Store-aware current-state selection or MAP ""..."" for exact Store-MAP selection, never both. At least one supported alias mutation clause must occur after the Store-state selector and before UPDATE ALIASES . An alias-only Work Order must not contain KEEP , MATERIALIZE , INVENTORY , conversion, Store repair, Work Order registry repair, cataloging, deferred Work Order composition, or another operation's terminal clause. Alias maintenance changes governed human-facing metadata only.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.2,"STORE AS, RID AS, and COL ... AS are the canonical alias-replacement clauses",W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, the canonical mutation clauses are: STORE AS ""Crime Statistics""
RID AS ""Row Number""
COL ""Crime Rate"" AS ""Police-Reported Crime Rate"" STORE AS ""..."" replaces the selected Store snapshot's store_alias . RID AS ""..."" replaces its rid_alias . COL ""<reference>"" AS ""..."" replaces the alias of exactly one existing mapped COL. The COL reference resolves under W002-STOR-021: it may be the exact physical column_filename or one unique current COL alias from the selected Store MAP. Missing, ambiguous, non-COL, or conflicting resolution must refuse rather than guess. One Work Order may update the Store alias, RID alias, and multiple distinct COL aliases together, provided the complete successor state satisfies all existing alias uniqueness/shadowing rules.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.3,"MAP ""<filename>"" is the exact historical Store-MAP selector",W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The canonical explicit Store-MAP selection clause is: MAP ""__DS__MAP__20260920T184512347Z__<uuid-v4>.csv"" The value is always the exact physical filename of one structurally valid immutable Store MAP. It is not a Store alias, WKO alias, timestamp shorthand, UUID-only selector, or latest expression. For MATERIALIZE, if present, the clause occurs immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP . It overrides automatic Store-MAP inheritance and binds the run to exactly the named Store snapshot. For alias-only maintenance, the Work Order uses either SOURCE ""..."" or MAP ""..."" as its Store-state selector, not both. For materialization, SOURCE ""..."" remains mandatory and an optional MAP ""..."" supplies the exact historical/current Store-state base. Validation must refuse an incompatible source/MAP pairing or a MAP that is not a valid Store-MAP profile. Health rule: explicit historical selection does not override the current Store-lineage health gate. The selected lineage must currently be VALID and every RID/COL binding referenced by the named MAP must currently be present and valid. Otherwise the operation refuses. This applies equally to MATERIALIZE and UPDATE ALIASES. F-05/P2-01 source-compatibility predicate: for materialization, an explicitly named MAP is compatible only when the mandatory Work Order SOURCE exactly equals the one common source_filename carried by that Store MAP. If the exact filenames differ, validation refuses before the F-04 existing-Store cardinality gate in W002-MAT-002.6. Equal row count never authorizes a different source to enter the selected Store lineage.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.4,Alias-only execution publishes one complete successor Store MAP and no rewritten data artifacts,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"A successful UPDATE ALIASES operation begins from the selected complete Store MAP, applies only the requested alias replacements in memory, validates the complete resulting Store state, writes the successor MAP under governed SCR , closes and reopens it, validates it fully, and promotes it to a new immutable MAP last. That successful promotion is the alias-update commit point. The operation must preserve the selected Store's physical RID and COL filenames and bytes, source-column keys, row order, cardinality, and lineage except for the human-facing alias fields explicitly changed by the Work Order. It must not reread source data rows merely to change aliases, must not create RID/COL artifacts, and must not rewrite or delete the inherited MAP. The prior MAP remains visible historical state. If validation or MAP publication fails, no successor alias state becomes current. The failure is reported through the governed diagnostic/Help path and any incomplete candidate remains subject to the retained- SCR failure-evidence rules in W002-STOR-023.1; WASM-002 does not emit RCV. Revision BM E-02 integration: when the alias-only operation uses an explicitly named historical Store MAP, publication is permitted only if the Store lineage currently evaluates VALID and every RID/COL binding referenced by that named MAP is currently present and valid. An older MAP cannot be used to bypass current damage. P3-06 validation depth: because UPDATE ALIASES does not consume RID/COL analytical contents, its Store-health and binding checks use Tier 1 under W002-STOR-019.10. The operation must not scan every RID/COL record merely to change aliases. This does not weaken later operations that actually consume those artifacts; they must perform the applicable Tier 2 validation before relying on the contents.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-007,Standalone Store/RID/COL alias maintenance acceptance,W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must establish a Store with one RID and at least three materialized COLs, then execute an alias-only Work Order that changes the Store alias, RID alias, and at least two COL aliases in one UPDATE ALIASES operation. One COL must be targeted by its unique current alias and another by its exact physical COL filename. The fixture must prove that exactly one complete successor Store MAP becomes current; prior MAP, RID, and COL artifacts remain byte-for-byte unchanged; no source-data row read is required; no new RID/COL artifact is published; and the successor MAP contains exactly the requested aliases while preserving all physical bindings and logical source-column keys. Missing/ambiguous COL references and successor alias collisions must refuse without publishing a successor MAP. F-23 CLEAR/RESET alias fixtures: acceptance must separately exercise CLEAR STORE ALIAS , CLEAR RID ALIAS , CLEAR COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS , RESET STORE ALIAS , RESET RID ALIAS , and RESET COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS . Each CLEAR fixture must prove that the successor MAP stores the governed empty alias without renaming or rewriting the referenced artifact. Each RESET fixture must prove restoration of the exact deterministic default governed by W002-WKO-012.6 and W002-STOR-019.7, including the oversized-header operational fallback where applicable. The fixtures must prove that CLEAR and RESET require no source-data row read, publish exactly one complete successor Store MAP on success, leave the predecessor MAP/RID/COL bytes unchanged, and deterministically refuse duplicate mutation of the same alias field or a reset/default value that fails the complete successor alias validity/uniqueness/shadowing rules.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-008,Explicit historical Store-MAP selection acceptance,W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must create at least two valid Store MAP snapshots for one Store, then prove that a Work Order containing MAP ""<older exact Store MAP filename>"" binds to that exact older snapshot even though a newer valid MAP exists. An alias-only fixture must publish its successor from the explicitly named older base rather than from the newer automatic current state. A materialization fixture must retain mandatory SOURCE ""..."" while using the explicit MAP as its Store-state base. The tests must also prove refusal for a missing MAP, malformed MAP, WKO-MAP profile supplied as Store MAP, and source/MAP incompatibility. No implementation may substitute the newest MAP after an explicit MAP clause has validated. F-21 chronology acceptance: the fixture must use at least three successive valid MAP snapshots for one Store so that an explicitly selected older base and a distinct pre-run current MAP both exist. Merely selecting/validating the older MAP must leave current authority unchanged. A successful governed operation from that older base must then publish exactly one new successor whose requested state is derived from the named older base, whose publication UTC is later than the pre-run current chronology predecessor, and which becomes current under ordinary greatest-UTC selection. The selected historical MAP and the formerly current MAP must remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Acceptance must prove that later mappings/aliases present only in the formerly current MAP are not silently merged into the historical-base successor unless the Work Order explicitly recreates them. Receipt evidence must identify the exact operation base and exact published successor through the already-frozen operation-specific Receipt fields. No additional warning/permission gate or informational diagnostic is required merely because the analyst explicitly chose a historical base.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.5,CLEAR ... ALIAS deliberately removes a human-facing alias,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, the canonical clearing forms are: CLEAR STORE ALIAS
CLEAR RID ALIAS
CLEAR COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS CLEAR deliberately stores the empty string in the corresponding alias field of the successor Store MAP. It does not restore a default alias. An empty-string replacement such as STORE AS """" , RID AS """" , or COL ""..."" AS """" is not the canonical clearing form and must be rejected by the bounded WASM-002 grammar. For CLEAR COL , <reference> resolves against the selected pre-mutation Store MAP by exact physical column_filename or one unique current COL alias under W002-STOR-021. All COL references in one UPDATE ALIASES Work Order are resolved before any mutation is applied so clause order cannot change target identity. Missing, ambiguous, duplicate-target, or non-COL references must refuse. Clearing an alias never renames, rewrites, or deletes the underlying RID/COL artifact and never changes physical identity.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-012.6,RESET ... ALIAS restores the deterministic default alias,W002-WKO,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Within an alias-only UPDATE ALIASES Work Order, the canonical reset forms are: RESET STORE ALIAS
RESET RID ALIAS
RESET COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS RESET STORE ALIAS restores the Store MAP's common exact source_filename . RESET RID ALIAS restores the literal RID . RESET COL ""<reference>"" ALIAS restores that mapped COL's deterministic operational default defined by W002-STOR-019.7 from its exact recorded source_header and physical source ordinal: the exact header when it contains at most 1,024 Unicode scalar values, or the deterministic Column <LETTERS> fallback/disambiguation rule when the recorded header exceeds that boundary. RESET never substitutes the potentially oversized exact header into the alias field merely because that header remains authoritative source evidence. RESET is therefore distinct from CLEAR . The restored value must pass the same governed alias validity, uniqueness, and shadowing rules as any explicit alias. If the deterministic default is empty or conflicts in the complete successor Store MAP, RESET must refuse except for the narrow oversized-header fallback/disambiguation rule already frozen in W002-STOR-019.7; Data Sculptor must not otherwise invent a suffix, alternate spelling, or substitute. AS , CLEAR , and RESET mutations may coexist in one Work Order when they target distinct alias fields; duplicate mutation of the same alias field in one Work Order must refuse. A successful operation publishes exactly one complete successor Store MAP under the existing UPDATE ALIASES commit contract.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-001,Canonical WASM-002 DS-STEPS materialization form,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The canonical WASM-002 materialization Work Order form is: # Optional human comment
SUITCASE: .
WORK ORDER AS ""Prepare monthly crime data""
SOURCE ""crime.csv""
[MAP ""__DS__MAP__YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ__<uuid-v4>.csv""]

KEEP
  HEADER ""REF_DATE"" AS ""Year""      # reporting year
  HEADER ""GEO""
  COLUMN 7 AS ""Crime Rate""

MATERIALIZE SUITCASE: . is governed by W002-WKO-008. WORK ORDER AS ""..."" is mandatory for an executable/saved WASM-002 Work Order and declares the immutable human-facing WKO alias governed by W002-STEPS-001.1. SOURCE ""..."" names the exact Suitcase-root source file. MAP ""..."" is optional with cardinality 0..1. If present, it occurs immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP , names one exact physical governed Store MAP filename, and binds the run to that exact current or historical Store lineage subject to W002-STOR-019.3 and W002-WKO-012.3. If absent, the Store-aware exact-source routing rules apply. KEEP is the bare governed keyword and introduces one or more column selectors. KEEP: is not valid WASM-002 syntax. Each selector is either HEADER ""..."" or COLUMN n and may optionally end with AS ""..."" . MATERIALIZE is the explicit terminal commitment verb. Duplicate structural clauses refuse. An empty KEEP refuses. After MATERIALIZE , only blank lines or comments may follow; a trailing comment on the physical MATERIALIZE line is permitted because comments are removed from the semantic token stream. # comments are governed by W002-STEPS-001.2. No RID/row-index clause appears in the Work Order. If this materialization establishes a new Store, the engine automatically generates exactly one RID artifact under W002-RID-002 and W002-RID-008. If it extends an existing Store, the existing RID is reused subject to the Store health/cardinality rules. This requirement freezes the bounded keyword structure and selector forms shown above for BM integration. Other complete-language lexical features remain outside this bounded syntax freeze unless separately specified. F-08 common-grammar boundary: MATERIALIZE is one of the seven executable WASM-002 operation grammars governed by W002-WKO-007. Its optional MAP clause remains in the frozen position immediately after SOURCE and before KEEP . The terminal MATERIALIZE clause is DS-STEPS syntax; the browser's Run action is not written into the Work Order. F-20 bounded KEEP: the canonical KEEP block contains at least one and at most 16,384 selectors, and after resolution those selectors must identify at least one and at most 16,384 distinct source columns. This is the complete WASM-002 selection-width bound.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-001.1,WORK ORDER AS declares the immutable human-facing Work Order alias,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An executable or saved WASM-002 Work Order must contain exactly one top-level clause: WORK ORDER AS ""<alias>"" In canonical forms it appears after SUITCASE: . and before the operation-specific source/selector clauses. The decoded alias must be non-empty. The quoted alias may contain spaces and ordinary UTF-8 phrase text subject to the governed string-literal rules. The alias affects display and governed alias resolution only; it does not replace the WKO filename/UUID as physical execution identity. The alias is stored in the immutable WKO bytes and is published into the current WKO MAP when the WKO save transaction commits. Changing the alias therefore requires saving a new WKO under the frozen WKO lifecycle. No valid executable/saved WKO in WASM-002 is unaliased. P3-10 alias-content rule: “non-empty” means that, after decoding the quoted string literal, the alias must contain at least one non-whitespace character. An alias consisting only of whitespace refuses Work Order validation. Data Sculptor must not trim, collapse, normalize, or otherwise rewrite leading or trailing whitespace in an otherwise valid alias; the decoded alias text remains authoritative and is preserved exactly in the immutable WKO and governed WKO MAP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-001.2,# introduces a DS-STEPS line comment outside double-quoted strings,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Outside a double-quoted string, the first # on a line begins a comment that continues through the line's LF terminator. Whole-line comments and trailing comments are permitted. Comment text has no execution semantics and is ignored by the DS-STEPS parser after lexical recognition. A # inside a double-quoted string is ordinary string content and does not begin a comment; for example WORK ORDER AS ""Analysis #3"" and HEADER ""CATEGORY #"" preserve the hash character. WASM-002 defines no block-comment syntax. Comments are preserved byte-for-byte in the saved immutable WKO TXT. Editing, adding, or removing a comment changes the WKO bytes and therefore requires saving a new WKO artifact even though analytical semantics may remain unchanged.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-002,HEADER selects by exact decoded source-header value,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"HEADER ""name"" resolves against the exact decoded header values established for the certified source. Header equality is exact Unicode scalar-value sequence equality under PB-STOR-010: Data Sculptor performs no case folding, locale folding, Unicode normalization, trimming, or filesystem-style comparison. A selector that matches no source header must refuse. If the same exact decoded header sequence occurs in more than one source column, the header selector is ambiguous and must refuse rather than choose by position, discovery order, normalization, case-insensitive similarity, or another heuristic. An analyst can disambiguate duplicate exact header text with the 1-based COLUMN n selector. F-20 selector identity: HEADER always matches the authoritative exact decoded source header. It never matches an operational fallback name such as Column AA , a generated collision-disambiguation suffix, a COL alias, or a truncated form of the source header.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-003,COLUMN selects by 1-based source ordinal,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"COLUMN n identifies the source column by 1-based ordinal position. COLUMN 1 is the first source column. Zero, negative values, non-integers, and ordinals greater than the source width must refuse. Ordinal selection does not suppress source metadata: Data Sculptor must still resolve and record the selected column's actual decoded source header in the successor MAP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-004,HEADER and COLUMN selectors may be mixed but may not select one source column twice,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"One KEEP block may contain any supported mixture of HEADER and COLUMN selectors. Selector order expresses the analyst's requested selection order for the governed operation. After resolution, two or more selectors that identify the same physical source column constitute a duplicate selection and must refuse before materialization. Data Sculptor must not materialize the same source column twice merely because it was named once by header and once by ordinal.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-005,AS assigns the resulting materialized-column alias,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The optional clause AS ""alias"" belongs to the immediately preceding HEADER or COLUMN selector and expresses an intentional human-facing alias assignment in the governed Work Order. For a logical source column not present in the inherited MAP, omission of AS uses the exact source header as the default alias. For a logical source column already present in the inherited MAP, omission of AS preserves the inherited alias. An explicit AS overrides either default for the successor MAP.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-006,The complete successor MAP must contain unique aliases,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"After inheritance, selector resolution, default-alias application, rematerialization continuity, and all explicit AS clauses are applied, every alias in the complete successor MAP must identify exactly one logical materialized column. If two different logical columns would have the same alias, including a collision with an inherited mapping, validation must refuse unless the Work Order has explicitly resolved the conflict through supported governed syntax. Data Sculptor must not invent suffixes such as Year_2 , use last-write-wins behavior, or silently shadow an existing alias. F-20 narrow generated-name exception: the prohibition on invented suffixes applies to ordinary source-header defaults and analyst-authored aliases. The only automatic suffixing permitted in WASM-002 is deterministic disambiguation of an oversized-header operational fallback under W002-STOR-019.7. That mechanism is not an alias-repair heuristic and must not be applied to an explicit AS value or to a short exact source-header default.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-007,MATERIALIZE commits the resolved KEEP set to the governed structural pass,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"MATERIALIZE is the explicit commitment verb for this WASM-002 DS-STEPS form. The KEEP selectors express which source columns belong in the operation; they do not themselves authorize data-row materialization. Before the bounded structural pass begins, the source, all selectors, actual source ordinals/headers, requested aliases, inherited alias state, and resulting alias uniqueness must be resolved and validated. Successful multi-column execution then follows the one-pass materialization contract.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-008,The Store MAP records resolved truth rather than selector spelling,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"The successor Store MAP must record the fully resolved materialization result using the frozen eight-column schema store_alias,rid_filename,rid_alias,source_filename,source_column_number,source_header,alias,column_filename , regardless of whether the analyst selected a column with HEADER or COLUMN . For example, COLUMN 7 AS ""Crime Rate"" records the Store alias, RID filename/alias, common source filename, source ordinal 7 , the actual decoded header found at column 7, alias Crime Rate , and the newly generated physical COL filename. DS-STEPS expresses intent; the Store MAP persists the resolved durable mapping truth.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-STEPS-009,DS-STEPS materialization syntax acceptance,W002-STEPS,W002-STEPS,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance must cover: one column selected by exact header; one column selected by 1-based ordinal; mixed header/ordinal selectors in one KEEP block; multiple columns materialized in one governed structural pass; AS alias assignment; default header aliasing; inherited-alias preservation on rematerialization; explicit alias replacement on rematerialization; duplicate-header ambiguity refusal; invalid ordinal refusal; duplicate resolved-column refusal; and duplicate successor-alias refusal. Acceptance must also prove that the generated successor MAP records the same resolved source filename, source ordinal, actual source header, resulting alias, and physical COL identity whether a column was selected by header or by ordinal. For a new Store, both the single-column and multi-column materialization fixtures must contain no RID/row-index instruction yet must automatically publish exactly one RID artifact. For a later permitted same-Store materialization, the fixture must likewise contain no RID instruction and must reuse the original RID without publishing another. Damaged-lineage Help acceptance: fixtures must prove that exact source routing to an INVALID Store, and to a DEGRADED Store whose every mapped COL is broken, refuses ordinary materialization without silently treating the source as unseen. The canonical diagnostic/Help evidence must identify the blocked lineage/current MAP and preserve the frozen analyst-owned exits: external restoration under the original governed physical filename followed by governed validation; source rename to begin a distinct new Store lineage; or moving all lineage MAPs out of the active Suitcase to retire that lineage from routing. The all-COLs-broken fixture must warn that moving only the latest MAP is insufficient. No fixture may imply a new Data Sculptor recovery command, automatic RID regeneration, silent replacement of the damaged lineage, or historical byte identity based only on a restored filename. P3-06 validation-tier acceptance: acceptance must prove that a routine routing/status or alias-only path can use Tier 1 without an end-to-end scan of every RID/COL value, while an operation that consumes artifact contents performs Tier 2 before relying on them. Fixtures must include: a RID that passes Tier 1 but fails Tier 2 because its declared N /sequence is internally wrong beyond the Tier-1 boundary; a COL that passes Tier 1 but fails Tier 2 because its data-record count or CSV body is invalid beyond the Tier-1 boundary; and a REPAIR MAP fixture proving that the Tier-2 failure set determines exactly which COL bindings are removed. P3-07 routing acceptance: fixtures must prove that routing discovers a lineage from a structurally valid Store MAP regardless of whether later Store-health evaluation is VALID , DEGRADED , or INVALID . A separate fixture must present no routable lineage together with at least one structurally malformed Store-MAP-class artifact in the active Suitcase and prove that ordinary materialization refuses before publishing a new RID or first Store MAP, while Help identifies the malformed MAP artifact or artifacts. No fixture may treat an all-MAPs-damaged condition as permission for a silent replacement lineage. F-08 cross-operation grammar acceptance: fixtures must prove the common preamble, ASCII-case-insensitive keywords, exact quoted-value preservation, required SPACE/TAB token separation, unknown-line refusal, one-operation-per-WKO refusal, and separation between DS-STEPS terminal phrases and Receipt OPERATION tokens. At least one fixture for each of the seven executable operations must prove that its canonical structure validates while an otherwise similar WKO containing another operation's terminal clause refuses. Separate fixtures must prove that browser Run does not require a textual RUN clause and that parsed RUN composition syntax refuses as deferred before analytical execution. P2-04 restoration-language acceptance: Help, diagnostics, UI text, and acceptance evidence may say that a file restored under the exact governed physical filename passed the required validation tier and may therefore re-enter use. They must not state or imply that filename equality alone proves restoration of the historical original bytes. If stronger historical-byte identity is desired, Help may point to the separately governed explicit fingerprint/LCK direction rather than silently hashing ordinary Store artifacts. F-20 selector/name/width acceptance: fixtures must additionally prove that HEADER resolves only against exact decoded source-header text and never against an operational fallback/default alias; a KEEP selecting all 16,384 columns is valid; a source wider than 16,384 refuses before data-row materialization; and RESET of an oversized-header COL restores the deterministic operational fallback rather than the exact oversized header as alias text. F-03 Store-health and REPAIR MAP acceptance set Target required: REPAIR MAP without exactly one current Store MAP target refuses. Historical target: a structurally valid but non-current historical Store MAP refuses for repair. Wrong profile: a WKO MAP supplied as the repair target refuses. DEGRADED repair: one or more broken COL bindings are removed while every valid binding and the exact RID identity are preserved. All COLs broken: repair refuses, publishes no successor MAP, and the Store remains DEGRADED . Malformed newest MAP: current-state resolution falls back to the greatest earlier structurally valid MAP in the same lineage and reports the malformed artifact. Missing COL in current valid MAP: no fallback occurs; the current MAP remains current and the Store evaluates DEGRADED . Missing RID in current valid MAP: no fallback occurs; the current MAP remains current and the Store evaluates INVALID . Original RID externally restored: the Store is re-evaluated after governed validation without Data Sculptor creating or inferring a replacement RID. No silent fork: neither DEGRADED nor INVALID permits ordinary materialization to create a replacement Store for the same routed lineage.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-003,Suitcase-relative Work Order portability acceptance,W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"An acceptance fixture must execute a saved WKO containing SUITCASE: . and ordinary Suitcase-relative file references, then move the intact fixture Suitcase to a different permitted parent path and execute the same saved WKO again. Resolution must identify the same logical Suitcase files without editing the WKO to insert the new absolute machine path.",NOT_STARTED,NOT_TESTED,NOT_REVIEWED,NOT_ACCEPTED,,,,,,,Revision BM Day 060 H-31 (frozen WASM-002 scope)
W002-WKO-ACC-004,WIP/WKO lifecycle acceptance,W002-WKO-ACC,W002-WKO,WASM-002,UNDER REVIEW,—,"Acceptance evidence must show that an editable WIP cannot Run; saving a valid WIP produces a distinct immutable WKO Run target; loading that WKO and changing instruction text creates a new non-runnable WIP; and the original WKO bytes, filename, identity, and provenance remain unchanged. F-02 alias-registry lifecycle acceptance: a first save for an unused alias must publish a successor WKO MAP containing exactly one CURRENT row for that alias. Saving a second valid WKO with the same exact alias must surface exactly Replace alias target and Cancel . The Cancel fixture must leave the predecessor WKO MAP authoritative and must not commit the pending WKO/WKO-MAP pair as a registry update. The Replace fixture must publish a successor WKO MAP in which the former owner is DEPRECATED , the new WKO is the sole CURRENT row for that alias, and any earlier deprecated history remains preserved. The former WKO bytes and filename and every predecessor WKO MAP must remain unchanged. Alias resolution against the successor registry must resolve to the new CURRENT row and never to a DEPRECATED row. A malformed fixture containing more than one CURRENT row for one exact alias must fail structural validation rather than choose by filename UTC, modified time, discovery order, or row order. P2-03 WKO-registry clock acceptance: using a deterministic injected clock seam, acceptance must prove that a successor WKO MAP publishes only when the observed transaction UTC is strictly greater than the current structurally valid WKO MAP UTC; equal-millisecond and backward/future-dated-predecessor cases refuse without committing the new WKO/registry state. The diagnostic must expose predecessor_map_filename , predecessor_utc , and observed_host_utc . A separate fixture must deliberately move the future-dated current WKO MAP out of the active Suitcase, rescan, and prove deterministic reselection of the remaining current structurally valid WKO MAP without Data Sculptor silently moving or deleting anything itself. Day 060 H-12: every equal/backward/future-predecessor chronology refusal in this acceptance set must emit DS-UTC-001 with exact map_profile: WKO , observed_host_utc , predecessor_map_filename , and predecessor_utc facts. F-23 save-transaction filesystem-fault fixture, reconciled by F-33: using a controlled create/write/close/rename/promotion failure at a deterministic point after a valid WIP has entered the governed save path, acceptance must prove that a failed WKO/WKO-MAP save is never represented as a committed alias-registry update. The pre-run current WKO MAP must remain authoritative; no malformed or unpromoted candidate may become current; and any rollback or retained SCR evidence must follow W002-STOR-018.3 and the shared non-Store publication/retained-evidence contract. No RCV artifact is emitted. F-02 registry-repair acceptance set Deadlock escape: with a repair-required current WKO MAP, a newly saved structurally valid repair-only WKO can Run by exact filename and successfully publish a repaired successor registry. No broad bypass: a newly saved unregistered WKO for any other operation remains ineligible to Run. Missing reference: repair removes a stale registry row but does not recreate the missing WKO, substitute a historical WKO, or promote an older WKO automatically. Discovered alias, no owner: one discovered valid WKO with an otherwise unowned alias becomes CURRENT . Discovered alias collision: a discovered WKO whose alias is already owned by a surviving CURRENT row becomes DEPRECATED . Several discovered WKOs, no owner: all become DEPRECATED ; no winner is inferred by UTC, filename, UUID, directory order, discovery order, or modified time. Mandatory alias: an unaliased WKO cannot be structurally valid. Line endings: otherwise-identical structurally valid WKO fixtures with LF and CRLF line endings are accepted; the lone-CR form refuses. Deterministic successor: repaired successor rows serialize in ascending UTF-8 byte order of exact wko_filename . Historical Run: a registered DEPRECATED WKO can Run by exact physical filename but not by alias. Receipt identity: a successful or refused registry-repair Receipt uses REPAIR_WORK_ORDER_REGISTRY as the operation token. Day 060 H-10 / BM-07 registry-repair Receipt-count acceptance Acceptance must include a successful repair-required-registry fixture in which the exact repair-only bootstrap WKO is initially visible and unregistered, runs by the bounded exact-filename bootstrap, and is then registered by the repair result. The committed successor WKO MAP must contain the repair WKO row. The successful Receipt must list that exact repair WKO under either REGISTERED_CURRENT_WKO_<INDEX>_FILENAME or REGISTERED_DEPRECATED_WKO_<INDEX>_FILENAME , according to the ordinary alias-ownership rule. The corresponding REGISTERED_*_COUNT must equal the number of newly registered rows in that status class, including the repair WKO when applicable. Pre-existing surviving CURRENT / DEPRECATED rows in the base registry must not inflate either registered count.
